### CHAPTER XVII.

<margin>Where one must sacrifice.</margin>
The Lord also spoke to Moses in this way: Explain these things to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites in these words. This is what the Lord commands. Anyone of the family of Israel who slaughters an ox, sheep, or goat in the camp or outside the camp, and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant to offer a gift to the Lord before the Lord’s Tabernacle, <margin>20</margin> shall be considered as if he committed murder, and shall be removed from among his people. Therefore, let the Israelites bring their sacrifices, which they were going to sacrifice in the open air, to the Lord at the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant to the priest, and sacrifice them to the Lord for their well-being. The priest shall pour the blood on the altar of the Lord at the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and burn the fat as a sweet-smelling offering to the Lord. They shall no longer perform sacrifices to the Satyrs <note>original: 'Satyris'; likely referring to goat-demons or desert spirits associated with idolatry</note>, with whom they have acted like harlots. Let this be a perpetual law handed down to their descendants. <margin>30</margin> I say, whoever of the stock of Israel or the foreigners living among them offers a burnt offering or sacrifice and does not bring the victim to the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant to offer it to the Lord, that person shall be cut off from among his people. <margin>Abstinence from blood.</margin> Anyone, whether of the Israelite stock or a foreigner living among them, who eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats blood and remove him from his people. For the life <note>original: 'anima'</note> of a living creature <margin>40</margin> is in the blood, which I give to you upon the altar to pray for your lives; for the blood itself makes atonement for the soul. For this reason, I forbid the Israelites, and any foreigners living among them, from eating blood. If any Israelite or foreigner living among them catches any wild beast or bird that may be eaten, he shall pour its blood on the ground and cover it with earth. For the life of all living things <margin>Gen. 9. a. The blood of a brute animal is poured out for a human soul, as mentioned before in 20. c.</margin> is the blood, which <gloss>stands for the life</gloss>: for this reason, I forbid the Israelites from eating the blood of any animal; because the life of every animal is its blood; whoever eats it must be put to death. Anyone who tastes what died of itself or was torn by beasts, whether a native or a foreigner, shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening; then he shall be purified. But if he does not wash his clothes or cleanse his body, he shall bear his punishment.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

<margin>1 Pet.</margin>
<margin>Rom. 10. Exod. 20. Gal. 3.</margin>
<margin>Forbidden incest.</margin>
Then he said, explain these things to the Israelites in my name: I am the Lord your God. Do not imitate the deeds of Egypt where you lived, nor those of Canaan where I am leading you, nor follow their laws. But follow my laws (I am the Lord your God) and keep my decrees, and live by them; for whoever performs them shall live through them. I am the Lord.
None of you shall approach his close relative to uncover their nakedness <note>original: 'naturam detegat' - a polite euphemism for sexual relations</note>. I am the Lord.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your father or mother: she is your mother, do not uncover her nakedness.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your stepmother; for it is your father's nakedness.
<margin>Protection</margin>
Do not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether born of your father or mother, at home or elsewhere.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your granddaughter, whether from your son or daughter; for she is your own nakedness.
<margin>Precepts of charity</margin>
Do not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your stepmother, born to your father: she is your sister.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for she is of your father’s blood.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is of your mother’s blood.
<margin>Exod. Eccl.</margin>
Do not uncover the nakedness of your paternal uncle—that is, do not approach his wife: she is your aunt.
Do not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law: she is your son’s wife, do not uncover her nakedness.

### CHAPTER XVII.

<margin>Where to sacrifice.</margin>
**I**ikewise, Jehovah spoke with Moses in this manner: Speak these things to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the Israelites in these words. This is what Jehovah has commanded. Whoever of the family of Israel slaughters an ox, a sheep, or a goat in the camp, or outside the camp, and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant to offer a gift to Jehovah before the Tabernacle of Jehovah, that man shall be held as if he had committed a murder, and shall be removed from the number of his people. Therefore, the Israelites shall bring their victims, which they were going to sacrifice in the open air, to Jehovah, to the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant to the priest, and sacrifice them for their well-being. The priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of Jehovah at the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and burn the fat as a sweet-smelling savor to Jehovah. Hereafter, they shall not perform sacred rites to Satyrs <note>original: "Satyris", referring to goat-demons or idols</note>, with whom they commit a kind of spiritual fornication. And let this everlasting ordinance be handed down by them to posterity. Whoever, I say, whether of the stock of Israel or of the strangers living among them, offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice, and does not bring the victim to the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Covenant to offer it to Jehovah, that man shall be cut off from the number of his people.

<margin>Abstaining from blood.</margin>
If anyone, either of the stock of the Israelites or a stranger living among them, eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats blood, and will remove him from the number of his people. For the soul <note>original: "anima", which can mean life or soul</note> of a living thing is in the blood, which I give to you upon the altar to make supplication for your souls: for by the blood itself, supplication is made for the soul. For this reason, I forbid the Israelites, so that no one at all, either among you or among the strangers living among you, shall eat blood. If any of the Israelites, or the strangers living among them, catches any wild animal or bird that is permitted for eating, he shall pour its blood on the ground and cover it with earth.

<margin>Genesis 9. The blood of a brute animal is poured out for the soul of a man, as mentioned shortly before.</margin>
For the soul of all living things is the blood, which ² stands for the soul: for this reason, I forbid the Israelites to eat the blood of any animal; because the soul of each animal is its blood: whoever eats it must be punished with death <note>original: "capite plectendus", literally "beaten with the head," a legal term for capital punishment</note>. Likewise, whoever eats anything that died of itself or was torn by wild beasts, whether he is a native or a stranger, shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening; and so he shall be purified. But if he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he shall pay the penalty.

### CHAPTER XXI.

<margin>The law of mourning for the Priest.</margin>
Admonish the priests, the sons of Aaron, that they should not be defiled by the funerals of their people, except for their closest kin: such as parents, children, brothers, or a virgin sister who is close to him and has no husband; for her funeral he may be defiled. They shall not be defiled even for a leader among their people, lest they be profaned. They shall not shave their heads. They shall not trim their beards. They shall not cut their bodies with marks. They shall be sacred to their God, and shall not profane His name. For since they perform the divine service for Jehovah and prepare the <term>feast offering <note>original: "dapem", referring to the sacred meal or bread of God</note></term> for their God, they must be sacred. They shall not take a harlot or a profaned woman as a wife, nor one divorced from her husband: for they are consecrated to their God. Therefore you must hold them as sacred, since they prepare the feast offering for your God. They shall be sacred to you, for I, Jehovah, who makes you sacred, am holy. If the daughter of a priest has ventured to play the harlot,

<column-break/>

she has profaned her father; she shall be burned with fire.

The High Priest, whose head has been sprinkled with the anointing oil and whose hands have been ordained to put on the sacred garments, shall not uncover his head, nor tear his garments, nor be present at any funeral—not even for his parents shall he be defiled—nor shall he leave the sanctuary, lest he profane the sanctuary of his God, since he has been crowned with the anointing oil of his God. I am Jehovah. He shall take a wife who is a virgin. He shall not take a widow, or a divorced woman, or one polluted by unchastity; but he shall take only a virgin from among his own people, lest he profane his offspring among his people. For I am Jehovah, who has consecrated him.

<margin>The blemished are not to perform sacred duties.</margin>
Then He said: speak these things to Aaron. If there is anyone from your lineage in the future who has a blemish <note>original: "uitium", meaning a physical defect or flaw</note>, he shall not approach to offer the feast offering to his God. For no one with a blemish may offer: such as one who is blind, or lame, or mutilated, or has an abnormal limb, or a broken foot or hand, or is a hunchback, or has a film over his eye <note>original: "lusciosus"</note>, or has a white spot, or is scabby, or has a skin disease, or has crushed testicles. In short, whoever of the seed of Aaron the priest has a blemish shall not administer the divine service of Jehovah; he is blemished, he shall not approach to offer the feast offering to his God. He may indeed eat of the feast offerings of his God, both from the most holy and from the holy things: but he shall not go near the veil, nor approach the altar, because he is blemished, lest he profane my sanctuary; for I am Jehovah, who makes them sacred. So Moses spoke with Aaron, and his sons, and all the Israelites.

### CHAPTER XXII.

<margin>Who may not eat of the sacred things.</margin>
Likewise Jehovah spoke with Moses in this manner: Speak to Aaron and his sons, that they restrain themselves from the sacred things which the Israelites consecrate to me, lest they profane my holy name, for I am Jehovah. Therefore say to them these words: In the future, whoever of your offspring approaches the sacred things while polluted—those things consecrated by the Israelites to Jehovah—that person shall be removed from my sight. I am Jehovah. Whoever of the seed of Aaron is a leper or suffers from a discharge <note>original: "genituræ substillo", referring to a seminal or bodily discharge</note> shall not eat of the sacred things until he is purified; or whoever touches anything made unclean by a corpse, or a man from whom a discharge has flowed, or who has been polluted by touching any beast or man who is unclean for any reason—that person shall be unclean until evening and shall not taste the sacred things until he has washed his body with water.

I am Jehovah: therefore let them obey my precepts, lest they bear sin for it and die because of profanation. I am Jehovah, who makes them sacred.

But if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow, or is divorced and has no children, and returns to her father’s house as she was in her youth, she may use her father’s food; but no outsider shall use it. <unclear>If someone</unclear> eats a sacred offering unintentionally, he shall add a fifth to its value and restore it to the priest. This shall be done so that the offerings dedicated to Jehovah <note>original: "Iouæ," a Latinization of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton used by humanist translators</note> by the Israelites are not profaned by them; if they were to eat these dedicated things, they would be liable for punishment. For I am Jehovah, who consecrates them.

Then Jehovah spoke to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the Israelites, saying: If any Israelite, or a foreigner living among the Israelites, makes an offering—whether it is a vow or a voluntary gift—to be offered as a burnt sacrifice, it must be a male without blemish from the cattle, sheep, or goats, so that you may find favor. Do not offer anything with a defect, otherwise it will not be accepted for you. If anyone offers a sacrifice for well-being to Jehovah, whether to fulfill a special vow or as a free-will offering, whether of cattle or sheep, it must be perfect to be an atonement, without any defect. Do not offer to Jehovah animals that are blind, or broken, or mutilated, or have warts, or scabs, or rashes; do not place any of these on the altar as a sacrifice to Jehovah. You may present a bull or a sheep with a limb too long or too short as a voluntary offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow. <margin>b</margin> Do not offer to Jehovah an animal whose testicles are crushed, or bruised, or torn, or cut; do not perform such acts in your land, nor shall you accept any of these from a foreigner to offer as food to your God. Because they are corrupted and defective, they will not be accepted on your behalf.

Furthermore, Jehovah said: When a calf, or a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall remain with its mother for seven days; from the eighth day onward, it will be accepted as an offering to Jehovah. But you shall not slaughter a cow or a sheep and its young on the same day. If you sacrifice a thank-offering to Jehovah (which you shall do to find favor), it must be eaten on that very day; do not leave any of it until the next morning. I am Jehovah. Therefore, keep my commandments and perform them (I am Jehovah), so that you do not profane my holy name; I shall be held holy among the Israelites. I am Jehovah, the author of your holiness, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God: I am Jehovah.

### CHAPTER XXIII.

Then Jehovah said to the Israelites: These are the festivals of Jehovah in which you shall hold a sacred assembly. Work shall be done for six days, but on the seventh day, which shall be the Sabbath of rest, a sacred assembly shall be held; you shall do no work. It is the Sabbath to Jehovah, wherever you live. These are the festivals of Jehovah for sacred assemblies, which you shall observe at their appointed times. On the fourteenth day of the first month at twilight is Jehovah's Passover. On the fifteenth day of the same month is the festival of unleavened bread <note>original: "azymalia"</note> to Jehovah; for seven days you shall live on unleavened bread. On the first of these days, hold a sacred assembly and do no ordinary work. For seven days you shall present a sacrifice to Jehovah; on the seventh day, which shall be a sacred assembly, you shall do no ordinary work. And Jehovah spoke these things to Moses: Tell the Israelites: When you have entered the land I am giving you and have harvested its crop, bring a sheaf of the firstfruits <term>firstfruits: the very first portion of a harvest, dedicated to God before the rest is used</term> of your harvest to the priest, who shall wave it before Jehovah to find favor for you; he shall do this on the day after the Sabbath.

<meta>This page continues the final warnings of the Holiness Code, specifically the "curses" for disobedience, and concludes with the regulations regarding vows, valuations, and tithes. ->LEVITICUS<-

I will also come against you in my anger, and I will inflict a sevenfold punishment upon you for your crimes, to such an extent that you will eat the flesh of your own children. I will devastate your chapels <note>original: "sacella," referring to high places or shrines</note> and I will tear down your idols. I will pile your corpses upon the corpses of your filthy dung-gods <note>original: "stercoreorum deorum," a derogatory term for idols common in Latin biblical translations</note>, and I will reject you. I will destroy your towns and lay waste to your sanctuaries, nor will I take delight in the scent of your sacrifices. I will devastate the land to such a degree that your enemies who inhabit it will be struck with wonder. I will scatter you among foreign nations and draw the sword against you; your land shall be a desert and your towns a waste. Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths for as long as it lies uncultivated and you are in the territories of your enemies; then the land shall rest and enjoy its Sabbaths. It shall rest, I say, for the entire time of its desolation, because it did not rest during your Sabbaths when you lived there. As for those of you who remain, I will strike such faint-heartedness into them in the land of their enemies that they will be put to flight by the sound of a fluttering leaf. They shall flee as if fleeing from an enemy's blade, and they shall fall even when no one pursues them. They shall stumble over one another as if fleeing a sword, though no one is chasing them. You will not be able to stand against your enemies; you will perish among the other nations, and the soil of your enemies will consume you. Those of you who remain will waste away in the enemy's land, not only for their own crimes but also for the crimes of their ancestors. Thus it will happen that they shall confess both their own guilt and the guilt of their ancestors, by whose wickedness—while they resisted me—it came to pass that I, in turn opposing them, deported them into the land of the enemy.

<margin>God is merciful to those who return to their senses.</margin>
Then at last, when their impure souls are subdued and they seek pardon for their guilt, I will remember the covenant that exists between me and Jacob, and between me and Isaac, and between me and Abraham. I will also remember the land; for the land itself, abandoned by them and left uncultivated, will have completed its Sabbaths. They themselves will seek pardon for their guilt because they rejected my laws and cast aside my statutes. Yet, while they are living in the land of their enemies, they will not be so rejected or cast aside that—the covenant between us being broken—they are utterly consumed, for I am still their God. I will remember the covenant made with their ancestors, whom I led out of Egypt in the sight of the nations so that I might be their God; I am Jehovah. These are the statutes, judgments, and laws which Jehovah established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai, through Moses.

<margin>The price and manner of vows and consecrated things.</margin>
### CHAPTER XXVII.

Furthermore, Jehovah spoke with Moses in this manner: Explain these things to the Israelites. If anyone makes a special vow to Jehovah, if persons are vowed, they shall be redeemed at the value at which they are estimated. For a male from twenty to sixty years of age, let the price be fifty sacred shekels of silver, and for a female, thirty. If the age is from five years to twenty, the price for a male shall be twenty shekels, and for a female, ten. From the age of one month to five years, the price for a male shall be five shekels of silver, and for a female, three. Above the sixtieth year, the price for a male shall be fifteen shekels, and for a female, ten. But if the person

<column-break/>

who makes the vow is poorer than the estimated price, he shall be brought before the priest, who shall value him according to what he can afford.

<margin>If the thing promised by the vow is a beast.</margin>
If it is an animal from the kind that is offered as a gift to Jehovah, whatever of this sort is given to Jehovah shall be holy. One shall not substitute another for it, neither a bad one for a good one, nor a good one for a bad one. If one beast is exchanged for another, then both the original and its substitute shall be consecrated. If, however, it is any unclean animal from which a divine sacrifice to Jehovah is not permitted, that animal shall be brought to the priest, who shall estimate it in good faith, and his estimation shall stand. But if the owner wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth part to the valuation. If someone consecrates his house to Jehovah, the priest shall estimate it in good faith, and his estimation shall stand. If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he must add a fifth of the silver valuation, and so he shall have the house. If someone consecrates to Jehovah a portion of the field of his possession, the valuation shall be according to the amount of seed required for it: a kor <note>original: "cori," a unit of dry measure</note> of barley seed shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver. If he consecrates his field immediately from the year of Jubilee, it shall stand at that valuation. But if he consecrates it some time after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years remaining until the next Jubilee year, so that a deduction is made from the valuation. And if the person who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall have it by adding a fifth part to that valuation.

<margin>Devoted to God, as are those things commonly called church property. EXODUS 30</margin>
If he does not redeem it, but has sold it to another, it may no longer be redeemed. When the field becomes free in the Jubilee, it shall be holy to Jehovah, and it shall pass into the possession of the priest as a devoted field. If, however, he consecrates to Jehovah a field he has bought, which is not part of his paternal inheritance, the priest shall calculate the sum of the valuation for him up to the year of Jubilee; and the man shall pay that estimated value on that day as a holy thing to Jehovah. In the year of Jubilee, the field shall return to the seller, to whom the possession of the land belongs.

<margin>Numbers 3, Ezekiel 45</margin>
Every such valuation shall be in sacred shekels, a shekel being worth twenty gerahs <note>original: "obolos," the Greek term for small coins, here used to translate the Hebrew gerah</note>. Furthermore, no one shall consecrate the firstborn among the livestock which already belongs to Jehovah, whether it is a calf, a lamb, or a kid; they are Jehovah's. If they are from unclean livestock, they shall be redeemed according to the valuation, with a fifth part added. If they are not redeemed, they shall be sold according to the estimated value. However, nothing "devoted"—which a man has devoted to Jehovah out of all his possessions, whether human, animal, or inherited field—shall be sold or redeemed; everything devoted is most holy to Jehovah. No person who has been devoted <note>original: "devotum," referring to the 'herem' or things set apart for destruction or total divine use</note> as holy shall be redeemed; he must be put to death. All tithes of the land, whether of grain or of fruit, belong to Jehovah; they are holy to Jehovah. If anyone redeems any of his tithes, he must add a fifth part to them.

<margin>It is in the care of the shepherds.</margin>
And all the tithes of the herd or the flock—whatever passes under the rod—shall be a holy tithe to Jehovah. No one shall inquire whether it is good or bad, nor shall any substitution be made. If a substitution is made, both the original and the substitute shall be holy; they cannot be redeemed.

So the Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

## CHAPTER II.

The Lord also spoke to Moses and Aaron in this manner: The Israelites shall camp each under his own standard, beneath the banners of their ancestral families, facing the Tabernacle of the Oracle on every side. On the east side, the standard of the camp of Judah shall be set up, divided into their units, with Nahshon son of Amminadab as their leader. The number of his recorded soldiers is 74,600. The Ephraimites shall camp on the west, with Elishama son of Ammihud as leader; 40,500 soldiers. Next to them, the tribe of Manasseh, with Gamaliel son of Pedahzur as leader; 32,200 soldiers. Then the tribe of Naphtali, with Ahira son of Enan as leader; 53,400 soldiers. The total of all Dan's forces is 157,600. These standards shall set out last. The total sum of the entire Israelite army, recorded by families, is 603,550—not counting the Levites among the Israelites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. Thus the Israelites did exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses; they camped by their standards and they moved out in the same way, organized by their clans and families.

The responsibility of the Gershonites in the Tabernacle of the Oracle included the Tabernacle itself, the tent and its covering, the screen for the entrance to the Tabernacle of the Oracle, the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance to the courtyard that surrounds the Tabernacle and the altar, and all the ropes used in its service. 

The Kohathite clans were these: the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites. The number of all their males a month old or more was eight thousand six hundred, and they were responsible for the care of the sanctuary. These Kohathites camped on the south side of the Tabernacle, led by Elizaphan son of Uzziel. Their charge included the Ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sacred utensils used in the ministry, and the screen, along with all the equipment related to them. The chief over the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest; he oversaw those responsible for the care of the sanctuary. 

The Merarite clans were the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbering six thousand two hundred males a month old or more, led by Zuriel son of Abihail. They camped on the north side of the Tabernacle, and were responsible for the frames of the Tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment and tools, as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard,

### CHAPTER V.

Then the Lord commanded Moses to instruct the Israelites to expel from the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone who has a bodily discharge, and everyone defiled by a dead body, whether male or female. <margin>The law of recompense. Leviticus 6</margin>
Then the Lord said to Moses: Explain this to the Israelites. If a man or woman commits any sin common to humanity, and by acting unfaithfully against the Lord incurs guilt, they must confess their sin and return the full amount of the recompense <note>original: "mulctæ," referring to a fine or restitution for a wrong</note>, adding a fifth part to it, and give it to the one they have wronged. But if the person has no close relative to whom the recompense can be paid, the recompense shall be paid to the priest for the Lord, in addition to the ram of atonement with which prayer is made for them. And every contribution from the sacred gifts of the Israelites that they bring to the priest shall belong to him; each person's sacred gifts are their own, but whatever anyone gives to the priest belongs to the priest.

->CHAPTER VI.<-

<margin>The law of the Nazirites.</margin>
Then the LORD spoke to Moses in this manner: Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If anyone, whether man or woman, makes a special Nazirite vow <note>The term "Nazirite" comes from the Hebrew word for "consecrated" or "separated"</note> to devote themselves to the LORD, they must abstain from wine and strong drink: they shall not drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink, nor shall they drink any juice of the grapes, nor eat grapes, whether fresh or dried. As long as they are thus consecrated, they shall eat nothing produced by the grapevine, not even the seeds <margin>Judges 13</margin> or the skins. Throughout the period of their vow of consecration, no razor shall touch their head; until the time for which they were consecrated to the LORD is completed, they shall be holy, letting the hair of their head grow long. As long as they are consecrated to the LORD, they shall not go near a dead body: not even for the death of their father, mother, brother, or sister shall they make themselves ritually unclean, because the consecration of their God is upon their head. Throughout the entire time of their consecration, they are holy to the LORD. But if someone dies very suddenly and unexpectedly in their presence, thus defiling their consecrated head, they shall shave their head on the day of their purification—that is, on the seventh day. On the eighth day, they shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Oracle. The priest shall offer one as a sin offering <note>original: "piaculum"</note> and the other as a burnt offering <note>original: "solido sacrificio," a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire</note>, to make atonement for the sin committed by being near the corpse, and he shall consecrate the person's head that same day. They shall rededicate the period of their consecration to the LORD and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering; the previous days shall not count, because their consecration was defiled. Now this is the law for the Nazirite when the period of their consecration is complete. They shall be brought to the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Oracle and present their offerings to the LORD: one year-old male lamb without blemish for a burnt offering, one year-old ewe lamb without blemish for a sin offering, and one ram without blemish for a peace offering <note>original: "pro salute," literally "for well-being or safety"</note>. Also a basket of unleavened bread made of fine flour, cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, along with their grain offerings and drink offerings. The priest shall present them before the LORD and perform the sin offering and the burnt offering. The ram...

### CHAPTER IX.

<margin>The Israelites observe the Passover.</margin>
The LORD also commanded Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after their departure from Egypt, that the Israelites should keep the Passover at its appointed time—that is, on the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight—and according to all its statutes and rituals. So Moses spoke to the Israelites about keeping the Passover. And the Israelites kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai; they carried out everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. But there were certain men who could not keep the Passover on that day because they were defiled by a dead body <note>original: "ex funere polluti," ritually unclean due to contact with a corpse</note>. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day and explained that, being defiled by a corpse, they were being prevented from presenting their offering to the LORD at the appointed time among the Israelites. Moses told them to wait while he consulted the LORD concerning them. And the LORD replied to him: Tell the Israelites: If any of you or your descendants are defiled by a corpse or are away on a long journey, they shall still keep the Passover to the LORD. They shall keep it on the fourteenth day of the second month at twilight, and shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs <note>original: "cichoreo," literally chicory</note>. <margin>Exodus 13. John 19.</margin> They shall leave none of it until the next day, nor shall they break any of its bones; they shall observe it exactly according to the statute of the Passover. But if anyone who is clean and is not on a journey neglects to keep the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people; because he did not bring the offering to the LORD at its appointed time, he shall bear the penalty. If a foreigner living among you keeps the Passover to the LORD, he must do so according to the statute and ritual of the Passover; you shall have the same law for the foreigner and the native-born. <margin>Exodus 40.</margin> Moreover, on the day the Tabernacle was set up,

...the cloud covered the tent of the oracular tabernacle <note>Latin: "edem oracularis tabernaculi," referring to the Tabernacle as the place where God's word or oracles were received</note>. In the evening, however, there appeared over the tent something like the appearance of fire until morning: and so it happened continually, that the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
<margin>1 Corinthians 10</margin>
<margin>The cloud is the leader of the camp.</margin>
And only then did the Israelites set out, when the cloud lifted itself from the tabernacle: and in the place where the cloud settled, there they made camp, and at the command of Jehovah <note>Latin: "Iouæ," a common 16th-century rendering of the divine name</note> they either moved or held the camp. As long as the cloud settled over the tabernacle, they held camp: but if it settled for a long time, they obeyed the mandate of Jehovah and did not set out. But if it ever happened that the cloud remained over the tabernacle for many days, at the nod of Jehovah they either held or moved the camp. And if it happened that the cloud stayed from evening until morning and was lifted in the morning, they set out: and whether it lifted by day or by night, they set out: and whether the cloud remained over the tabernacle for one or two days, or a month, or a whole year, they kept their station and did not set out: but when it lifted, they set out. At the nod of Jehovah they either pitched or moved camp, and they took care to execute what Jehovah had commanded them through Moses.

### CHAPTER X.

<margin>Trumpets.</margin>
Then Jehovah spoke with Moses in this manner: Make two silver trumpets, and let them be solid, which you shall use for calling the assembly and for moving the camp, and at the sound of which the whole multitude shall gather to you at the door of the oracular tabernacle. But if only one trumpet is sounded, the princes, the leaders of the Israelite forces, shall gather to you. When, however, you sound with an alarm <note>Latin: "ouatu," referring to a rhythmic or broken blast, often called a 'teruah' in Hebrew</note>, those who are stationed to the east shall set out. When likewise you sound the second alarm, those who are stationed to the south shall move. G. L. When the third, those to the west: when the fourth, those to the north: H. and they shall sound the alarm as they set out. But in calling the assembly, you shall sound but not give the alarm. Moreover, the sons of Aaron shall blow these trumpets, and this custom shall be passed down to your descendants forever. And when you engage in battle in your borders with an enemy who is hostile to you, you shall sound the alarm with these trumpets: thus it will happen that Jehovah your God, being mindful of you, will defend you from your enemies. Then in your joys, in your solemnities, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your solid sacrifices <note>Latin: "solidis sacrificijs," referring to whole burnt offerings</note> and over the sacrifices for your well-being, so that these may stir up a remembrance of you before Jehovah your God—that is, before me. It happened in the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, that the cloud was lifted from the tabernacle of the oracle. Therefore the Israelites set out, having preserved the order of their ranks, from the desert of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the desert of Paran: and then for the first time they moved camp just as Jehovah had commanded through Moses. First, the standard of the ranks of the Judean forces set out, over whom was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
<margin>The order of the ranks on the journey.</margin>
Moreover, Nathanael the son of Zuar was over the forces of the tribe of Issachar: and Eliab the son of Helon was over those of Zebulun. Then, having taken down the tabernacle, the Gershonites and Merarites set out, carrying the tabernacle. Then the standard

<column-break/>

of the Reubenite ranks set out with their forces, over whom was Elizur the son of Shedeur. Moreover, Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai was over the forces of the tribe of Simeon: and Eliasaph the son of Deuel over those of Gad. Then the Kohathites set out carrying the sanctuary, and in anticipation of their arrival, the others set up the tabernacle. Then the standard of the ranks of the Ephraimites set out with their forces, over whom Elishama the son of Ammihud presided. Moreover, Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur was over the forces of the tribe of Manasseh: and Abidan the son of Gideoni over those of Benjamin. Finally, the standard of the ranks of the Danites set out, closing the entire column of the army, over whose forces Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai presided. Moreover, Pagiel the son of Ocran was over the forces of the tribe of Asher: and Ahira the son of Enan over those of Naphtali. In such order the Israelites proceeded on their journeys, distributed into ranks.

Moses spoke with Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, his father-in-law, in this way: We are setting out for the place which Jehovah promised to give us. Come with us, and we will do you good. For Jehovah has determined to bestow benefits upon the Israelites. And when he said he would not go, but would return to his own native land, Moses spoke to him thus: Do not, I pray, desert us. For you know our camping places in the deserts, and you will serve as eyes for us. And if you accompany us, whatever benefits we happen to receive from Jehovah, we will bestow the same upon you. Therefore they set out from the mountain of Jehovah and made a three-day journey, the ark of the covenant of Jehovah preceding them during those three days to scout out a resting place, while in the meantime the cloud of Jehovah hovered over them as they journeyed by day. And as the ark set out, Moses would say:

### CHAPTER XI.

<margin>The place Taberah.</margin>
But it happened that the people complained wickedly in the ears of Jehovah. When these things were heard, Jehovah being angry, his fire blazed against them, and it was already consuming the outskirts of the camp, when the people cried out to Moses: and when he had prayed, the fire subsided: and the place was called Taberah <note>a name meaning "burning"</note>, because the fire of Jehovah had blazed there. But then the mixed multitude that was among them, as well as the Israelites, led by desire, wept again, saying:
<margin>The food of Egypt is longed for.</margin>
"Who will feed us with meat? We remember the fish which we ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic. Now our souls are wasting away, while nothing else but this Manna is observed by our eyes."
<margin>What the Manna was like.</margin>
Now the Manna was like coriander seed, with the appearance of bdellium <note>a fragrant resin resembling a pearl</note>, which they gathered here and there, and having crushed it in a mill or ground it in a mortar, they cooked it in pots, and from this they made kneaded loaves, with the taste of a cake prepared with oil.
<margin>Exodus 16, Wisdom 16, Psalm 78, John 6</margin>
This Manna was brought down at night with the dew that fell upon the camp. Moreover, Moses heard the people weeping by their families, each before their own tents, which thing caused great anger in Jehovah and grief to Moses. And Moses said to Jehovah: Why do you afflict your servant with this evil, and hold me in such disfavor, that you [lay the burden] of all this [people upon me]?
<margin>Quails. Psalm 78.</margin>

...should you lay the burden of this people upon me? Did I conceive this whole people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me: "Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant," into the land which you swore to their ancestors? Where can I get meat to give to all these people? For they cry before me, demanding that I give them meat to eat. I cannot carry this whole people alone; for it is too heavy for me. If you deal with me this way, kill me—if I have any favor in your sight—so that I do not have to endure this evil. 

Then Jehovah said: "Gather for me seventy men from the elders of the Israelites, whom you know to be the elders of the people and their officers; bring them to the tabernacle of the oracle and have them stand there with you. And I will descend to speak with you there, and I will take of the spirit with which you are endowed and put it upon them; thus they shall support the burden of the people with you, so that you do not bear it alone. Moreover, warn the people that they should purify themselves for tomorrow, so that they may eat meat; for they have wept in the hearing of Jehovah, demanding that meat be given to them for food, and claiming they were better off in Egypt. Therefore, Jehovah will give them meat to eat, and indeed they shall not eat it for one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty: but for a whole month, until it is vomited through their nostrils and creates nausea; because they have rejected Jehovah who dwells among them, and have complained before him, weeping that they had departed from Egypt." 

Then Moses said: "There are six hundred thousand footmen in this people among whom I dwell, and yet you say you will give them enough meat to eat for a whole month? Shall the sheep, and the goats, and the oxen be slaughtered to be enough for them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together to satisfy them?" But Jehovah replied: "Is the hand of Jehovah<gloss>a</gloss> <note>original Latin: "Iouæne," a common 16th-century humanist rendering of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton</note> shortened? Now you shall see whether my promises are fulfilled for you or not." 

Then Moses went out and reported the words of Jehovah to the people, and having gathered seventy men from the elders of the people, he stationed them around the tabernacle. And Jehovah descended in a cloud and spoke with him, and took of the spirit with which Moses himself was endowed and put it upon the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied<gloss>b</gloss> without ceasing. 

But two men remained in the camp, one named Eldad and the other Medad, who, although they were among those registered, had not gone out to the tabernacle; and they also, being inspired by the spirit, began to prophesy in the camp. When a certain youth had run to report this to Moses, showing that Eldad and Medad were prophesying in the camp, Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' assistant from his youth, responded: "My lord Moses, stop them." To whom Moses said: "Are you jealous on my behalf? Would that all the people of Jehovah were prophets, inspired by his spirit!" Then, when Moses with the senate of the Israelites had returned to the camp, a wind sent from Jehovah carried a great force of quails from the sea and scattered them into the camp, so that on all sides around the camp, for nearly a day's journey, they stood two cubits high above the ground. Therefore the people set to work all that day and night, and all the following day,

<column-break/>

<margin>The Graves of Craving.</margin>
gathering so many quails that he who gathered the least gathered ten bushels <note>Latin: "modios," a Roman unit of dry measure</note>, which they spread out all around the camp. The meat was still between their teeth, not yet chewed, when Jehovah, becoming incensed against the people, struck them with a very great slaughter; and that place was named the **Graves of Craving** <note>Latin: "Busta cupiditatis," translating the Hebrew *Kibroth-Hattaavah*</note>, because there the people who had craved were buried. From the Graves of Craving, the people set out for Hazeroth.

### CHAPTER XII.

<margin>The envy of Miriam and Aaron.</margin>
<margin>2. That is, out of the camp, for the tabernacle was outside the camp.</margin>
<margin>Hebrews 3.</margin>
**A**ND meanwhile, while they were at Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian wife he had taken (for he had married an Ethiopian woman). They said: "Has Jehovah spoken only through Moses? Has he not also spoken through us?" Now Moses was the mildest of all men who walked the earth. Upon hearing this, Jehovah suddenly commanded Moses, Aaron, and Miriam that they should all three go out<gloss>2</gloss> to the tabernacle of the oracle. When they had done so, Jehovah descended in a column of cloud, and standing before the tabernacle, he called Aaron and Miriam; and when they both had come forward, he spoke thus: "Come, hear my words. If there is a prophet of Jehovah among you, I shall make myself known to him through visions and speak with him in dreams. But it is not so with my servant Moses, to whom the faithfulness of my whole house is entrusted: for I speak to him face to face, clearly and without riddles, and he beholds the form of Jehovah. Why then did you not fear to speak against my servant Moses?" 

Thus being angry with them, Jehovah departed, and the cloud left the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam was leprous, white as snow; and when Aaron looked back and saw her leprous, he said to Moses: "I beseech you, my lord, do not hold against us this sin committed so thoughtlessly by us, nor let her be like a stillborn child, who comes out of the mother's womb with half the body consumed." Then Moses, calling upon Jehovah, said: "O God, I beseech you, heal her." To him Jehovah said: "If her father had spat in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days? Let her be excluded from the camp for seven days, and afterward she shall be admitted." Thus Miriam was excluded from the camp for seven days, and the people did not move camp until Miriam was admitted. Afterward, having set out from Hazeroth, they made camp in the wilderness of Paran.

### CHAPTER XII.

He called Aaron and Miriam, and when they both stepped forward, he said: "Hear my words. If there is a prophet among you, I, Jehovah, make myself known to him in visions and speak with him in dreams. But it <margin>30</margin> is not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with my entire house. <margin>Heb. 3.</margin> With him I speak face to face, clearly and not in riddles, and he beholds the very form of Jehovah. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?" In his anger, Jehovah left them, and the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle. Suddenly, Miriam was leprous, white as snow. When Aaron turned toward her and saw her leprosy, he said to Moses: "I beg you, my lord, do not hold this sin against us, which we have committed so foolishly. Do not let her be like a stillborn child, who comes out of its mother's womb with half its flesh consumed." Then Moses <margin>40</margin> cried out to Jehovah: "O God, heal her, I pray!" But Jehovah said to him: "If her father had but spit in her face, would she not be in shame for seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp for seven days, and after that she may be brought back." So Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days, and the people did not move camp until she was brought back in. Afterward, they departed from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.

The name Joshua means "Jehovah is salvation."</note> Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan and commanded them to go up through the south and, having crossed the mountains, to observe what kind of land it was: whether the people living there were strong or weak, few or many. After forty days of exploring the land, they returned and went to Moses, Aaron, and the entire community of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They reported everything to them and showed them the fruit of the land, telling their story: "We went into the land where you sent us; it truly flows with milk and honey, and here is its fruit. But the inhabitants are strong, and the cities are very large and fortified; moreover, we saw the descendants of Anak there. The Amalekites live in the south; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the mountains; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan." Then Caleb hushed the people before Moses, urging them to go up at once and take possession of it, for they would surely overcome it. But the men who had gone with him said they were not able to attack that people, as they were stronger than themselves. They spread an unfavorable report among the Israelites about the land they had scouted, saying it was a land that "consumes its inhabitants" and that all the people they saw there were of immense stature. They even said they had seen the Anakite giants there, descendants of giants, compared to whom they felt like mere grasshoppers.

As for the men whom Moses had sent to explore the land, who returned and incited the entire multitude to sedition against him by disparaging that land—those men, I say, who spoke maliciously against the land, died, struck down by a plague before Jehovah. But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh survived from among those who had gone to explore the land. When Moses reported all these things to all the Israelites, they mourned greatly. Rising early the next morning, they went up to the top of the mountain, saying they were ready to invade the place promised by Jehovah and confessing their sin. But Moses showed them that this must not be done without the command of Jehovah, for it would not succeed. He warned them not to set out while Jehovah was absent, lest they be slaughtered by their enemies. For there they would run into the Amalekites and Canaanites and fall by the sword, since Jehovah, whom they had abandoned, would not be with them. Yet they stubbornly persisted in crossing over the mountain, even though the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah and Moses did not move from the camp. Consequently, the inhabitants of that mountain, the Amalekites and the Canaanites, came down and struck them down, pursuing them as far as Hormah.

### CHAPTER XV.

Jehovah also spoke with Moses, telling him to speak to the Israelites in this manner: "When you have entered the land of your habitation which I am giving to you, and you make an offering to Jehovah, whether a burnt offering or a sacrifice to perform a vow, or a voluntary offering, or at your solemn feasts, to soothe Jehovah with a sweet aroma—whether it be from the herd or the flock—the one who offers his gift shall bring to Jehovah a grain offering <note>original: "fertum," a sacrificial cake</note> of a tenth part of fine flour mixed with a fourth of a *hin* <note>original: "binis," likely referring to the hin, a Hebrew unit of liquid measure</note> of oil. You shall also prepare a fourth of a *hin* of wine for a drink offering with the burnt offering or sacrifice for each lamb. Or for a ram, prepare a grain offering of two tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a *hin* of oil; then offer a third of a *hin* of wine for a drink offering to Jehovah as a sweet aroma. When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice to Jehovah, whether for a vow or a peace offering, offer with the bull a grain offering of three tenths of fine flour mixed with half a *hin* of oil, and bring half a *hin* of wine for the drink offering to Jehovah as a sweet aroma. The same shall be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat; however many victims you prepare, do the same for each. Every native-born Israelite shall do these things in this way when offering a sweet aroma to soothe Jehovah."

<column-break/>

"If any foreigner <note>original: "peregrinans," a sojourner or resident alien</note> living among you, or whoever may be among you in future generations, makes a sacrifice to soothe Jehovah with a sweet aroma, he shall do exactly as your community does. There shall be one statute for both you citizens and for the foreigners dwelling among you; this shall be a permanent rite for both you and the foreigner before Jehovah in the future. The same law and the same right shall apply both to you and to the foreigners living among you."

<margin>Offerings set aside for Jehovah.</margin>
Jehovah also commanded Moses to speak these words to the Israelites: "When you enter the land into which I am leading you, and you eat the bread of that land, you shall set aside an offering for Jehovah. Specifically, from the first of your dough you shall set aside a cake, just as you set aside an offering from the threshing floor. From the first of your dough you shall give an offering to Jehovah throughout your generations."

<margin>Atonement for public error.</margin>
"But if through ignorance <note>original: "per imprudentiam," by mistake or unintentionally</note> you fail to execute all these commandments which Jehovah spoke to Moses—namely, everything Jehovah commanded you through Moses from the day he first gave them and onward through your generations—if, I say, anything was committed through the blind error of the multitude, then the entire multitude shall offer one young bull for a burnt offering to soothe Jehovah with a sweet aroma, together with its grain offering and drink offering according to the custom, and one male goat for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for the entire multitude of Israelites and pray for their pardon, because it was an error. They shall bring their gift to be burned for Jehovah and a sin offering for their error before Jehovah, so that the entire multitude of Israelites and the foreigners living among them may be forgiven, since the entire people were in error."

<margin>Atonement for private error.</margin>
"But if a single individual sins through ignorance, he shall bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering. The priest shall pray before Jehovah for that person who sinned by mistake, so that through that prayer he may obtain pardon. You shall have the same law for the native-born Israelites and the foreigners dwelling among them who act through error."

<margin>He who sins defiantly.</margin>
"But he who acts defiantly <note>original: "data opera," with deliberate purpose or "with a high hand"</note>, whether he is a native or a foreigner, has despised Jehovah and shall be cut off from the number of his people, because he has held the word of Jehovah in contempt and violated his commandment. He shall be removed from your midst and shall bear his guilt."

<margin>He who violated the Sabbath by gathering wood.</margin>
"Furthermore, while the Israelites were in the wilderness, a certain man was caught gathering wood on the Sabbath day. Those who caught him brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the entire multitude. He was placed in custody because it was not yet clear what should be done with him. Then Jehovah said to Moses that the man must die, and he must be stoned by the entire multitude outside the camp. So the entire multitude led him outside the camp and overwhelmed him with stones until he died, just as Jehovah had commanded Moses."

Now Korah, the son of Izhar, descended from Kohath the son of Levi, along with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On the son of Peleth, a Reubenite, conspired together and rose up against Moses. ## CHAPTER XVI.

<margin>The rebellion of Korah. Ecclesiasticus 45; Jude 1; 2 Corinthians 10.</margin>
Now Korah, son of Izhar, descended from Kohath, son of Levi, along with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth, a descendant of Reuben, rose up and conspired against Moses. They were joined by two hundred and fifty Israelites, leading men of the community, members of the council, and well-known figures. These men gathered against Moses and Aaron, saying that the entire multitude was made up of holy people and that Jehovah dwelt among them; this, they argued, should be enough. Dathan and Abiram, however, came out and stood at the entrances of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little children. If these men die in any natural human way, or if they suffer any common human punishment, then Jehovah has not sent me. But if God does something new, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and everything they own, and they go down alive into the underworld <note>original: "tartara," a classical Latin term for the abyss or hell, used here to translate the Hebrew 'Sheol'</note>, then you shall know that these men have spoken impiously against Jehovah." As soon as he finished saying these things, the ground beneath them split apart, and the earth opened its mouth and devoured them, their households, all of Korah's men, and all their possessions. They and all that belonged to them went down alive into the grave <note>original: "orcum," another classical term for the underworld</note>; the earth closed over them, and they perished, removed from the commonwealth of the Israelites. <margin>The sons of Korah did not perish, as stated in chapter 26; Psalm 105; Deuteronomy 11.</margin> All the Israelites who were around them fled at their cries, fearing that the earth might swallow them as well. And fire came out from Jehovah and consumed those two hundred and fifty men who were offering the incense. Then Jehovah commanded Moses to tell Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take the censers out of the midst of the burning, for they were holy, and to scatter the coals. He ordered that the censers of those men who had sinned at the cost of their lives be hammered into thin plates to plate the altar (for they were holy, having been presented before Jehovah), so that they might serve as a sign to the Israelites. So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that those who were burned had offered, and he had them hammered out to plate the altar, just as Jehovah had commanded him through Moses. This was to remind the Israelites that no outsider, who was not of the lineage of Aaron, should dare to offer incense before Jehovah, lest he suffer the fate of Korah and his followers. <margin>The rod of Aaron. Hebrews 9.</margin> On the next day, however, the whole multitude of the Israelites conspired against Moses and Aaron, accusing them, saying, "You have killed the people of Jehovah." ### CHAPTER XVII.

Then Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying: "Speak to the Israelites and take from the leaders of each of their ancestral families a rod—that is, twelve rods—and write each man's name upon his rod. But write Aaron's name on the rod of Levi, with one rod for each head of their ancestral houses. Place these in the Tabernacle of the Oracle before the Testimony, where I reveal myself to you. It shall happen that the man whom I choose, his rod will sprout. In this way, I will rid myself of these rebellions with which the Israelites conspire against you." When Moses had explained this to the Israelites, each of the leaders of their ancestral houses gave him a rod, twelve in total, among which was the rod of Aaron; these Moses placed before Jehovah in the Tabernacle of the Oracle. The next day, when Moses entered the Tabernacle of the Oracle, he saw that the rod of Aaron, for the family of Levi, had sprouted; it had brought forth buds, produced blossoms, and yielded almonds. Then Moses brought out all the rods from the presence of Jehovah to all the Israelites; when they saw this, each man took his own rod. And Jehovah commanded Moses to return Aaron’s rod to the front of the Testimony to be kept as a sign for the rebels, so that their complaints against Jehovah might be silenced and they would not die. Afterward, the Israelites complained to Moses, crying out that they were perishing, they were dying, they were all being destroyed; that whoever approached the Tabernacle of Jehovah would die. They asked: "Will there ever be an end to our perishing?"

Every animal that first opens the womb, brought to Jehovah, whether human or beast, shall be yours. However, you must redeem the firstborn of humans and the firstborn of unclean animals. The method of redemption is this: for those a month old, you shall redeem them at the set price of five shekels of silver according to the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs <note>original: "obolorum," used here to represent the Hebrew weight</note>. But do not redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat; they are holy. Sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat as a food offering of sweet aroma to Jehovah. But the meat shall be yours, just as the breast that is presented and the right thigh are yours. <margin>The Red Heifer.</margin>

Then Jehovah spoke to Moses and Aaron in this manner: "This is the statute of the law which Jehovah commands in these words: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer, whole and without blemish, which has never known the yoke. You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, who shall lead her outside the camp and have her sacrificed in his presence. Then the heifer shall be burned in his sight: its hide, flesh, and blood, along with its dung, shall be burned. The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet thread, and cast them into the midst of the burning heifer. Then he shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may enter the camp, though he shall be unclean until evening. The one who burns her shall also wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening. Then a man who is clean shall collect the ashes of the heifer and place them outside the camp in a clean place."

<margin>a. The ashes of this heifer are for making the water of purification, as is taught a little later.</margin>
<gloss>a</gloss> The community of the Israelites shall keep this for the water of purification, which serves as an atonement. Then the one who collected the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigners living among them. Whoever touches the corpse of any human being shall be unclean for seven days. He must purify himself with this water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he shall be clean; but if he is not purified on the third day, he will not be clean on the seventh. Whoever touches the body of a deceased person and is not purified, defiles the Tabernacle of Jehovah; that person shall be cut off from Israel because the water of purification was not sprinkled on him. He remains unclean as long as his uncleanness clings to him.

<margin>The law of a man dying in a tent.</margin>
Next follows the law of a man who dies in a tent. Everyone who enters the tent, and everyone who is already in the tent, shall be unclean for seven days. Every open vessel that has no cover fastened on it shall be unclean. Whoever, out of doors, touches someone killed by a weapon, or a corpse, or human bones, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days. For such an unclean person, some of the dust from the burned sin offering <note>the ashes of the red heifer</note> shall be taken, and fresh water shall be poured over it in a vessel. Then a clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the vessels, and all the people who were there, as well as the one who touched the bones, the slain, the dead, or the grave. The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third and seventh days, and on the seventh day he shall be purified; then he shall wash his clothes, bathe his body in water, and

<column-break/>

at evening he shall be clean. But the man who is unclean and is not purified shall be cut off from the midst of the community, for he has defiled the sanctuary of Jehovah by not being sprinkled with the water of purification; he is unclean. This shall be a permanent statute for them: the one who sprinkles the water of purification shall wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening. Whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

### CHAPTER XXI.

But when the Canaanite king of Arad, who dwelt to the south, heard that the Israelites were coming by the way of the spies, he attacked them in battle and led some of them away as captives. Then the Israelites made a vow to Jehovah, that if He would subject those people to them, they would utterly destroy their cities. When Jehovah heard their plea and the Canaanites were subdued through Him, they utterly destroyed both the people and their cities; for this reason, they named the place Hormah <note>Hormah means "destruction" or "devotion to God through destruction"</note>. But when they set out from Mount Hor to go toward the Red Sea to bypass the borders of the Edomites, the people began to grow weary of the journey and to complain against God and against Moses, asking why they had been led out of Egypt to die in the wilderness, where there was neither bread nor water; for they loathed that most worthless bread <note>referring to the Manna</note>. Therefore, Jehovah sent fiery serpents <note>original: "præsteres serpentes," from the Greek for "burning," referring to the venomous bite</note> among the people, and as they bit the men, many of the Israelites died. So they went to Moses and confessed that they had sinned, speaking both against him and against Jehovah: they begged him to pray to Jehovah to deliver them from these serpents. Therefore, as Moses prayed for the people, Jehovah replied that he should make a fiery serpent and set it upon a pole: thus it would be that everyone who was bitten and looked upon it would be healed. So Moses made a bronze serpent and raised it upon a pole. Thus, if a serpent happened to bite anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and be healed. Departing from there, the Israelites camped at Oboth. From Oboth they set out and camped at the heaps of Abarim, in the wilderness which is opposite the Moabites, toward the rising of the sun. Setting out from there, they encamped at the river Zared. From there they moved and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the desert and flows from the borders of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the border of the Moabites, dividing them from the Amorites.

Then Balaam commanded him to remain there by his sacrifice while he himself withdrew. And Jehovah met him, and having instructed him on what to say, ordered him to return to Balak and speak thus. When he came to him, he found him standing by his sacrifice along with the princes of the Moabites. And Balak asked: "What has Jehovah spoken?" Then he began his pronouncement:

> Arise, Balak, and hear; listen to me, son of Zippor <note>original: "Sepphoris"</note>. God is not a man, that he should lie; nor the son of man, that he should repent. Would he speak and not act? Would he promise and not fulfill? Truly, I have received favorable omens, and I shall not return anything but favorable omens: No fault is seen in the descendants of Jacob; no crime exists among the Israelites. Jehovah their God is with them, <margin>b</margin> accompanied by the shout of a king. God, who led them out of Egypt, is endowed with the strength of a unicorn <note>original: "monocerotio"; referring to the 'reem' or wild ox, often translated as unicorn in older texts</note>. <margin>b</margin> Indeed, there is no divination among the descendants of Jacob, nor is there any sorcery among the Israelites. In due time it shall be proclaimed concerning the house of Jacob and the Israelites what God has done. Behold, a people rising like a lioness, stirred up like a lion: he shall not lie down until he has devoured the prey and drunk the blood of the slain.

Then Balak said to Balaam: "At least do not pursue them with curses, nor with favorable omens." To which Balaam replied: "Did I not tell you before that whatever Jehovah commanded, that I must do?" And Balak said: "Come, I will lead you to another place, if perhaps it will please Jehovah that you might curse them for me from there." Then he led him to the peak of Peor <note>original: "Phegoris"</note>, which looks toward Jeshimon. And Balaam commanded him to build seven altars there and prepare seven bulls and as many rams. Balak did as he was told, and sacrificed bulls and rams upon the altars.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

When Balaam saw that it pleased Jehovah to follow the Israelites with favorable omens, he did not go, as he had done once and twice before, to seek out an oracle. Instead, turning his gaze toward the desert and looking intently with his eyes, he saw the Israelites camping tribe by tribe. Being inspired by God, he began his pronouncement in these words:

> Thus says Balaam the son of Beor; thus says the man <margin>a</margin> with closed eyes <note>original: "obthuratis oculis"; some translations interpret this as "open eyes," but this Latin text suggests "closed" to the physical world but open to the divine</note>; thus says the hearer of divine words, who saw the things foretold by the Almighty, <margin>b</margin> to whom, having fallen,

<column-break/>

<margin>c. When he saw the divine spirit.</margin>
his eyes were opened. How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, and your dwellings, O Israelite! Like spreading valleys, like gardens planted by a river, like tents pitched by Jehovah, like cedars situated near the water. Water shall drip from his bucket, and his seed shall be in abundant moisture; his king shall be exalted above Agag, and his kingdom shall be lifted up. God led him out of Egypt, endowed with the strength of a unicorn. He shall consume the nations that oppose him, break their bones, and shatter them with arrows. Who would rouse him when he crouches and lies down like a lion or a lioness? Blessed is he who wishes you well; cursed is he who wishes you ill.

At this, Balak grew angry with Balaam and, clapping his hands, said: "I called you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them now three times! Therefore, flee from here to the place you came from. I had intended to honor you, but know that Jehovah has deprived you of honor." To which Balaam replied: "As if I did not also say to the messengers you sent to me: even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not of my own accord do anything good or evil against the command of Jehovah; rather, what Jehovah commanded me, that I would speak. And indeed, I am now going to my people; but I wish to explain to you what this people will one day do to your people." Then, beginning his pronouncement, he spoke thus:

> Thus says Balaam the son of Beor; thus says the man with closed eyes; thus says the hearer of divine words and one conscious of the supreme knowledge, who sees the foretellings of the Almighty, and to whom, having fallen, his eyes were opened. I shall see him, but not now; I shall behold <margin>Matthew 2.</margin> him, but not soon. A star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall arise out of Israel, which shall crush the nobles of the Moabites and subdue all the sons of Seth. And with Edom subdued, Seir shall be occupied by its enemies, while the Israelites perform brave deeds. A ruler shall come from the line of Jacob who shall destroy the remnants of the city.

Then, looking upon the Amalekites, he began his pronouncement thus:

> Amalek was the first of the nations, but in the end, he shall perish forever.

Then, looking upon the Kenites <note>original: "Cenæos"</note>, he began his pronouncement thus:

> Though you have a strong dwelling and have placed your nest in a rock, yet the Kenite shall be for devastation, until the Assyrian carries you away captive.

Then he began to speak his pronouncement thus:

> Alas, who shall live when God performs this? When a fleet from the borders of Kittim <note>original: "Cittimorum"; usually associated with Cyprus or the Western Mediterranean</note> shall subdue the Assyrian and the Hebrew <note>original: "Hebrem"</note>, who himself shall also perish forever.

Then Balaam departed from there and hastened to return to the place he had come from; and Balak also went his own way.

### CHAPTER XXVII.

<margin>30</margin>**T**hen the daughters of Zelophehad <note>original: "Salphaadi"</note>, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph (the names of these daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah), <margin>1</margin>came forward and stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, <margin>2</margin>the leaders, and the entire congregation at the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Oracle <note>The Tent of Meeting</note>. They pointed out that their father had died in the wilderness, though he was not among those in Korah’s company who had gathered against Jehovah; rather, he died for his own sin and had no sons. "Why," they asked, "should our father’s name be taken away from his family because he had no son? Grant us a possession among our father's kinsmen." <margin>40</margin>When Moses brought their case before Jehovah, Jehovah replied: "The daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly. You shall certainly give them an inheritance of possession among their father's kinsmen, and you shall transfer their father’s inheritance to them. Then, instruct the Israelites that if a man dies without a son, they shall pass his inheritance to his daughter. If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers. If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father's brothers. If his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the next of kin in his family, and he shall possess it. This shall be a legal statute for the Israelites, just as Jehovah commanded Moses." Jehovah also said to Moses: "Go up into this mountain of Abarim to view the land I am giving to the Israelites. After you have seen it, you also will be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron was gathered, because you both rebelled against my command in the wilderness of Zin during the strife of the multitude, when you did not honor me as holy at the waters in their sight."

<column-break/>

(These are the waters of Meribah <note>original: "iurgij," meaning "of strife"</note> in Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.) Then Moses spoke: "May Jehovah, the animator of the spirits of all mortals, appoint someone over the republic <note>the community of Israel</note> who may go out and come in before them, who may lead them out and bring them back, so that Jehovah’s multitude may not be like sheep <margin>Joshua.</margin> lacking a shepherd." Jehovah said to him: "Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man of heart <note>a man of spirit or wisdom</note>, and lay your hand <margin>Deut. 3.</margin> upon him. Set him before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation; commission him in their sight and bestow some of your authority upon him, so that the whole community of the Israelites may obey him. He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the ritual of CLARITY <note>original: "CLARITATIS"; likely referring to the Urim, the sacred lot used by the High Priest to discern God's will</note> before Jehovah. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in—he and all the Israelites with him, the entire multitude." So Moses did as Jehovah commanded him. He took Joshua and set him before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, laid his hands on him, and gave him his instructions, just as Jehovah had commanded through Moses.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

<margin>The law of the perpetual sacrifice.</margin>**J**ehovah also spoke to Moses in these words: "Command the Israelites to take care to offer me my food-offering for a divine ceremony at its appointed time, as a soothing aroma to me. Say to them: This is the divine ceremony you shall make for Jehovah: two yearling lambs without blemish every day as a regular burnt offering. Offer one in the morning and the other in the evening, along with a tenth of an ephah <note>a dry measure</note> of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with a fourth of a hin <note>a liquid measure</note> of pressed oil. This is a perpetual, regular burnt offering, like that which was made at Mount Sinai, <margin>10</margin>the aroma of which ceremony delights Jehovah. The drink offering shall be a fourth of a hin of wine for each lamb; the strong drink shall be poured out to Jehovah in the sanctuary. The second lamb you shall offer in the evening, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, a divine ceremony to soothe Jehovah. On the Sabbath day, <margin>Matt. 12.</margin> offer two yearling lambs without blemish, with a grain offering of two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, and its drink offering. This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, <margin>20</margin>in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its drink offering. At the beginnings of your months, present a burnt offering to Jehovah: two young bulls, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without blemish, with a grain offering of three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull; a grain offering of two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for the one ram; and a grain offering of one-tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb. Jehovah is delighted by the aroma of this ceremony of burnt offerings. Their drink offering shall be <margin>30</margin>half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a fourth of a hin for each lamb. This is the monthly burnt offering to be made for each month of the year. Also, one male goat shall be offered as a sin offering to Jehovah, with its drink offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering. <margin>Exo. 12.</margin> On the fourteenth day of the first month is Jehovah’s Passover. <margin>Levit. 23.</margin> On the fifteenth day of the same month is a feast; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten. On the first of these days, a sacred assembly shall be held; you shall do no worldly work."

Then one sin offering goat, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and the wine libation. These things you shall do for Jehovah during your appointed feasts, in addition to your vows and your voluntary gifts for your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings. Moses explained all these things to the Israelites, just as Jehovah had commanded him.
