But if, upon hearing it, her father prohibits her, then all her vows and the religious obligation by which she bound herself shall be void; and Jehovah <note>original: "Ioua"; a Latinized form of the Hebrew name for God, Yahweh</note> will forgive her, since she was prohibited by her father. Furthermore, if she has a husband when she takes her vows, or has bound herself by some rashly uttered promise, and if her husband hears of it and says nothing to her, then her vows and the religious obligation by which she bound herself shall stand firm. But if the husband, upon hearing the matter, prohibits it, he shall release the vow she had taken and the rashly spoken word by which she bound herself, and Jehovah will forgive her. But the vow of a widow or a divorced woman, by whatever she has bound herself, shall stand firm. If, however, she made a vow in her husband’s house, or bound herself with an oath-bound religious obligation, and her husband heard the matter and bore it in silence, neither prohibiting it, then all her vows and every religious obligation by which she bound herself shall stand firm. But if the husband nullified the matter upon hearing it, then whatever she uttered by vowing and binding herself shall be void, as it was nullified by her husband; and Jehovah shall forgive her. Every vow and every religious obligation of a sworn fast <note>original: "iurati ieiunij"</note> her husband shall make either firm or void. If he says nothing against it from day to day, he confirms all her vows and every obligation by which she is bound; he makes it firm because he bore the matter in silence when he heard it. But if he nullifies them sometime after he has heard them, he shall bear her guilt. And these indeed are the statutes which Jehovah commanded Moses concerning a husband and a wife, and between a father and a daughter while she is still a young girl in the house of her father.

### CHAPTER XXXI.

<margin>Num. 3.</margin>
Jehovah also commanded Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites on behalf of the Israelites, after which he would pass away to his ancestors. Therefore Moses commanded the people that they should hold a muster of their soldiers to invade the Midianites and exact Jehovah's punishment from them. From all the tribes of the Israelites, they were to send a thousand men for that expedition. Thus, from the forces of the Israelites, one thousand were chosen from each tribe, that is, twelve thousand equipped for war, whom Moses sent on the expedition together with Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest <note>original: "pontificis"; literally 'pontiff', used here to mean the High Priest</note>, who carried the sacred vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm with him. They then attacked the Midianites, as Jehovah had commanded Moses, and killed every male. They also put to death the kings of the Midianites during that indiscriminate slaughter: namely Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—the five kings of the Midianites. They also executed Balaam son of Beor with the sword. The Israelites took the women and little ones of the Midianites as captives, and having plundered all their cattle, wealth, and goods, and having burned all the towns and forts in which they lived, they took all the spoils and all the prey of both humans and cattle. They brought the captives, the prey, and the spoils to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the multitude of the Israelites at the camp in the plains of Moab, which is by the Jordan near Jericho. To meet them, Moses,

<column-break/>

Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the republic proceeded outside the camp. "Is it really so," he said, "that you have saved all the women? But these are the very ones who, at the advice of Balaam, led the Israelites to offend Jehovah in the matter of Peor <note>referring to the worship of the idol Baal-Peor, which brought a plague upon the people</note>, from which a disaster arose within Jehovah’s community. <margin>10</margin> Therefore, kill all the male children, and kill all the women who have had knowledge of a man by lying with him. Purify also every garment, every leather vessel, everything made of goat skins, and <margin>Lev. 6, 11.</margin> every wooden instrument." Then Eleazar the <margin>20</margin> priest spoke thus to the soldiers who had gone to war: "This is the statute of the law commanded to Moses by Jehovah: gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—whatever, in short, can endure fire—purify by applying fire, and then let it be cleansed with the water of purification. There were sixteen thousand humans, of which thirty-two fell to Jehovah. And Moses gave that portion set aside for Jehovah to Eleazar the priest, as Jehovah had ordered. ### CHAPTER XXXII.

<margin>The Reubenites and Gadites request a place to settle across the Jordan.</margin>
Now the Reubenites and the Gadites had a very large number of livestock. When they noticed that the land of Jazer and the region of Gilead were suitable for livestock, they came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community, and spoke to them as follows: "Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Shebam, Nebo, and Beon—the lands which Jehovah has subdued before the community of Israel—are lands suitable for livestock, and your servants have livestock." Therefore, they asked that if they had found favor in his eyes, this land might be given to them as a possession, and that they might not be made to cross over the Jordan River. Moses responded to them in this manner: "Shall your kinsmen go to war while you sit idle here? Why do you discourage the hearts of the Israelites from entering the land that Jehovah has given them? This is exactly what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to scout the land. When they reached the Valley of Eshcol and explored those borders, they discouraged the hearts of the Israelites from entering the land given to them by Jehovah. Because of this, Jehovah's anger was kindled, and he swore that those men who had come out of Egypt, who were now over twenty years old, would not see the land he had promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they had not fulfilled their duty to him—except for Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua the son of Nun, who performed their duty toward Jehovah. Thus Jehovah was angry with the Israelites and made them wander back and forth through the wilderness for forty years, until that entire generation that had offended him was consumed. And look, you have risen up in your fathers' place, a brood of sinful men, to increase the heat of Jehovah's anger against Israel. For if you turn away from him, he will leave them in the wilderness even longer, and you will destroy all these people." Then they drew near to him and

They shall receive their possession by drawing lots according to their clans, so that those who are more numerous shall hold more, and those who are fewer shall hold less, and whatever place the lot assigns to each, he shall have it, with the possessions divided among the families of the tribes. But if they do not drive out the inhabitants, those whom they allow to remain will be like barbs in their eyes and thorns in their sides, and they will be troublesome to them in the land where they settle; and it will happen that what I decreed to do to them, I will do to you instead."

### CHAPTER XXXIV.

<margin>Description of Canaan. Joshua 15.</margin>
Then he said, "Command them in this manner: When you enter Canaan, the land which you will receive by lot as a possession shall be the land of Canaan in its full extent, whose southern side shall be for you from the wilderness of Zin to the borders of Edom <note>original: "Iumææ"</note>, and that southern side shall extend from the end of the Salt Sea <note>The Dead Sea</note> to the east. Your border shall turn from the south to the Ascent of Scorpions <note>original: "aſcenſum ſcorpiorum"; a mountain pass</note>, pass on to Zin, and reaching from the south to Kadesh-barnea, it shall go out to Hazar-addar and extend to Azmon. From Azmon it shall turn toward the River of Egypt and end at the Sea. For the western border, you shall have the Great Sea, and the coast itself shall be the western limit. For the northern border, you shall go from the Sea to Mount Hor, and from there you shall proceed to the entrance of Hamath, so that the border goes out to Zedad, and being led to Ziphron, it ends at Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern border. For the eastern border, you shall mark it out from Hazar-enan to Shepham. From Shepham the border shall go down to Riblah, on the east of Ain; from here it shall descend and reach the shore of the Sea of Chinnereth <note>The Sea of Galilee</note> on the east; then sloping down toward the Jordan, it shall be terminated by the Salt Sea. With these boundaries, you shall have the land defined on all sides." Then Moses commanded the Israelites to occupy that land by lot, which Jehovah had ordered to be given to the nine and a half tribes. For two tribes and a half—namely the tribes of Reuben and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh—had already received their possession by their families on this side of the Jordan, across from Jericho, toward the rising sun. Then Jehovah spoke with Moses and showed him the names of those who were to divide the possession of the land for them. These are: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun. Then they were to choose one prince from each tribe for the distribution of the land, whose names are these: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh; from the tribe of Simeon, Samuel the son of Ammihud; from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon; from the tribe of Dan, the prince Bukki the son of Jogli. Of the descendants of Joseph: from the tribe of Manasseh, the prince Hanniel the son of Ephod; from the tribe of Ephraim, the prince Kemuel the son of Shiphtan; from the tribe of Zebulun, the prince Elizaphan the son of Parnach; from the tribe of Issachar, the prince Paltiel the son of Azzan; from the tribe of Asher, the prince Ahihud the son of Shelomi; from the tribe of Naphtali, the prince Pardahel the son of Ammihud. These are the ones whom Jehovah commanded to divide the possessions for the Israelites in Canaan.

<margin>Joshua 21; Deuteronomy 4</margin>
Beyond the walls on the eastern side, you shall measure two thousand cubits, and likewise on the south, the west, and the north, with the town remaining in the center; these shall be the suburbs <note>original: "pomoeria"; the open space or pasture land surrounding a city</note> of the towns. Among the towns granted to the Levites, there shall be six cities of refuge where those who have struck someone <note>original: "percussores"</note> may flee for safety. In addition to these, you shall give them forty-two other towns, so that the towns given to the Levites shall total forty-eight, along with their suburbs. From the land possessed by the Israelites, you shall take more from those who have more and fewer from those who have less, so that each tribe shares its towns with the Levites in proportion to the size of the inheritance they occupy. <margin>Deuteronomy 19; Refuges; Joshua 20</margin>
When you have crossed the Jordan into the land of Canaan and have built your towns, you shall designate cities of refuge where anyone who kills a person unintentionally <note>original: "per imprudentiam"; by mistake or without malice</note> may flee. You shall use these towns to escape the avengers <note>original: "uindices"; specifically the 'blood avenger'—a relative of the deceased tasked with seeking justice</note>, so that the one who killed does not die before his case has been heard in judgment. These towns that you designate as places of refuge shall be six: three across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. These six cities shall serve as a refuge for Israelites, for strangers, and for those dwelling among you, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there. But if he strikes someone with an iron tool and the person dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death. Likewise, if he strikes someone with a stone held in the hand that can cause death, and the person dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death. Likewise, if he strikes someone with a wooden weapon held in the hand that is lethal, and the person dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death. The avenger of blood shall kill the murderer; he shall kill him whenever he meets him. But if he pushes someone out of hatred, or intentionally

<margin>Deuteronomy 19</margin>
hurls something at him and he dies, or if he strikes him with his hand out of enmity and he dies, the one who struck him shall be put to death; he is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall kill the murderer when he finds him. However, if he pushes someone by pure chance <note>original: "fortè fortuna"</note> without enmity, or hurls any weapon at him unintentionally, or accidentally throws any lethal stone that happens to hit him so that he dies—though he was not his enemy nor was he plotting him harm—then the assembly shall judge between the one who struck and the blood avenger according to these laws. The assembly shall protect the killer from the blood avenger and send him back to the city of refuge to which he had fled; he must remain there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil. But if the killer ever goes outside the borders of the city of refuge to which he fled, and the blood avenger finds him and kills him outside those borders, the avenger shall not be guilty of murder. For the killer should have stayed in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; only after that death may he return to his own land. These shall be your legal statutes throughout your generations wherever you live. Anyone who kills a person shall be put to death only on the testimony of witnesses. The testimony of a single witness shall not be enough to sentence a person to death. You shall not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of a capital crime; he must be put to death. Nor shall you accept a ransom from one who has fled to a city of refuge to allow him to return to his home

<column-break/>

before the death of the high priest, lest you defile the land in which you live. For blood defiles the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it. Therefore, do not pollute the land where you reside, in which I also dwell. For I, Jehovah, dwell among the Israelites.

### CHAPTER XXXVI.

<margin>Numbers 21</margin>
Then the heads of the families of the descendants of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, came forward and spoke: Jehovah commanded you, my lord, to give the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot; furthermore, you were commanded by Jehovah to give the inheritance of our kinsman Zelophehad <note>original: "Salphaadi"</note> to his daughters. Now, if they marry men from other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken away from our ancestral heritage and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry; thus it will be taken from our allotted inheritance. When the Jubilee <note>original: "Iubile"; the year of release every fifty years when land returned to its original owners</note> of the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be permanently added to the tribe they joined and removed from our patrimony. Then Moses, by the command of Jehovah, instructed the Israelites in this manner: The tribe of the sons of Joseph is right in what they say. This is what Jehovah commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whomever they wish, provided they marry within the tribe of their father’s clan. In this way, the inheritance of the Israelites

<margin>The Law of the daughters of Zelophehad; Tobit 7</margin>
will not be transferred from tribe to tribe, but every Israelite shall hold fast to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe. Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the Israelites shall marry someone from her father’s tribal clan, so that every Israelite may possess his paternal inheritance. No inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another, for every tribe of the Israelites shall keep its own land. The daughters of Zelophehad did exactly as Jehovah commanded Moses: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins. They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained within the tribe of their father's clan.

# DEUTERONOMY

In the eleventh month, *Moses* spoke to the *Israelites* all that Jehovah had commanded him for them, after the fall of *Sihon* king of the *Amorites*, who lived in *Heshbon*, and *Og* king of *Bashan*, who lived in *Ashtaroth* in *Edrei*. On this side of the *Jordan*, I say, in the borders of the *Moabites*, *Moses* began to explain the law in these words. Jehovah our God warned us at *Horeb* <note>original: "Horebo"; another name for Mount Sinai</note> that we had stayed long enough on that mountain; he commanded us to turn back and head toward the mountain of the *Amorites* and all the neighboring places—the plains, the mountains, the valleys, the south, and the coast—namely into *Canaan* and *Lebanon*, as far as the great river *Euphrates*. For he was granting those borders to us: therefore, we were to go in and take possession of the land which he had sworn to give to our ancestors *Abraham*, *Isaac*, and *Jacob*, and to their descendants after them. At that time, I proposed to you that I alone could not lead you, as you had been so increased by Jehovah your God that you already equaled the multitude of the stars. I wished indeed that Jehovah, the God of your fathers, might increase you even a thousandfold more and follow you with his favor, as he had promised; but how could I alone bear your business, your burdens, and your disputes? Therefore, I asked that you provide the wisest, most prudent, and most experienced men of your tribes, whom I would appoint as your leaders. When you answered that this pleased you, I chose the chiefs of your tribes, wise and experienced men, and appointed them as your officials: captains of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens, as well as tribal officers. I commanded your judges at that time to hear the controversies of their kinsmen and to judge justly in cases between fellow citizens or with foreigners, and not to show favoritism in judgments; rather, they should hear the lowly as well as the powerful and fear no man, for judgment belongs to God. Cases that were too difficult for them, they were to refer to me for a hearing. At that time, I also commanded you in everything you were to do. Setting out from *Horeb*, we traveled through all that vast and terrible wilderness which you saw, toward the *Amorite* mountain, just as Jehovah our God had commanded us, and we reached *Kadesh-barnea*. Then I pointed out to you that you had reached the *Amorite* mountain which Jehovah our God would give us, and I showed you that Jehovah your God was assigning that land to you; therefore, you should not doubt or fear to enter into possession of it, as it was promised to you by Jehovah, the God of your fathers. But you all came to me and urged that men be sent ahead to scout the region for you and to inform you about the way you should enter and the towns you should attack. When this plan pleased me, I chose twelve of you, one from each tribe, who set out to climb into the mountains. Reaching as far as the river *Eshcol* and having scouted the region, they took some of the fruits of that land with them; and returning to us, they reported that the land Jehovah our God was giving us was good. But you, unwill-

<column-break/>

ing to go up, provoked Jehovah your God, and muttering in your tents, you repeatedly said that Jehovah brought you out of *Egypt* because he hated you, so that he might hand you over to the *Amorites* to be destroyed. You said you did not know where to turn; that your own kinsmen had broken your spirit by reporting that the people there were both greater and more powerful than you, with cities that were massive and fortified to the heavens; and that they had even seen the <term>Anakim</term> <note>original: "Enaquinos"; a race of giants described in the Hebrew Bible as descendants of Anak</note> there. I urged you not to be terrified or afraid of them, for Jehovah your God, who goes before you, would fight for you, just as he did in *Egypt* before your very eyes, and also in the wilderness, where you saw how we were carried by him as a father carries his son, throughout the entire journey you made until you reached this place. But in this <margin>Exodus 13</margin> matter, you did not trust Jehovah your God, who went before you on the way (to scout a place for your camps), by fire at night so you could see the path you were walking, and by a cloud during the day. Therefore, Jehovah, having heard the sound of these words, was angry and swore that no one of such a wicked generation would see <margin>Numbers 14</margin> that good land which he had sworn to give to your ancestors, except for *Caleb* son of *Jephunneh*; for he would see it, and God would grant to him and his children the land he had walked upon, because he had performed his duty to Jehovah. Your little ones also, who you said would be plunder, and your children, who today do not know good from evil, they shall arrive there; to them I will <margin>Numbers 14</margin> hand over that land to possess. But as for you, turn back into the wilderness toward the Red Sea. Then, having confessed your sin against Jehovah, you answered me that you would go up and wage war, just as Jehovah our God had commanded you. And so, girded with weapons, you prepared to climb the mountain. But Jehovah warned me to dissuade you from that expedition, lest you be defeated by your enemies since he himself would not be present with you. When I reported this to you, you did not obey; and despising Jehovah’s warnings, you insolently climbed the mountain. Therefore, the *Amorite* inhabitant of that mountain came out against you and, chasing you as bees do, cut you down from *Seir* all the way to *Hormah*. Thus you returned and wept before Jehovah; but he did not listen to you, nor did he lend you his ear.

Do not follow foreign gods from the gods of the neighboring nations, 
<margin>Luke 4</margin>
lest Jehovah <note>original: "Ioua"; a Latinization of the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God, commonly rendered as 'Jehovah' or 'Yahweh'</note> your God, who dwells among you and is a jealous God, becomes angry with you and removes you from the earth. Do not test Jehovah your God, just as you tested Him at Massah <note>The place where the Israelites quarreled and doubted God's presence, demanding water from the rock (Exodus 17:7)</note>. 
<margin>Matthew 4, Luke 4, Numbers 22, Exodus 17</margin>
Keep the commandments of Jehovah your God, along with the testimonies and the statutes He has commanded you. Do what is approved and pleasing in His eyes, so that it may go well with you, and that you may enter into the possession of that good land which He swore to your ancestors, to drive out all your enemies before you, as Jehovah promised. When your children ask you in time to come what these testimonies, statutes, and laws mean which Jehovah your God has commanded you, you shall answer them: "When we were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, we were led out from there by Jehovah with a strong hand. Jehovah pursued the Egyptians and Pharaoh, with his entire household, with great and terrible signs and wonders before your eyes, and He led us out from there to bring us into the land He had sworn to our ancestors, to give it to us." Therefore, Jehovah commanded us to perform all these statutes in fear of Jehovah our God, so that it may be well with us as long as we live, as is the case today. And it will be our righteousness if we take care to perform all this instruction before Jehovah our God, just as He commanded us.

### CHAPTER VII.

<margin>30</margin>
<margin>How the Canaanites should be dealt with. Exodus 23, 34.</margin>
When Jehovah your God brings you into the land you are entering to occupy, and destroys many nations before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—seven nations greater and more powerful than you, and when He has given them to you to be struck down, you must destroy them utterly. You shall not enter into a treaty with them, nor shall you show them mercy. You shall not contract marriages with them, neither by giving your daughters to their sons, nor by taking their daughters for your sons. Otherwise, they will lead your sons away from Jehovah to the worship of foreign gods; 
<margin>40</margin>
thus it would happen that Jehovah, being angry, would destroy you quickly. But you shall do this to them: tear down their altars, break their statues, cut down their sacred groves <note>original: "lucos"; likely referring to Asherah poles or trees dedicated to Canaanite deities</note>, and burn their idols with fire. For you are a holy people to Jehovah your God, who chose you to be His own special people, above all other peoples on the face of the earth. It was not because you were the most numerous of all peoples that Jehovah embraced you and chose you—for you are the smallest of all peoples—but because He loved you, and to keep the oath He swore to your ancestors, He led you out with a strong hand and 
<margin>50</margin>
liberated you from the house of slavery, that is, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Know therefore that Jehovah your God is God—the faithful God, who keeps His covenant and mercy toward those who love Him and keep His commandments, even to a thousand generations; but He repays those who hate Him with open destruction, and without doubt He will repay them to their face with the rewards they deserve for their deeds. Therefore, keep this instruction, the statutes, and the laws which I command you to hold fast today.

### CHAPTER VIII.

Take care to follow every instruction that I deliver to you today, so that you may live, increase, and enter to possess the land which Jehovah swore to your ancestors. Remember the whole journey on which Jehovah your God has led you these forty years through the wilderness, to humble you and test you, to learn what was in your heart—whether you would keep His commandments or not. Thus He 
<margin>Manna. Matthew 4, Luke 4</margin> humbled you and fed you with manna, which was unknown to both you and your ancestors, to show you that man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah. Your clothes did not wear out, nor did your feet swell during these forty years. Convince yourselves of this: just as a man disciplines his own son, so you are disciplined by Jehovah your God. Therefore, keep His commandments, and by living according to His prescriptions, fear Him. For Jehovah your God is bringing you into a good land—a land flowing with rivers of water, with springs

It is a land in which you will eat without scarcity of food and lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains you will dig metals <note>likely referring to copper</note>. When you have eaten and are satisfied, give thanks 
<margin>Gratitude</margin> to Jehovah your God for that good land He has given you. Otherwise, when you have eaten your fill and have built and lived in elegant houses, and when your herds and flocks, your silver and gold, and indeed all your possessions have increased, you might become proud in spirit and consign Jehovah your God to oblivion—the one who led you out of the house of Egyptian slavery. But if you forget Jehovah your God and follow other gods, serving and worshiping them, I testify to you today that you will surely perish, no less than the nations which Jehovah is destroying before you, because you would not listen to the voice of Jehovah your God.

### CHAPTER VIII.

<margin>Manna. Thus He humbled you and fed you with manna when you were hungry—a food unknown to you and your ancestors—to show you that man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah. tains and lakes springing up through the valleys and the mountains: a land of wheat, barley, vines, figs, and pomegranates; a land abundant in olive oil and honey; a land where you will eat without scarcity and lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains you will dig metals <note>likely referring to copper or bronze ores</note>. ### CHAPTER IX.

**H**ear, O Israelites: you are now about to cross the Jordan to dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourselves, with great cities fortified to the heavens—a people great and tall, the Anakim <note>original: "Enaquini"; a race of giants mentioned in the Bible</note>, about whom you know it is said, "Who can stand against the Anakim?" Understand today that it is Jehovah your God who goes before you as a consuming fire; He will destroy them and subdue them before you, so that you may quickly drive them out and destroy them, just as Jehovah promised you. Do not think in your hearts, once Jehovah your God has scattered them before you, "Because of my righteousness Jehovah has brought me in to occupy this land." Rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that Jehovah is driving them out before you. It is not because of your righteousness or the integrity of your heart that you are entering to possess their land <margin>The Golden Calf</margin>; but Jehovah your God is driving out these nations because of their own vices, and to fulfill the oath He swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Know, therefore, that it is not because of your righteousness that Jehovah your God is giving you this good land to possess; for you are a stiff-necked <note>original: "ceruicosus"; meaning stubborn or obstinate</note> people. Indeed, at Horeb you offended Him to such an extent that in His wrath He almost destroyed you. When I had ascended the mountain to receive the stone tablets—the tablets of the covenant which Jehovah <note>original: "Ioua"; a Latinization of the Tetragrammaton, the divine name often rendered as 'the LORD'</note> was striking with you—and I remained on that mountain for forty days and forty nights, taking neither food nor drink; and when Jehovah had given me the two stone tablets inscribed by the divine finger, upon which were written all the same words that Jehovah Himself had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly: I say, when the forty days and nights were finished, and Jehovah had delivered those two stone tablets of the covenant to me, He began to speak with me thus: "Rise, go down from here quickly; for your people, whom you led out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They have turned aside quickly from the path which I commanded them, and have cast an idol for themselves." Furthermore, He said, "I see clearly that this is a <term>stiff-necked people</term> <note>A biblical idiom for stubbornness, referring to an ox that refuses to bow its neck to the yoke</note>. Allow me to overthrow them and erase their name from the very nature of things, and I will lead out from you a nation mightier and more numerous than they." Then I turned and descended from the mountain, which was then blazing with fire, carrying the two tablets of the covenant in both hands. And behold, I perceived your crime against Jehovah your God: you had cast a calf for yourselves; you had turned aside so quickly from the path Jehovah had prescribed for you. Then I seized the two tablets in both hands and threw them down, breaking them before your very eyes. Afterward, I lay prostrate before Jehovah, as before, for forty days and as many nights, using neither food nor drink in the meantime, because of your great crime, by which you provoked Jehovah to anger. For I was terrified of that wrath and the heat with which Jehovah was incited toward your destruction. Therefore, Jehovah listened to me on that occasion as well. <margin>2</margin> I also prayed at that same time for Aaron, with whom Jehovah was also deathly angry. But as for your crime—the calf you had made—I seized it and burned it with fire, and after it was crushed and ground into the finest dust, I threw that dust into the stream that flowed down from the mountain. Nor was it only there; at Taberah, at Massah, and at the <term>Graves of Craving</term> <note>original: "Bustā cupiditatis"; usually rendered as Kibroth-hattaavah</note> you offended Jehovah. Likewise, when Jehovah sent you from Kadesh-barnea to go and occupy the land given to you by Him, you resisted the command of Jehovah your God; you neither believed Him nor obeyed His word. Briefly, from the time I first knew you, you have always been rebellious against Jehovah. For that reason, I lay prostrate before Jehovah for forty days and as many nights (for He had determined to destroy you), and I supplicated Him with these words: "O Lord Jehovah, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, whom You redeemed by Your greatness, and whom You led out of Egypt with a strong hand. Remember Your servants—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look upon the hardness, the impiety, and the crime of this people, lest those from whose borders You led us out should keep saying: 'Because Jehovah was unable to lead them into the land He promised them, and because He hated them, He led them out to slay them in the wilderness.' Yet they are Your people and Your heritage, whom You led out by Your great power and Your outstretched arm."

### CHAPTER X.

<margin>The second tablets. Exodus 34.</margin>
Then Jehovah commanded me to cut two stone tablets similar to the first ones, and then, having made a wooden chest <note>The Ark of the Covenant</note>, to ascend the mountain to Him. For He would write on the tablets the same words that had been on the first ones I broke, so that I might put them in the chest. Therefore, I made a chest of cedar wood, cut two stone tablets similar to the previous ones, and carrying them with me, I ascended the mountain. And He inscribed on the tablets the same things as before: namely, the Ten Commandments <note>original: "decem dicta"; literally 'ten sayings'</note> which He had spoken to us on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly, and He delivered them to me. Then I departed, and when I descended from the mountain, I placed those tablets in the chest I had made; and there they remain, just as Jehovah commanded me. 
<margin>Numbers 33, Numbers 20.</margin>
Then the Israelites set out from the wells of the Jaakanites to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar performed the priesthood in his place. From there they set out for Gudgodah, and then to Jotbathah, a land overflowing with rivers. At that time, <margin>The duty of the Levites.</margin> Jehovah set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah, to stand before Jehovah to minister to Him, and to celebrate His name, just as is done today. And for that reason, the Levites have no portion or inheritance with their kinsmen, because Jehovah your God is their inheritance, just as He promised them. I, therefore, stayed on the mountain as long as before—namely, forty days and as many nights—and Jehovah heard me then also, so that He ceased His desire to destroy you; and He commanded me to go before you on this journey, as you enter to possess the land which He swore to your ancestors He would give to you. Now, Israelites, what does Jehovah your God require of you, except that you fear Jehovah your God, that you walk entirely in His ways, that you love Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul: that you keep His precepts and statutes, which I deliver to you today, so that it may be well with you? Since the heavens and the highest heavens belong to Jehovah your God, as does the earth and everything in it, He nevertheless embraced your ancestors with love and chose their descendants above all other nations, as is apparent. Therefore, circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not be <margin>True circumcision.</margin> stiff-necked any longer. For Jehovah your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords: the great, mighty, and terrible God, who shows no partiality nor accepts bribes, and who renders justice to orphans and widows: and He loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing. Therefore, love the foreigners, for you yourselves were foreigners <margin>1 Chronicles 19, Job 34, Romans 2, Galatians 2, Matthew 4, Luke 4, Genesis 46.</margin> in Egypt. Fear Jehovah your God: worship Him, cling to Him, and swear by His name. He is your praise, He is your God, who for your sake has done those great and stupendous things which you have seen with your own eyes. Your ancestors went down into Egypt numbering seventy, but now He has increased you to the number of the stars of heaven.

Furthermore, at Taberah, at Massah, and at the Graves of Craving <note>original: "Buſta cupiditatis"; a translation of the Hebrew place name Kibroth-Hattaavah</note> <margin>40</margin> you offended Jehovah. Likewise, when Jehovah sent you from Kadesh-barnea to set out to occupy the land given to you by Him, you resisted the command of Jehovah your God; you neither believed Him nor obeyed His word. <margin>45</margin> Briefly, from the day I first knew you, you have always been rebels against Jehovah. For that reason, I lay prostrate before Jehovah for forty days and as many nights (for He had determined to destroy you), and I supplicated Him with these words: "Lord Jehovah, do not destroy your <margin>50</margin> people and your heritage which you have redeemed by your greatness, and whom you led out of Egypt with a strong hand. Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not look upon the stubbornness, the impiety, or the crime of this people; lest those from whose borders you led us out should keep saying: 'Because Jehovah was not able to lead them into the land which He had promised them, and because He hated them, He led them out so that He might kill them in the desert.' And yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you led out by your great power and your outstretched arm."

<column-break/>

### CHAPTER X.

<margin>The second tablets. Exodus 34.</margin>
Then Jehovah commanded me to cut two stone tablets, similar to the first ones, then, having made a wooden ark, to ascend to Him on the mountain. For He would write on the tablets the same words that had been on the previous ones which I had broken, so that I might replace them in the ark. Therefore, I made an ark of cedar wood <note>original: "cedrinam"; likely referring to acacia or shittim wood used for the Ark</note>, and I cut two stone tablets similar to the earlier ones, and carrying them with me, I ascended the mountain. And He inscribed on the tablets the same things as on the previous ones: namely the Ten Commandments <note>original: "decem dicta", literally 'ten words'</note> which <margin>10</margin> He had spoken to us on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly, and He delivered them to me. Then I departed, and when I descended from the mountain, I placed those tablets in the ark which I had made; and there they remain, just as Jehovah commanded me.

<margin>Numbers 33, Numbers 20.</margin>
Then the Israelites set out from the wells of the Jaakanites <note>Beeroth Bene-Jaakan</note> to Moserah: where Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son entered into the priesthood in his place. From there they set out for Gudgodah, and then to Jotbathah, a land abundant with streams. At that time <margin>20</margin> <margin>The duty of the Levites.</margin> Jehovah set apart the Levite tribe to carry the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, to attend upon Jehovah, to minister to Him, and to celebrate His name, as is done today. And for that reason, the Levites have no share or inheritance with their kinsmen, because Jehovah your God is their inheritance, just as He promised them. I therefore stayed on the mountain as long as before, namely forty days and as many nights: and Jehovah heard me then also, so that He ceased wanting to destroy you, and He commanded me to <margin>30</margin> go before you on this journey, as you enter into the possession of the land which He himself swore to your ancestors He would give to you. Now Israelites, what does Jehovah your God require of you, except that you fear Jehovah your God, that you walk entirely in His ways, that you love Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul: that you keep His precepts and statutes, which I deliver to you today, so that it may be well with you? Since the heavens belong to Jehovah your God, even the heavens of heavens, and the earth and everything <margin>40</margin> in it, yet He embraced your ancestors with love and chose their descendants above all other nations, as is apparent. Therefore, circumcise <margin>True circumcision.</margin> the foreskin of your heart, and do not harden your neck henceforth. For Jehovah your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords: a great God, mighty and terrible, who shows no <margin>1 Chronicles 19, Job 34, Romans 2, Galatians 2, Matthew 4, Luke 4, Genesis 46.</margin> partiality nor accepts bribes, and who renders justice to orphans and widows: and loving the strangers, He gives them food and clothing. Therefore, love the strangers, for you were strangers in Egypt. Fear Jehovah your God; <margin>50</margin> worship Him; cling to Him; swear by His name. He is your praise, He is your God, who for your sake did those great and stupendous things which you saw with your own eyes. Your ancestors went down into Egypt seventy in number; but now He has increased you to the number of the stars of heaven.

<margin>The nature of Canaan.</margin>
For the land which you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you departed, where you sowed your seed and irrigated it with your feet <note>A reference to foot-powered water wheels or the practice of opening and closing irrigation channels using one's foot</note> as if it were a vegetable garden. Instead, this land has mountains and valleys, and it drinks in the water of the celestial rain. It is a land for which Jehovah your God always cares, and His eyes are fixed upon it from the beginning to the end of the year.

<margin>God’s favor accompanies obedience.</margin>
If you will truly obey my commandments, which I teach you today—that is, if you love Jehovah your God and worship Him with all your heart and soul—He says, "I, in turn, will water your land with rain in its proper season, both the early and the late rain <note>The 'early rain' fell in autumn for planting; the 'late rain' in spring for ripening the harvest</note>, so that you may gather your grain, your new wine, and your oil. I will also provide grass in your fields for your cattle, so that you may have an abundance of food." Be careful that your hearts are not deceived, and you do not turn away to serve and worship other gods. For if you do, Jehovah will be angry with you and will shut the heavens so that the rain will not fall; then the earth will not yield its fruit, and you will soon be removed from that good land which Jehovah has given you. Therefore, commit these words of mine to your heart and memory; bind them upon your hands as a sign, and keep them before your eyes as frontlets <note>Ritual items, later known as tefillin or phylacteries, containing scriptural passages</note>. Teach these things to your children, speaking of them when you are staying at home, when you are traveling, when you lie down, and when you rise up. Inscribe them upon the doorposts and gates of your houses, so that you and your descendants may live as long in the land—which Jehovah swore to give to your ancestors—as the heavens remain above the earth. For if you keep all this discipline which I command you to hold, loving Jehovah your God and following all His ways of living and clinging to Him, it will happen that Jehovah will overthrow all those nations that are larger and stronger than you, and you will occupy their territories. Every place where you set your feet shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon,

### CHAPTER XII.

<margin>Idolatry must be rooted out.</margin>

Having gone there, you shall bring your burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, the gifts you have set aside as offerings, your vows, your voluntary gifts, and the firstborn of your cattle, sheep, and goats. There, in the presence of Jehovah your God, you shall feast and rejoice in all the works of your hands and those of your families, for you have been blessed by Jehovah your God. Do not do as we are doing here today, where everyone does whatever he pleases. For you have not yet reached the place of rest and the inheritance which Jehovah your God is going to give you.

...and whatever I command you, see that you do it. Slaughter animals according to your own judgment, and eat the meat in abundance, just as Jehovah <note>original: "Ioua"; a Latinized form of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton</note> your God has bestowed upon each of you, wherever you may live. Whether a person is ritually unclean or clean, they may eat of it, just as one eats the gazelle or the deer. However, you must not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground like water. You are not permitted to eat the tithes of your grain, wine, or oil, nor the firstborn of your larger or smaller livestock, nor any of your vows, voluntary gifts, or set-aside offerings at home. Instead, you shall offer these before Jehovah your God in the place chosen by Him, together with your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites living among you; and you shall rejoice before Him in all the works of your hands. Take care, as long as you live within your borders, that you do not forsake the Levites. When Jehovah your God expands your borders as He promised, if you desire to eat meat, you may eat as much as you wish. If the place Jehovah your God chooses to set His name is too far away, you may slaughter from your larger or smaller livestock which Jehovah has given you, just as I have commanded you, and eat it at home as you please. Just as the gazelle or the stag is eaten, let both the unclean and the clean eat of it. Only be sure to abstain from eating blood, for since the blood is the life <note>original: "anima", literally "soul" or "breath of life"</note>, you must not eat the life with the meat. Do not eat it; pour it out on the earth like water. I say again, do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your descendants, if you are obedient to Jehovah. But as for the things you have consecrated or vowed, bring them to the place chosen by Jehovah; offer the meat and the blood of your victims on the altar of Jehovah your God. Once the blood of your sacrifices has been poured upon the altar of Jehovah your God, you may eat the meat. Take care to obey all these words I command you, so that it may be well with you and your children forever, if you do what is approved and pleasing to Jehovah your God. When Jehovah your God cuts off the nations you are going in to dispossess, and you settle in their land, take care that you do not fall into the same trap after they have been destroyed. Do not seek out their gods or ask how those nations worshipped their gods, intending to do the same. Do not act this way toward Jehovah your God. For every abomination that Jehovah hates, they have done for their gods—to the point that they even burn their own children in the fire for their gods. Whatever I command you, see that you do it; do not add to it or take away from it.

### CHAPTER XIII

**I**f a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder, and that sign or wonder which he predicted actually comes to pass, yet he urges you to follow and worship foreign gods that are unknown to you: do not listen to the words of that prophet or the dream of that dreamer. For Jehovah

<column-break/>

your God is testing you, to learn whether you love Him with all your heart and soul. Follow Jehovah your God; fear Him; keep His commandments; listen to His voice; serve Him, and cling to Him. But that prophet or author of the dream shall be put to death, because he preached rebellion against Jehovah your God—who brought you out of Egypt and rescued you from the house of slavery—to lead you away from the path that Jehovah your God commanded you to walk. Therefore, remove the evil from your midst. <margin>How greatly the worship of foreign gods is to be detested.</margin> Even if your own brother, born of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife you embrace, or a friend who is as dear to you as your own soul, secretly entices you to the worship of foreign gods unknown to you and your ancestors—the gods of the nations surrounding you, whether nearby or far away in any part of the earth—do not yield to him or listen to him. Do not spare him, show him no mercy, and do not conceal his crime. Instead, you must kill him; your hand shall be the first against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people. You shall overwhelm him with stones until he dies, because he tried to lead you away from Jehovah your God, who brought you out of the house of Egyptian slavery. When all the Israelites hear of this, they will be afraid to commit such a wicked deed among you again. If you hear it said of one of the towns Jehovah your God has given you to live in, that certain worthless men have arisen from among you and incited their fellow citizens to worship foreign and unknown gods, you must investigate, search, and inquire diligently. If it is found to be true and the crime has certainly been committed among you, put the inhabitants of that town to the sword. Destroy the town and everything in it, even the livestock, with the edge of the sword. Gather all the spoil into the middle of the public square and burn the town and all its plunder completely for Jehovah your God; it shall remain a ruin forever, never to be rebuilt. Let nothing of that cursed thing cling to your hands, so that Jehovah may turn from His fierce anger and show you mercy, increasing your numbers just as He swore to your ancestors—provided you listen to the voice of Jehovah your God, keeping all His commandments which I teach you today, and obeying the judgment of Jehovah your God.

When Jehovah your God has cut off the nations before you whom you are going to dispossess, and you have settled in their land, take care that you do not fall into the same trap after they have been destroyed; do not seek out their gods, asking, "How did these nations worship their gods? For every abomination which Jehovah hates, they have performed for their gods, even to the point of burning their own children in the fire for their gods. Whatever I command you, take care to do it; neither add anything to it nor take anything away.

### CHAPTER XIII.

If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and shows you a sign or a wonder, and that sign or wonder which he predicted actually comes to pass, yet he still urges you to follow and worship foreign gods unknown to you, do not listen to the words of that prophet or the dream of that dreamer. For Jehovah your God is testing you

<column-break/>

<margin>How much one must shrink from foreign worship.</margin>
to learn whether you love Him with all your heart and soul. Follow Jehovah your God; fear Him; keep His commandments; listen to His voice; serve Him, and cling to Him. But that prophet or author of dreams shall be put to death, for he has preached rebellion against Jehovah your God—who led you out of Egypt and rescued you from the house of slavery—to lead you away from the path in which Jehovah your God commanded you to walk. Therefore, remove the evil from your midst. If even your brother, born of the same mother, or your son, or daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or a friend as dear to you as your own soul, secretly urges you to worship foreign gods unknown to you and your ancestors—such as the gods of the nations surrounding you, whether nearby or far away in distant lands—do not yield to him, do not listen to him, do not spare him, do not pity him, and do not conceal him. Instead, put him to death; let your hand be the first to strike him, followed by the hands of all the people. Overwhelm him with stones until he dies, because he tried to lead you away from Jehovah your God, who led you out of the house of Egyptian slavery. When all the Israelites hear of this, they will be afraid to commit such a crime among you again. If you hear that in one of the towns Jehovah your God has given you to live in, certain worthless men have arisen from among you and incited their fellow citizens to worship foreign gods unknown to you, then inquire, search, and investigate diligently. If you find the report to be true and that this crime has certainly been committed among you, you must put the inhabitants of that town to the sword and utterly destroy the town and everything in it, even the livestock. Gather all the plunder into the middle of the public square and burn the town and all its plunder completely for Jehovah your God; it shall remain an eternal ruin <note>original: "rudus"; a pile of debris or rubble</note>, never to be rebuilt. Let nothing of that doomed thing cling to your hands, so that Jehovah may turn from His fierce anger and show you mercy, increasing your numbers as He swore to your ancestors, provided you listen to the voice of Jehovah your God, keeping all His commandments which I teach you today, and obeying the judgment of Jehovah your God.

### CHAPTER XIV.

<margin>Funerals.</margin>
You are the children of Jehovah your God. Do not lacerate your bodies or shave your foreheads for the dead. For you are a people holy to Jehovah your God, and He has chosen you to be His own special people, above all the nations on the face of the earth.

<margin>Which animals it is lawful to eat. Leviticus 11.</margin>
Eat nothing that is detestable. These are the animals you may lawfully eat: the ox, sheep, goat, deer, gazelle, roe deer, wild goat, pygarg <note>likely a white-rumped antelope</note>, oryx, and giraffe <note>original: "camelopardali"; while literally "camel-leopard," in early translations this often referred to various exotic mountain sheep or large ruminants</note>. In short, you may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, is cloven-footed, and chews the cud. However, of those that chew the cud or have a cloven hoof, you must not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rabbit <note>original: "cuniculo"; likely the rock hyrax or similar small mammal</note>. For though they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof; these shall be unclean for you. The pig also, since it has a divided hoof but does not chew the cud...

### CHAPTER XIX.

<margin>Cities of Refuge. Numbers 35. Joshua 20.</margin> When you have driven out the nations whose land Jehovah your God is giving to you, and you have settled in their towns and houses, you shall set aside three towns in the midst of your land which Jehovah your God has given you to occupy. You shall prepare the way and divide the territory of your possession, granted to you by Jehovah your God, into three parts, so that every killer may flee there. This shall be the rule for killers who seek their safety by fleeing to that refuge: Whoever kills another through imprudence <note>unintentionally</note>, whom he did not hate before—as if someone went into the woods with another to gather timber, and as his hand swung the axe to cut a tree, the iron slipped from the handle and struck the other, killing him—he shall flee into one of those towns and look to his safety. This is so that the avenger of blood <note>original: "sanguinis uindex"; a kinsman tasked with seeking justice</note> does not pursue the killer in the heat of anger and, if the way is too long, overtake him and take his life, even though his crime was not a capital offense, since he did not hate him beforehand. For this reason, I command you to set aside three towns. If Jehovah your God expands your borders, as He swore to your ancestors, <margin>Genesis 18.</margin> and gives you all the land He promised to give to your ancestors (provided you take care to obey all these teachings which I deliver to you today, that you always love Jehovah your God and walk in His ways), then you shall add three more towns to these three. This is so that innocent blood is not shed in this land which Jehovah your God has given you as a possession, lest you incur the guilt of bloodshed. ### CHAPTER XXV.

If there is a dispute between men, they shall go to court, and the judges shall judge them, acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty. If the <unclear>guilty person</unclear> deserves a flogging <note>original: "fustuarium"; a Roman-style punishment of beating with rods or sticks</note>, the judge shall have him lie down and be beaten in his presence with the number of lashes his crime deserves. He may strike him forty times, but no more; if he adds more to this beating, your brother would be degraded in your presence. Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain. If brothers live together and one of them dies without children, the wife of the deceased shall not marry a stranger. The brother-in-law <note>original: "Leuir"; referring to the custom of Levirate marriage</note> shall go to her and take her as his wife by the right of a brother-in-law. The firstborn son she bears shall succeed to the name of the dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out from Israel. But if the man does not wish to take his sister-in-law <note>original: "glotem"</note>, the sister-in-law shall go to the elders at the gate and declare: "My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel; that is, he is unwilling to perform the duty of a brother-in-law to me." Then the elders of his city shall call him; if he stands his ground and says, "I do not wish to take her," then the sister-in-law shall approach him in the presence of the elders, pull the shoe off his foot, and spit in his face, saying: "This is what is done to the man who does not build up his brother's house." And his name among the Israelites shall be: "The house of the unsandaled one" <note>original: "discalceati"</note>. If men are fighting together and the wife of one intervenes to rescue her husband from the one striking him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his private parts, you shall cut off her hand without any mercy. Do not have different weights in your bag, some heavy and some light. Do not have different measures in your house, some large and some small; you must have accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land that Jehovah your God is giving you. For anyone who does these things, anyone who acts dishonestly, is detestable to Jehovah your God. Remember what the Amalekites did to you on the way after you came out of Egypt, how they met you on the road and, having no fear of God, attacked all the stragglers at your rear when you were weary and exhausted. Therefore, when Jehovah your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land he is giving you to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven; do not forget this.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

When you have entered the land that Jehovah your God is giving you as an inheritance and have taken possession of it and settled in it, take some of the firstfruits of all that you produce from the soil which Jehovah your God gives you and put them in a basket. Go to the place Jehovah will choose as a dwelling for his Name and say to the priest in office at that time: "I declare

<column-break/>

today to Jehovah your God that I have come into the land which Jehovah swore to our ancestors to give us." Then the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down in front of the altar of Jehovah your God, and you shall speak as follows before Jehovah your God: "Our ancestors descended into Egypt while the Syrians were oppressing them <note>This refers to the Aramean/Syrian heritage of Jacob and the patriarchs</note>; they arrived there few in number as foreigners, but there they grew into a great, powerful, and numerous nation. Then, when the Egyptians treated us harshly and imposed hard labor upon us, we cried out to Jehovah, the God of our ancestors. He heard our voice and saw our misery, toil, and oppression; he brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror and with signs and wonders. He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey. Therefore, I now bring the firstfruits of the soil that Jehovah has given me." Then you shall set them before Jehovah your God and bow down before him, and you shall rejoice in all the good things that he has given to you and your household, together with the Levites and the foreigners among you. When you have finished setting aside a tenth of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, give it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied. ### CHAPTER XXXII.

<margin>The Song of Moses.</margin>
Give ear, O heavens, while I speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth. May my doctrine drop like the rain and my speech flow like the dew—like showers upon the stalks and like fine rain upon the grass. For I will proclaim the name of Jehovah: ascribe greatness to our God! His works are perfect, and all his ways are just; he is a faithful God, without iniquity, just and upright. From him, those who have degenerated by their own fault—I will not call them his sons, but a lost and ruined nation. Is this how you repay Jehovah, you foolish and ignorant people? Is he not your father who acquired you? Is he not your maker and author? Remember the ancient times, consider the years of all generations; ask your father and he will tell you, or your elders and they will narrate it to you: how the Supreme Jehovah, when he divided the possessions among the nations and separated the human race, assigned the boundaries to other nations according to the number of the Israelites. For Jehovah’s portion is his people; the lot of his inheritance is the descendants of Jacob. He found them in a desert, in an inaccessible, wild, and vast land; he led them about, he taught them, and he guarded them as the apple of his eye—just as an eagle stirring up its nest hovers over its young, spreading its wings to catch them and carrying them on its feathers. Jehovah alone, with no foreign god, led them, and <margin>a. The most excellent of lands.</margin> brought them up to the <sup>a</sup> high places of the earth, where they might eat the produce of the fields. They despised the power of their salvation and provoked him with foreign things; they incensed him with crimes, sacrificing to demons and not to God—to gods they did not know, new gods newly arrived, whom your ancestors did not fear. You were unmindful of the God who fathered you and forgot the God who created you. ### CHAPTER XXXIII.

<margin>The final words of Moses.</margin>
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the Israelites before his death. He said: "Jehovah came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran. He came with holy myriads, having a fiery law for them at his right hand. Truly he loves the people; all his holy ones are in your hand. They sit down at your feet, receiving your words. Moses gave us a law, a possession for the assembly of Jacob. He was king in Jeshurun <note>original: "inter probos"; literally "among the upright," a translation of the poetic name for Israel, Jeshurun.</note> when the heads of the people were gathered together with the tribes of Israel. Let Reuben live and not die, though his men be few." And this he said of Judah: "Hear, O Jehovah, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his
<margin>Deuteronomy 33</margin>
people; let his hands be sufficient for him, and be a help against his enemies." Of Levi he said: "Your Thummim and your Urim <note>original: "integritas, & claritas"; meaning "perfection and light," the traditional translation of these oracular objects used by the High Priest.</note> belong to your godly man, whom you tested at Massah and with whom you contended at the waters of strife; who said of his father and mother, 'I do not know them,' and did not acknowledge his brothers or recognize his children. For they observed your word and kept your covenant. They shall teach Jacob your judgments and Israel your law; they shall put incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar. Bless, O Jehovah, his substance, and accept the work of his hands; strike the loins of those who rise against him and those who hate him, so that they do not rise again." Of Benjamin he said: "The beloved of Jehovah shall dwell in safety by him; he shields him all the day long and dwells between his shoulders." Of Joseph he said: "Blessed by Jehovah be his land, with the bounty of heaven, with the dew,
<margin>from the ground</margin>
and from the deep that lies beneath; with the bounty of the fruits of the sun and the bounty of the yield of the months; with the finest
<margin>Exodus 3</margin>
of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills; with the bounty of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of him who dwelt in the bush. Let these come upon the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who was prince among his brothers. His majesty is like a firstborn bull, and his horns are like the horns of a unicorn <note>original: "monocerotijs"; the Latin term for a single-horned creature, often used in older translations for the Hebrew 're'em'.</note>; with them he shall gore the nations to the ends of the earth. Such are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh." Then of Zebulun he said: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents. DEUTERONOMY. JOSHUA

## CHAPTER XXXIV.

Then Moses ascended from the plains of Moab unto Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho; and Jehovah showed him all of Gilead <note>original: "Gaditidem"; though referring to the land of Gad, it is standardly translated as the region of Gilead in this context.</note> as far as Dan, and all of Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, <margin>30</margin> even unto the Western Sea; likewise the south, and the plain of Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Zoar <note>original: "Siorim".</note>. And Jehovah said, "This is the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying I would give it to their descendants. I have allowed you to see it with your own eyes, but you shall not cross over into it." And so Moses, the servant of Jehovah, died there in the land of the Moabites, according to the word <note>literally "before the face/mouth"</note> of Jehovah, who buried him in a certain valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor; and no man to this day <margin>40</margin> has known the location of his grave. Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not dim, nor had he lost his natural vigor. The Israelites mourned for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days. When the period of mourning for Moses was finished, Joshua the son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom (for Moses had laid his hands upon him), and the Israelites obeyed him, doing as Jehovah had commanded Moses. There has not arisen since then any prophet in Israel equal to Moses, whom Jehovah knew so familiarly <note>original: "tam familiariter noto"; a reference to Moses speaking with God "face to face."</note>, with all the signs and miracles <margin>50</margin> for which he was appointed and sent by Jehovah into Egypt: and with all that great power and the many great wonders which he performed in the sight of all the Israelites.

## CHAPTER I.

<margin>God gives commands to Joshua.</margin>
<image-desc>A decorative drop cap letter 'P' featuring a landscape scene with figures.</image-desc>After Moses the servant of Jehovah had died, Jehovah spoke to Moses' assistant, Joshua the son of Nun, in this manner: "Since my servant Moses is dead, come now, cross over this Jordan, you and all this Israelite people, into the land which I give to them. Every place where the soles of your feet shall tread, I give to you, just as I <margin>Deut. 11.</margin> promised to Moses. From the wilderness and that Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates (which is all the land of the Hittites), and to the Great Sea where the sun sets, your boundaries shall extend. No one shall stand against you as long as you live: and just as I was present with Moses, so I will be with you; I will never leave you nor forsake you. <margin>Heb. 13.</margin> Gather your strength and be firm, for you shall distribute as an inheritance to this people the land which I swore to their ancestors I would give to them. Only be strong and undaunted, and take care to obey all the law which my servant Moses brought to you; do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may act wisely wherever you go. Keep the book of this law always in your mouth, and meditate upon it day and night, so that you may be careful to carry out everything written in it. For in this way your affairs will result in prosperity and be conducted with wisdom. I command you to be of a firm and constant mind, free from all terror and dread, because Jehovah your God is with you everywhere." <margin>Joshua warns the magistrates to prepare to cross the Jordan.</margin> Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people to go through the camp and instruct the people to prepare provisions for themselves. For after three days they were to cross the Jordan and enter into possession of the land given to them by Jehovah their God. <margin>Num. 32.</margin> Then he spoke to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, saying: "Remember what Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded you—namely, that since Jehovah has given you rest and this land, you yourselves (leaving your wives and little ones in the land given to you by Moses on this side of the Jordan) shall cross over armed ahead of your kinsmen and bring them aid, as many of you as are fit for military service, until they also, like you, have obtained rest from Jehovah and have secured possession of the land given to them by Jehovah their God; so that you may then return to your own land and possess what was granted to you by Moses the servant of Jehovah on the eastern side of the Jordan." Then they answered Joshua, saying that they would do whatever he commanded and go wherever he sent them: they would obey him completely, just as they had obeyed Moses, provided that Jehovah his God was with him as He had been with Moses. Anyone who rejected his authority and did not execute all his commands would be put to death; only let him be strong and vigorous.

JOSHUA.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>
Joshua sends spies into Canaan.

<margin>
Rahab. James 2. Heb. 11. <note>The margin references New Testament passages that praise Rahab's faith and actions.</note>

Then Joshua the son of Nun sent from Shittim <note>original: "Setimo"; the last campsite of the Israelites before crossing the Jordan.</note> two men as secret spies, whom he commanded to go and explore the region in general, and Jericho in particular. When they had arrived there, they turned into the house of a certain woman who was a harlot, named Rahab, to lodge there. However, when it was reported to the King of Jericho that men from the Israelites had come there that night to explore the region, he sent word to Rahab, ordering her to produce the men who had come to her house, for they had come to spy on the whole land. But the woman, having hidden both of them, replied that the men had indeed come to her, but she did not know where they were from; and when it grew dark and the gate was to be closed, they had departed. She claimed she did not know where they went, but if they were pursued quickly, they might be overtaken. However, she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under stalks of flax <note>original: "lini fafciculis"</note> which she had laid out on the roof. Therefore, the king's men pursued them toward the fords of the Jordan, and once the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut. But before the spies had lain down to sleep, she went up to them on the roof and spoke to them in this manner: "I know that Jehovah <note>original: "Ioua"; a Latinization of the Tetragrammaton.</note> has given you this land, and that such great terror of you has fallen upon us that all the inhabitants have lost heart. For we have heard how Jehovah dried up the waters of the Red Sea for you when you departed from Egypt, and how you treated the two kings of the Amorites across the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed. Hearing these things has so weakened our hearts with fear that no one has the spirit to stand against you, for your God, Jehovah, is God in heaven above and on the earth below. Therefore, swear to me by Jehovah that since I have shown you this kindness, you will also show equal favor to my father’s house; and give me a certain sign by which you will preserve my parents, brothers, sisters, and all they have, and defend our lives from death." To which they replied: "We offer our lives unto death for you (provided you do not report our business), and we will faithfully return this favor to you when Jehovah has given us the land." Then she let them down by a rope through a window (for her house was joined to the city walls, as it was built upon them) and warned them to hasten to the mountain so that the pursuers would not find them, and to hide there for three days until the pursuers returned, after which they could go their way. But the men said to her: "We shall be free from this oath by which you have bound us unless you tie this scarlet cord <note>original: "laqueū coccineū"; often symbolized as a precursor to the blood of Christ in early Christian interpretation.</note> to the window through which you let us down, and gather your parents, brothers, and your entire father’s family into the house with you. Anyone who goes outside the doors of your house does so at his own risk, and we shall be blameless. But if anyone touches anyone who is inside with you, we shall pay for it. However, if you make this matter public, we shall be free from the oath by which you have bound us." Then she accepted the condition, sent them away, and tied the purple cord to the window. They hastened into the mountain and remained there for three days, until those who were pursuing

<column-break/>

had returned, having searched the entire way without finding them. Then both men turned back and descended from the mountain, and having crossed the river, they came to Joshua the son of Nun. <margin>The spies return.</margin> They explained to him everything that had happened to them, and showed that the whole region was being subjected by Jehovah to their power, for all the inhabitants were struck down by fear of them.

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>
The Israelites approach the Jordan.

Therefore, the next day when Joshua arose, he moved the camp from Shittim and came to the Jordan with all the Israelites, and they stayed there overnight before crossing. After three days had passed, the officials went through the camp and instructed the people that when they saw the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah their God being carried by the Levite priests, they should move from their place and follow it. However, they were to keep a distance of about two thousand cubits <note>approximately 3,000 feet or 900 meters.</note> between themselves and the Ark, and not come any closer, so they might see the way they were to go, for they had not traveled that way before. Then Joshua told the people to sanctify themselves, because the next day Jehovah would do wonders among them. Next, he commanded the priests to take up the Ark of the Covenant and go before the people. So they, carrying the Ark, went ahead of the people. And Jehovah said to Joshua: "This day I will begin to make you great in the eyes of the Israelites, so they may understand that just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. Command the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant that when they reach the edge of the Jordan’s water, they shall stand still in the Jordan itself." And Joshua spoke to the Israelites: "Come forward and hear the words of Jehovah your God. By this you shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will drive out from before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites. Behold, the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord of all the earth is about to cross the Jordan before you. Therefore, choose twelve men from the tribes of the Israelites, one from each tribe. For as soon as the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah, the Lord of all the earth, set their footprints in the water of the Jordan, the flow of the Jordan river shall be divided; the water flowing down from above shall stand in a single heap." Accordingly, when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, <margin>The Jordan is crossed on dry feet. Ps. 114. Acts 7. Eccl. 24.</margin> with the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant before them, as soon as those carrying the Ark reached the Jordan and their feet were dipped in the edge of the water (now the Jordan usually overflows its banks throughout the time of harvest), the water flowing down from above stopped and rose up in a heap very far off, from the town of Adam which is situated near Zarethan <note>original: "Sarthanis"</note>. The water below it was cut off and flowed into the Salt Sea <note>original: "falfum planiciei lacum"; the Dead Sea.</note> until it was exhausted. The people then crossed over opposite Jericho. The priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all the Israelites crossed over on dry land until the entire nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
