whatever words I say to you, take them into your heart and hear them with your ears. Go to your exiled countrymen and speak to them; say to them: "Thus says the Lord Jehovah," <note>original: "Ioua," a Latinization of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton YHWH</note> whether they listen or refuse. Then I was lifted up by the spirit, and I heard behind me the sound of a great movement: The glory of the Lord is to be proclaimed from his place! I also heard the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching <note>original: "mutuo deosculantium," literally "kissing each other"</note> one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a great rumbling. So, lifted up and taken away by the spirit, I went away embittered and glowing with heat in my soul, with the hand of the Lord acting powerfully upon me. I went to the exiles at Tel-Abib <note>original: "Thelabib"</note> who lived by the river Chebar <note>original: "Chobar"</note>; I stayed where they were staying for seven days, mourning among them. After seven days had passed, the Lord spoke to me as follows: "Son of man, I have appointed you as a watchman <term>watchman: a "speculator" in Latin, referring to a sentry who stands on a wall to warn a city of approaching danger</term> for the descendants of Israel. When you hear words from my mouth, you must warn them on my behalf. When I have threatened a wicked man with death, if you do not warn that wicked man with words, for the sake of turning him from his wicked way so that he may live, that wicked man will indeed die by his own fault, but I will demand the penalty for his blood from you. But if you have warned the wicked man, and he does not turn from his wickedness or his wicked ways, he will indeed die by his own fault, but you will have delivered yourself. Likewise, when a good man turns from his virtue to act wickedly, and I place some misfortune before him from which he might die, because you did not warn him, he will indeed die in his sin—no account will be taken of his past righteous deeds—but I will avenge his blood upon you. However, if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he shall live because he was warned, and you will have delivered yourself." Then, the Lord’s hand acting upon me there, he spoke to me: "Rise up, go out into the plain, and there I will speak with you." So I rose and went out into the plain, where I found the glory of the Lord standing, just like the glory I had seen at the river Chebar, and I fell on my face. But the spirit entered into me, set me on my feet, and spoke with me: "Go," it said, "shut yourself inside your house. And for you, son of man, cords <note>original: "lora," leather straps or thongs</note> will be applied to bind you, so that you cannot go out among the common people. I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you become mute and cannot act as a corrector for them, since they are a rebellious race. But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth so that you may say to them: 'Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Let him who hears, hear; let him who refuses, omit,' for they are a rebellious race."

### CHAPTER IV.

<margin>The siege of Jerusalem on a brick.</margin>
But you, son of man, take a brick <note>original: "laterem," a clay tile or tablet</note> and place it before you. Inscribe upon it the city of Jerusalem. Set a siege against it: build a wall, raise a mound, set up camps, and arrange battering rams all around it. Then take an iron griddle <note>original: "fartaginem ferream"</note> and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it, and let it be besieged; you are to lay siege to it. This shall be a sign <note>original: "prodigiosum," a wonder or portent</note> for the house of the Israelites. Then, lie down on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of the Israelites upon it; you shall bear that guilt for as many days as you lie on it. I assign to you the years of their guilt according to the number of days: three hundred and ninety days, during which you shall bear the guilt of the house of Israel. When these are completed, you shall lie again on your right side and bear the guilt of the house of Judah for forty days. I have given you each day for a year. <column-break/> You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem and prophesy against it with an outstretched arm. And behold, I will apply cords to you so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege. Now take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and vetch <note>original: "viciam," a type of legume often used for animal fodder</note>; put them into a single vessel and make bread for yourself from them. You shall eat this bread for the number of days you lie on your side: three hundred and ninety days. You shall eat it by weight: twenty shekels <note>original: "siclorum"</note> each day at set hours. You shall also drink water by measure: a sixth part of a hin, drinking it at certain hours. You shall eat it as barley cakes, preparing it in their sight using fuel of human excrement. "Thus," said the Lord, "shall the Israelites eat their unclean bread among the nations where I will drive them." But I said, "Ah, Lord Jehovah! Look, I have never been polluted; I have never eaten anything that died of itself or was torn by beasts since my childhood, nor has any unclean meat entered my mouth." And he said, "See, I will give you cow dung instead of human excrement, upon which you may prepare your bread." Furthermore, he said to me: "Son of man, I am going to break the staff of bread <note>original: "panis adminiculum," the support of bread</note> in Jerusalem, so that they will eat bread by weight with anxiety and drink water by measure with horror. Lacking bread and water, they will look at one another in dismay and waste away because of their guilt."

### CHAPTER V.

<margin>Calamity signified by shaved hair.</margin>
And you, son of man, take a sharp knife or a barber’s razor. Having taken it, shave your head and your beard. Then take scales to divide the hair: burn a third part with fire in the middle of the city when the days of the siege are completed; take another third and strike it with a knife on every side; and scatter the final third into the wind, for I will pursue them with a drawn sword. From these, you shall take a few in number and bind them in the folds of your robes. And from those you shall take more and throw them into the middle of the fire to burn them; from there, a fire will go out into the whole house of Israel. Thus says the Lord Jehovah: This is Jerusalem, which I placed in the center of the nations, surrounded by other lands. She has changed my judgments into wickedness more than the foreign nations, and my decrees more than the lands that border her; for she has rejected my judgments and has not followed my decrees. Therefore, thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because you are more turbulent than the nations around you, and have not followed my statutes or carried out my judgments, and have not even imitated the customs of the surrounding nations <note>original margin: "a. Again, the word of Jehovah came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them with these words: O mountains of Israel, hear the words of the Lord Jehovah. Thus says the Lord Jehovah to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you and I will destroy your high places. I will ensure your altars are laid waste, your sun-images <note>original: "signa," likely referring to pillars or statues dedicated to sun worship</note> are shattered, and I will cast down your slain men before your filthy idols <note>original: "stercoreis diuis," literally "dung-gods," a derogatory term used by the prophets for idols</note>. I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their dung-idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars. Wherever you live, the cities shall be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars may be ruined, your filthy idols broken and abolished, your sun-images cut down, and your works wiped out. When the slain lie among you, you shall know that I am Jehovah. Yet I will leave a remnant of those who escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the lands. Those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they were captives, because I was crushed by their unfaithful minds which departed from me, and by their eyes which went whoring after their filthy idols. They will loathe themselves for the evils they committed in all their abominations. They shall know that I am Jehovah and that I did not threaten to bring this evil upon them without cause. Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Strike your hands together and stamp your foot, and say: "Alas!" over all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, for they shall fall by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence. He who is far off shall die of pestilence; he who is near shall fall by the sword; and he who remains and is besieged shall die by famine. Thus will I spend my wrath upon them. Then you shall know that I am Jehovah, when their slain lie mixed among their filthy idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every leafy tree, and under every thick oak—places where they offered sweet incense to all their filthy idols. I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah <note>original: "Deblatha"</note>, throughout all their dwellings. Then they shall know that I am Jehovah.

### CHAPTER XII.

Then the word of Jehovah came to me, saying: "Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, who have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear; for they are a rebellious house. Therefore, son of man, prepare for yourself baggage for exile and go into exile by day in their sight; go from your place to another place while they watch, if perhaps they will see that they are a rebellious house. You shall bring out your belongings, as baggage for exile, by day in their sight; and you shall go out in the evening in their sight, as those who go into exile. Dig through the wall while they watch, and carry your things out through it. In their sight you shall carry them on your shoulders in the dark; you shall cover your face so that you do not see the ground, for I have made you a sign to the house of Israel." So I did as I was commanded: I brought out my belongings like baggage for exile by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my own hand. I brought them out in the dark, carrying them on my shoulders while they watched. In the morning, Jehovah spoke to me again: "Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, asked you, 'What are you doing?' Say to them: Thus says the Lord Jehovah: This sad oracle <note>original: "triste fatum," literally "sad fate" or "grim destiny"</note> concerns the prince in Jerusalem and the entire house of Israel who are there. Say: I am a sign for you; as I have done, so shall it be done to them: they shall go into exile as captives. The prince who is among them shall carry his baggage on his shoulder in the dark and go out; he shall dig through the wall to go out through it <margin>See below, 17:31</margin>, and he shall cover his face so that he may not see the ground with his eyes. I will spread my net over him, and he shall be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there. I will scatter to every wind all his attendants who are around him and all his troops, and I will pursue them with a drawn sword. They shall know that I am Jehovah when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the lands. But I will spare a few of them from the sword, famine, and pestilence, so that they may confess all their abominations among the nations where they go, and it may be known that I am Jehovah." Jehovah also spoke to me with these words: "Son of man, eat your bread with trembling and drink your water with quaking and anxiety. Speak to the inhabitants of the land: Thus says the Lord Jehovah concerning those who dwell in Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water with despair, so that the land may be stripped of everything in it because of the lawlessness of all who dwell there."

### CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>Against false prophets.</margin>
Likewise, Jehovah spoke with me in this way: Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy out of their own inventions: Hear the words of Jehovah. Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit when they have seen nothing. Your prophets, O Israel, are like foxes in the desert. You have not gone up into the breaches, nor built a wall for the house of Israel to stand in battle <margin>Below in chapter 14.</margin> <margin>a. They are deceptive; the prophets do not fight for the Israelites, nor do they turn away God's anger.</margin> on the day of Jehovah. ### CHAPTER XV.

Likewise, Jehovah spoke with me in these words: Son of man, what can be made of the wood of the vine, among all the branched trees that are in the forest? Shall wood be taken from it to be used for any work? Or can a peg be taken from it upon which any utensil might be hung? What if it is cast into the fire to be consumed, and the fire has consumed both its ends, and the middle is scorched; will it then be fit for any work? Even when it was whole, it was not used for any work, much less after it has been consumed by fire and scorched; can any work be made from it? Therefore, thus says the Lord Jehovah: As the wood of the vine is among the trees of the forest, which one might cast into the fire to be burned, so will I give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And I will set my face against them; they shall go out from one fire, yet fire shall consume them; and you shall know that I am Jehovah, when I set my face against them and make their land a wasteland, because they have committed a crime against me, says the Lord Jehovah.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

Again, Jehovah spoke with me in these words: What is the meaning of this proverb that you repeat throughout the land of Israel, saying: "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge" <margin>c</margin>? "As I live," says the Lord Jehovah, "you shall no longer have any use for this proverb among the Israelites. Since all souls are mine—the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is mine—the soul that has sinned, that one shall die."

But if a man is righteous, and does what is just and right: if he has not feasted upon the mountains <note>Referring to ritual meals at pagan shrines.</note>, or lifted his eyes to the dungy idols <note>original: "sterccoreos diuos," a common biblical epithet for false gods, suggesting they are as worthless as refuse.</note> of the house of Israel; if he has not defiled his neighbor's wife, nor approached a woman during her uncleanness; if he has harmed no one, has returned the pledge to his debtor, has committed no robbery, has shared his food with the hungry and covered the naked with clothing; if he has not lent at interest or taken usury; if he has kept his hand from iniquity and rendered true judgment in disputes between men; if he has walked according to my decrees and kept my laws by acting truthfully—that man is righteous; he shall surely live, says the Lord Jehovah.

But if he fathers a son who is a destroyer, a man of blood, who commits any of these things and does not carry out these duties—who instead feasts on the mountains, defiles his neighbor's wife, harms the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return a pledge, lifts his eyes to dungy idols, commits an abomination, or lends at 

<column-break/>

interest and takes usury—shall he live? He shall not live. He who has committed all these abominations shall surely pay the penalty with death.

Again, if this man fathers a son who, having observed all the sins committed by his father, is afraid and does not imitate them: who does not feast on the mountains, nor lifts his eyes to the filth of the house of Israel, nor defiles his neighbor's wife; who harms no one, does not withhold a pledge, does not commit robbery, gives his food to the hungry, covers the naked with clothing, withholds his hand from hurting the poor, and takes no interest or usury; who executes my laws and follows my statutes—he shall not die for his father’s guilt, but shall live. As for his father, if he defrauded, or robbed a brother, or did what was not right among his people, he has died for his own guilt.

Yet you ask, "Why does the son not pay for the father's guilt?" <margin>Deuteronomy 24; 2 Kings 14; 2 Chronicles 25.</margin> Because the son did what was right and just, and kept all my decrees and observed them, he is worthy to live. The soul that has sinned, it shall die: the son shall not pay for the father's guilt, nor the father for the son's. The righteous man shall bear his own righteousness, and the wicked man his own wickedness.

But if a wicked man turns away from all the sins he has committed, and keeps all my delights and does what is right and just, he shall live; he shall not die. None of the sins he committed shall be remembered against him; he shall live because of the righteousness he has practiced. "Do I desire the death of the wicked?" <margin>Psalm 29; Below, chapter 33.</margin> says the Lord Jehovah, "and not rather that he should turn from his ways and live?"

Conversely, if a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and acts wickedly, imitating all the abominations that the wicked commit, shall he live? None of the virtues he practiced shall be remembered; he shall die because of the crime and the sin he has committed.

And yet you say that my <margin>a. That the Lord is just. Below, chapter 33.</margin> reasoning is inconsistent? Hear now, O house of Israel: Is it my reasoning that is inconsistent, or rather your own? When a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and acts wickedly, and dies for it, he dies because of the guilt he himself committed. Again, when a wicked man turns away from the wickedness he practiced and does what is right and just, he preserves his life; because he considered and turned away from all the sins he practiced, he ought to live and not die.

And yet the house of Israel says the Lord's reasoning is inconsistent? Is it my reasoning, and not rather yours, O house of Israel, that is inconsistent? Therefore, I will judge each of you according to his merits, O house of Israel, says the Lord Jehovah. <margin>Matthew 5.</margin> Return, and turn yourselves from all your sins, and your guilt shall not be your ruin. Cast away from you all the sins you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit, so that you do not die, O house of Israel. "For I do not desire the death of one who is dying," <margin>Below, chapter 33.</margin> says the Lord Jehovah; "turn yourselves, and live!"

### CHAPTER XIX.

The word of Jehovah came to me again, saying: "And you, son of man, will you judge, will you judge the bloody city? In you, fathers and mothers are treated with contempt; in your midst, the foreigner is wronged; in you, the orphan and the widow are oppressed. You have despised my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths. In you are slanderers intent on shedding <margin>Jeremiah 5, etc. Sons had relations with stepmothers, Exodus 22.</margin> blood; in you, they eat at the mountain shrines; in your midst, they commit lewdness. In you, a father’s nakedness is uncovered; in you, they force women who are unclean from their periods. In you, one man commits an abomination with another’s wife; another lewdly defiles his daughter-in-law; and another forces his sister, his own father’s daughter. In you, they take bribes to shed blood; you take interest and usury, and have greedily defrauded others by extortion, and have forgotten me, says the Lord Jehovah. Now, behold, I strike my hands together at the dishonest gain you have practiced and the bloodshed in your midst. Will your heart endure, or will your hands be strong, in the days when I deal with you? I, Jehovah, have spoken and I will act. I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the countries, and I will consume your filthiness out of you, so that you will be profaned in yourself in the sight of the nations, and you shall know that I am Jehovah."

And the word of Jehovah came to me, saying: "Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross <note>original: "scoria"; the waste material produced when smelting metal.</note> to me; they are all copper, tin, iron, and lead in the middle of a furnace; they are the dross of silver. Just as silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin are gathered into a furnace to be blown upon with fire and melted, so I will gather you in my anger and in my fury; I will set you there and melt you. I will gather you and blow upon you with the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst of it. As silver is melted in a furnace, so you shall be melted in it; and you shall know that I, Jehovah, have poured out my fury upon you."

### CHAPTER XXV.

<margin>Against the Ammonites.</margin> And Jehovah spoke to me with these words: Son of man, turn your face toward the Ammonites <note>a people living east of the Jordan River, descendants of Lot</note> and prophesy against them, and say to the Ammonites: Hear the words of the Lord Jehovah. Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because you mocked my sanctuary because it was profaned, and the land of Israel because it was devastated, and the house of Judah because they went into exile; therefore, I will hand you over to be occupied by the <margin>a. The Chaldeans (Babylonians).</margin> people of the East, who shall place their encampments in you and set up their dwellings; they shall eat your fruit and drink your milk. I will turn Rabbah <note>the capital city of Ammon</note> into a stable for camels and the borders of the Ammonites into a resting place for sheep, and I will make you know that I am Jehovah. For thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet, rejoicing with all the malice of your soul over the <margin>b. That is, the devastated region.</margin> land of Israel; therefore, I will stretch out my hand against you and give you as plunder to the nations; I will cut you off from the peoples and destroy you wretchedly from the lands; you shall know that I am Jehovah.

<margin>Against the Moabites.</margin> Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because the Moabites and those of Seir keep saying, <margin>c. That they suffer no less evil than others, nor are they dearer to God.</margin> "The house of Judah is like all other nations," therefore, I will lay open the flank of Moab, starting from their frontier cities, the most noble of the region—namely, Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim—to the people of the East, <margin>d. Through which flank he invades the Ammonites.</margin> along with the Ammonites; I will see that their country is occupied so that the Ammonites may no longer be remembered among the nations. I will execute the same judgments on the Moabites, that they may know that I am Jehovah.

<margin>Against the Edomites.</margin> Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because the Edomites acted vengefully against the house of Judah and committed a great crime by taking revenge on them, for this reason (says the Lord Jehovah) I will stretch out my hand against Edom, and having cut off both man and beast from it, I will make it a wasteland from Teman even to Dedan; they shall fall by the sword. I will take such vengeance on the Edomites by the hand of my people Israel (who shall treat the Edomites as my anger and fury require) so that it may be known that this is my vengeance, says the Lord Jehovah.

<margin>Against the Philistines.</margin> Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because the Philistines acted vengefully and with a petulant soul, seeking to destroy with eternal enmity, therefore thus says the Lord Jehovah: I will stretch out my hand against the Philistines, I will cut off the Cherethites <note>a group of Philistines often associated with Crete</note>, and I will destroy the remnant of the seacoast. I will impose such great punishments upon them with angry rebukes that they shall understand I am Jehovah when I have taken vengeance upon them.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

<margin>Against the Tyrians.</margin> In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, a word of this kind came to me from Jehovah: Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, "Aha! she is broken, she who was the <margin>a. Most celebrated and crowded with people.</margin> gate of the nations; she is turned toward me; I shall be filled now that she is laid waste." Therefore, thus says the Lord Jehovah: I am against you, O Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea brings up its waves. They shall destroy the walls of Tyre and throw down her towers; I will scrape her dust from her and make her a bare rock, so that she shall serve as a place for spreading nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord Jehovah. She shall become plunder for the nations, and her daughter-villages on the mainland shall be slain by the sword; and they shall know that I am Jehovah. For thus says the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I will bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, from the north—a king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, and a vast multitude of troops. He shall slay your daughter-villages on the mainland with the sword; he shall set up a siege wall against you, cast up a mound against you, and lift up a buckler against you. He shall direct the shock of his battering rams against your walls and break down your towers with his weapons. The abundance of his horses will be so great that their dust shall cover you; your walls shall shake at the noise of the horsemen, the wagons, and the chariots, when he enters your gates as one enters a city that has been breached. With the hooves of his horses, he shall trample all your streets; he shall slay your people with the sword, and your powerful pillars shall be brought down to the ground. They shall plunder your riches, seize your merchandise, break down your walls, and destroy your pleasant houses; they shall cast your stones, your timber, and your dust into the midst of the water. Thus I will silence the noise of your songs, <margin>Jeremiah 7</margin> and the sound of your harps shall be heard no more. I will make you a bare rock, a place for spreading nets; you shall never be rebuilt, for I, Jehovah, have spoken, says the Lord Jehovah. Thus says the Lord Jehovah to Tyre: Surely at the sound of your fall (when the wounded groan and slaughter is dealt in your midst) the islands shall shake. All the princes of the sea shall descend from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments; they shall clothe themselves with trembling and sit upon the ground; they shall tremble every moment and be astonished at your sudden ruin. Now the ships tremble on the day of your fall; the islands of the sea are troubled by your end." For thus says the Lord Jehovah: When I make you a desolate city, like cities that are not inhabited, when I bring the deep over you and the vast waters cover you, I will bring you down with those

### CHAPTER XXVII.

Then Jehovah spoke to me in this way: You, son of man, take up a lament <note>original: "naeniam"; a funeral dirge or song of mourning</note> for Tyre, and say to Tyre—situated at the entries of the sea, the merchant for the peoples of many islands: Thus says the Lord Jehovah: O Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty." Your borders are in the heart of the sea; those who built you have made your beauty absolute. They fashioned all your planks from the pines of Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you. They made your oars of the oaks of Bashan; they made your benches of Assyrian ivory, brought from the islands of Cyprus. Variegated fine linen from Egypt was your sail; your canopy was provided by the blue and purple brought from the islands of Elishah. You had the men of Sidon and Arvad as rowers; your own most skilled men, O Tyre, were your pilots. The elders and wise men of Gebal <note>Gabalenses; an ancient Phoenician city famous for its stonemasons and shipbuilders</note> were your repairers. You used all the ships of the sea and their sailors to conduct your trade. Persians, Lydians, and Libyans were in your army as your warriors; they hung their shields and helmets upon you, bestowing glory upon you. The men of Arvad and your own soldiers were all around your walls, and the Gammadims were in your towers; they hung their quivers around the circuit of your walls, perfecting your beauty. The merchants of Cilicia <note>The Latin text uses "Cilicum," referring to Cilicia in Asia Minor, where the Hebrew text usually refers to Tarshish</note> dealt in your marketplaces with an abundance of all kinds of wealth: silver, iron, tin, and lead. The Greeks, Iberians, and Moschi were your traders in slaves and vessels of bronze, supplying your merchandise. Those of the house of Togarmah supplied horses, horsemen, and mules to your fairs. The merchants of Rhodes were yours; many islands were the coast of your trade, supplying you with ivory tusks and ebony as payment. The Syrians were your merchants because of the multitude of your works, providing carbuncles, purple, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral, and crystal for your fairs. Judah and the land of Israel were your traders; they supplied you with the finest wheat, balsam, honey, oil, and resin as merchandise. The people of Damascus were your traders because of the multitude of your works and your great wealth, with excellent wine and white wool. Then the Danites and the wandering Greeks displayed at your fairs wrought iron, cassia <note>original: "stacten"; a fragrant resin or oil</note>, and reed, as goods for your use. The people of Dedan traded with you in precious saddle blankets. The Arabs and all the chiefs of Kedar contracted with you for lambs, rams, and goats. The merchants of Sheba and Raamah, trading with you, brought to your fairs every kind of the finest spices, precious stones, and gold. The merchants of Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the Sabeans, Assyrians, and the people of Chilmad were your traders; they dealt with you in the most perfect goods—in blue and embroidered cloths, and in precious chests bound with ropes and

<column-break/>

made of cedar, which were in your markets. The ships of Cilicia were the leaders of your trade; and you, being filled and made most glorious in the heart of the sea, shall be led into the deep by your rowers, only to be broken by the East Wind in the midst of the sea. Your riches, your fairs, your merchandise, your sailors, your pilots, your repairers, your brokers, and all your soldiers who are in you, and your entire crowd that is within you, shall fall into the heart of the sea on the day of your ruin. At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the suburbs shall shake. All the rowers and sailors shall descend from their ships; all the pilots of the sea shall stand upon the land, and they shall cry out bitterly over you with a raised voice. They shall cast dust upon their heads and wallow in ashes; they shall shave their heads for you and clothe themselves in sackcloth. They shall weep for you with bitter grief of soul and mourning. Their sons shall take up a lament for you, mourning you thus: "Who was ever like Tyre, which now lies destroyed in the sea?" When your wares went out from the seas, you satisfied many peoples; with the abundance of your wealth and trade, you enriched the kings of the earth. Now you are broken by the sea in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your company have collapsed within you. All the inhabitants of the islands are appalled at you, and their kings are seized with horror, their faces troubled. The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you are brought to nothing, and you shall be destroyed forever.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

<margin>Against the prince of Tyre</margin>
<margin>a. Against you, who seem to yourself to be endowed with such excellent wisdom.</margin>
Moreover, Jehovah spoke to me, saying: Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre: Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said, "I am a God, I sit in the seat of gods, in the heart of the sea"—even though you are a man and not God, you set your heart as if it were the heart of God. Indeed, you think you are wiser than Daniel; there is no secret so hidden that it escapes you. By your wisdom and your prudence you have gathered wealth; you have gathered gold and silver into your treasury. By your great wisdom in trade you have increased your wealth, and because of this wealth your heart is insolent. Therefore, I say, thus says the Lord Jehovah: Because you set your heart as if it were the heart of God, for this reason I will bring enemies against you, the most ferocious of nations. They shall draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom ^a^ and shall defile your splendor, casting you down into destruction; and so you shall die a violent death in the heart of the sea. Will you still say, "I am God," in the presence of your executioner? But you shall be a man, and not God, in the hand of the one who slays you; you shall die the death of the uncircumcised <note>original: "inhonesta morte"; literally a dishonest or shameful death</note> by the hand of foreigners, for I have spoken, says the Lord Jehovah. Again Jehovah spoke to me, saying: Son of man, take up a lament for the king of Tyre, and say to him, Thus says the Lord Jehovah: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty. You were in Eden, the divine garden; every kind of precious stone was your covering: sardis, topaz, diamond, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, carbuncle, emerald, and gold. The workmanship of your timbrels and flutes was prepared with you on the day you were created. You were the anointed and overshadowing Cherub; I placed you on the holy mountain of God...

You were placed so that you might be as a god, and you walked in the midst of the stones of fire. You were perfect in your ways from the day you were created, until wickedness was found in you. By the abundance of your trade, your heart was filled with iniquity and you sinned; therefore, I will cast you out as a profane thing from the mountain of God, and I will destroy you, O overshadowing Cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire—you whose soul was lifted up because of your beauty. <margin>Against Sidon.</margin>
Likewise, Jehovah spoke to me in these words: Son of man, set your face against Sidon, and prophesy against her, saying: Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will gain glory for myself in your midst. It shall be known that I am Jehovah when I execute judgments in her and manifest my holiness. No longer shall the house of Israel have pricking briars or grieving thorns from all their neighbors who treated them with contempt. They shall know that I am the Lord Jehovah. Thus says the Lord Jehovah: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, I will manifest my holiness in them in the sight of the nations. They shall dwell in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob; and they shall dwell in it securely. They shall build houses and plant vineyards, living in safety when I have executed judgments on all their neighbors who treat them with contempt; and they shall know that I am Jehovah their God.

### CHAPTER XXIX.

<margin>Against the King of Egypt.</margin>
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day, Jehovah spoke these words to me: Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt, speaking in these words: Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, you great sea monster <note>original: "cete ingens"; likely referring to a crocodile, a symbol of the Nile's power and Pharaoh's pride</note> lying in the midst of your rivers, who boasts of the river you possess and says that you made it for yourself.

<margin>a. You take pride in the wealth of the Nile and are so arrogant as if you were a God, existing by your own power and not created by God.</margin>
But I will put hooks in your jaws and make all the fish of your rivers stick to your scales. I will pull you out from the midst of your rivers, with all the fish of your rivers clinging to your scales. I will cast you and all the fish of your rivers into the desert; you shall lie in the open field, neither gathered nor buried. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the air. Then all the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am Jehovah, because they have been a staff of reed <note>A metaphor for an unreliable ally; a reed looks like a sturdy walking stick but snaps under weight</note> to the house of Israel. When they took hold of you by the hand, you splintered and tore their whole shoulder; when they leaned on you, you broke and pierced their sides. Therefore, thus says the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you and cut off both man and beast from you. The land of Egypt shall be desolate and waste; and they shall know that I am Jehovah, because—

<column-break/>

<page-num>384</page-num>
—because you say that the river is yours and that you made it yourself. Therefore, I am against you and your river, and I will reduce the land of Egypt to such a wasteland of solitude—from the tower of Syene <note>Modern-day Aswan, the southern frontier of Egypt</note> even to the borders of Ethiopia—that no human foot nor foot of beast shall pass through it, nor shall it be inhabited for forty years. I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and her cities shall be waste among devastated cities for forty years; and I will scatter the Egyptians themselves among the nations and lands. But thus says the Lord Jehovah: At the end of forty years, I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples where they were scattered. I will bring back the Egyptian captives and return them to the land of Pathros <note>original: "Phariam"; refers to Upper Egypt, the ancestral home of the Egyptians</note>, which is the land of their birth. There they shall be a lowly kingdom—the lowliest of kingdoms—never again exalting itself above the nations. I will diminish them so they shall no longer rule over the nations. Nor shall they ever again be a source of confidence for the house of Israel, which only brings their iniquity to mind when they turn to them for help. Then they shall know that I am the Lord Jehovah.

<margin>b. They depend on them.</margin>
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, the word of Jehovah came to me in these words: Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to labor so hard against Tyre that every head was made bald and every shoulder was rubbed bare; yet neither he nor his army had any reward from Tyre for the labor he performed against it. Therefore, thus says the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He shall carry off her wealth, seize her spoil, and plunder her goods; this shall be the wages for his army.

<margin>c. Tyre.</margin>
For the service he performed against <margin>c</margin> her <note>referring to Tyre</note>, I give them the land of Egypt because they worked for me, says the Lord Jehovah.

<margin>d. Addressing the prophet.</margin>
In that day, I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and <margin>d</margin> I will give you the opening of the mouth in their midst; and they shall know that I am Jehovah.

### CHAPTER XXX.

Then Jehovah spoke to me, saying: Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord Jehovah: Wail, "Alas for the day!" For the day is near, even the day of Jehovah is near—a cloudy day; it shall be the <margin>a</margin> time of the nations.

<margin>a. Fatal punishment.</margin>
The sword shall come upon Egypt, and there shall be great anguish in Ethiopia when the slain fall in Egypt, her wealth is taken away, and her foundations are torn down. The Ethiopians, Libyans, Lydians, all the mixed people, and the men of the <margin>b</margin> allied region <note>original: "foederatae regionis"; likely referring to the Jews or allies living in Egypt</note> shall fall with them by the sword, as Jehovah says.

<margin>b. The Israelites.</margin>
Those who uphold Egypt shall fall, and the pride of her power shall come down; from the tower of Syene they shall fall by the sword, says the Lord Jehovah. They shall be desolate among desolate lands, and her cities shall be among desolate cities. They shall know that I am Jehovah when I set a fire in Egypt and all her helpers are destroyed. In that day, messengers shall go out from me in ships to terrify the secure Ethiopians; and great anguish shall come upon them, <margin>c</margin> as in the day of Egypt; for indeed, it is coming, says the Lord Jehovah. You were placed so that you were as a God, and you walked in the midst of the fiery stones. You were perfect in that state from the day you were created, until wickedness was discovered in you. Because of the abundance of your trade, your heart was filled with iniquity, and you sinned; therefore, I will cast you out as profane from the mountain of God and destroy you, O overshadowing Cherub, from the midst of the fiery stones, you who lift up your soul because of your beauty. With the force of fiery ferocity, I declare that on that day there shall be such a great shaking in the land of the Israelites that the $^e$ fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the wild beasts, and everything that crawls on the ground, and all the humans on the face of the earth shall tremble before me. The mountains shall be overturned, the towers shall fall, and every wall shall tumble to the ground. And I will summon swords against him throughout all my mountains, says the Lord Jehovah, so that every man’s sword is against his brother. I will contend against him with pestilence and slaughter; I will rain down overflowing rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur upon him, his troops, and the many peoples accompanying him. Thus I will show my greatness and my holiness, and I will be known in the sight of many nations, and it shall be known that I am Jehovah.

<margin>30</margin> all around the side chambers, so that they were continuous with one another but did not touch the temple wall itself. As the side chambers went higher, they became wider and had a larger circuit, because the gallery of the temple became wider as it went higher; thus the lowest story had an ascent to the highest through the middle ones. And when I looked at the height of the temple all around, the foundations of the side chambers were visible, a full rod <term>decempeda: a ten-foot measuring rod</term> in length, that is, a space of six cubits. The thickness of the wall that was outside the side chambers was five cubits.

Thus the building itself, placed at the front of the courtyard, faced west and was seventy cubits wide, ninety cubits long, surrounded by a wall five cubits thick.

### CHAPTER XLIII.

Then he led me to the gate, the gate that faced toward the east. And behold, the splendor of the God of the Israelites came from the way of the east; the sound of this God was like the sound of many waters, and the earth was illuminated <margin>see chapter 9</margin> by his splendor. The appearance of the vision was like the vision which I had seen when <margin>see chapter 1</margin> I went to destroy the city, and similar to the vision <margin>30</margin> I had seen by the river Chebar. Then the spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and I noticed that the temple was filled with the splendor of Jehovah. I heard one speaking to me from the temple, while a man stood by me, who addressed me thus: "Son of Man <note>original: "Homo G." — likely an abbreviation for the Hebrew 'Ben Adam' used throughout Ezekiel</note>, you see this place of my throne, the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The Israelites shall no longer pollute <margin>40</margin> my holy name—neither they nor their kings—by their harlotry, nor by the corpses of their kings and their high places. While they placed their thresholds next to my threshold, and their doorposts next to my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them, they polluted my holy name by the abominations they committed; therefore, in my anger, I consumed them. Now let them remove their harlotry and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever. You, Son of Man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so that, being ashamed of their sins, they may measure its pattern. And if they are ashamed of all they have done, show them the form of the temple, its arrangement, its exits and entrances—indeed, all its forms, ordinances, descriptions, and laws. Write it before their eyes so they may keep all its forms and ordinances and carry them out. This is the law of the temple: Upon the top of the mountain, its entire territory all around shall be most holy. Indeed, this is the law of the temple. These are the dimensions of the altar, measured in cubits that

### CHAPTER XLIV.

Then he brought me back toward the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faces the east; and it was shut. And Jehovah said to me: "This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it; for Jehovah, the God of the Israelites, has entered by it; therefore it shall remain shut. As for the prince, the prince shall sit in the sanctuary to eat bread before Jehovah; he shall enter by way of the vestibule and go out by the same way." Then he led me toward the north gate, to the front of the temple; and when I saw the house filled with the splendor of Jehovah, I fell prostrate. And Jehovah spoke to me thus: "Son of Man, pay attention, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything I say to you concerning all the ordinances and laws of the temple of Jehovah; and mark well the entrance of the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary. And say to the rebellious house of Israel—

It stood toward the north. And he spoke to me thus: "This chamber, which faces south, is for the priests who keep charge of the temple. But the one facing north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar; these are the Zadokites <note>original: "Sadociani"</note>, who alone among the Levites may approach the Lord <note>original: "Iouam" — a Latin rendering of the Tetragrammaton</note> to minister to him." Then he measured the court: its length and width were each one hundred cubits, forming a square. The altar stood before the temple. He then led me into the vestibule of the temple, and he measured each side of the vestibule as five cubits; the gate was three cubits wide on each side. The length of the vestibule was twenty cubits and the width was ten, and it was reached by ten steps. There was a column on each side next to the side-pillars.

### CHAPTER XLI.

Then he led me into the nave <note>original: "cella" — the central hall of the temple</note>, and he measured the side-pillars on both sides; they were six cubits wide, which was the width of the enclosure. The width of the entrance was ten cubits, and its side walls <note>original: "humeri" — literally "shoulders"</note> were five cubits on each side. He measured the length of the nave as forty cubits and the width as twenty cubits. Then he went into the inner room and measured the side-pillar of the entrance at two cubits; the entrance itself was six cubits, and the width of the entrance <gloss>G.</gloss> and its side walls <gloss>H.</gloss> were seven cubits. He measured the length of the inner sanctuary as twenty cubits and the width as twenty cubits at the front of the nave, and he said to me: "This is the Most Holy Place" <note>original: "sanctius sacrarium"</note>. He measured the wall of the temple as six cubits; and there were side chambers all around the temple, four cubits wide. These side chambers were in three stories, one above the other, thirty in each story. There were ledges all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side chambers, so that they were fastened to them but not embedded into the wall of the temple itself.

The higher the stories were, the wider they became, as the structure narrowed as it went up; because the temple was surrounded by a gallery that widened as it rose. Thus, one could ascend from the lowest story to the highest by way of the middle one. When I looked at the height of the temple all around, the foundations of the side chambers were visible, measuring a full rod <note>original: "decempeda" — a ten-foot measuring rod</note>, which is a space of six cubits. The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits.

The open area between the side chambers of the temple was such that the chambers surrounding the temple were twenty cubits apart all the way around. The doors of the side chambers opened onto the free space, one facing north and another facing south. The free space all around was five cubits wide. The building that faced the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide and ninety cubits long, surrounded by a wall five cubits thick. Thus, he measured the length of the temple as one hundred cubits. Likewise, the length of the courtyard and the building, including its walls, was one hundred cubits; also the width of the front of the temple together with the courtyard on the east side was one hundred cubits. He measured the length of the building facing the courtyard at the back of the temple, including its galleries on both sides, as one hundred cubits. The inner nave, the vestibules of the court, the thresholds, the narrow windows, and the galleries that surrounded the three-

<column-break/>

story chambers of the vestibules, were all paneled with wood from the floor up to the windows (and the windows were covered), from the area above the door to the inner temple and outside, and on all the walls all around, both inside and out. These were decorated with Cherubim and palm trees, so that a palm tree was placed between every two Cherubim. Each Cherub had two faces: a human face looking toward the palm tree on one side, and a lion’s face looking toward the palm tree on the other side. This craftsmanship covered the entire temple all around, with Cherubim and palm trees carved from the floor to the area above the entrance to the wall of the nave. The nave had square doorposts, and the front of the sanctuary had a similar appearance. There was a wooden altar three cubits high and two cubits long; its corners, its length, and its sides were of wood. And he said to me, "This is the table that stands before the Lord" <note>original: "Iouæ" — Jehovah</note>. Both the nave and the sanctuary had double doors, each door having two swinging leaves. On these doors of the nave were carved Cherubim and palm trees, just as they were on the walls. On the outside front of the vestibule was a wooden canopy, and there were narrow windows and palm trees on the side walls of the vestibule, as well as on the side chambers of the temple and the canopies.

### CHAPTER XLII.

Then he led me out into the outer court by the way toward the north, and he brought me to the chambers that were opposite the temple courtyard and opposite the building to the north. The length of the building whose door faced north was one hundred cubits, and the width was fifty cubits. Facing the twenty cubits of the inner court and facing the pavement of the outer court, these chambers were arranged in three stories, with gallery facing gallery.

In front of the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide, leading into the interior, and a path of one cubit; their doors faced north. Now the upper chambers were narrower, for the galleries took more away from them than from the lower and middle stories of the building. For they were in three stories and did not have columns like the columns of the courts; therefore the upper stories were set back from the ground more than the lower and middle ones. The wall that was outside alongside the chambers, toward the outer court and in front of the chambers, was fifty cubits long. For the length of the chambers of the outer court was fifty cubits, while those facing the nave were one hundred cubits. Below these chambers was the entrance from the east, as one enters them from the outer court. In the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, facing the temple courtyard and the building, were chambers with a walkway in front of them, similar in form to the chambers toward the north—of the same length and width, with the same exits, arrangements, and doors. Just like the doors of the chambers toward the south, there was a door at the head of the walkway, the walkway that was in front of the corresponding wall, toward the east as one enters. Then he said to me: "The northern chambers and the southern chambers which are in front of the courtyard are the holy chambers, where the priests who approach the Lord shall eat the most holy things..."

<margin>The Kitchens.</margin> He said to me: This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offerings and the sin offerings, and where they shall bake the grain offerings, so that they do not carry them into the outer court and thereby
<margin>30</margin> sanctify the common people <note>original: "consecrent" — referring to the idea that contact with holy items would make the people "ritually set apart" in a way that might interfere with daily life</note>. Then he led me out into the outer court and led me around to the four corners of the court. In each corner of the court, there was another small court; in the four corners, these were smoking areas <note>original: "fumosa" — likely referring to the smoke from the cooking fires</note>, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; all four corner courts were the same size. Around the inside of these four courts were stone galleries, and beneath the galleries were kitchens built all around. And he said to me: These are the houses of the cooks, where the ministers of the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people.

### DANIEL ▶

#### CHAPTER I.

In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and besieged it. The Lord delivered Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into his hand, along with a portion of the vessels of the temple. He carried them away into the land of

</margin>
Shinar <note>ancient Babylonia</note>, and he placed the vessels in the temple of his god, putting them into the treasury of his god. Then the king commanded Ashpenaz, the master of his eunuchs, to bring in some of the Israelites from the royal and noble families—young men without any physical defect, handsome in appearance, skilled in all wisdom and learning, knowledgeable and discerning, and possessed of enough strength to serve in the king’s palace. They were to be taught the literature and the language of the Chaldeans <note>The elite class of scholars and priests in Babylon</note>. The king assigned them a daily portion of food from the royal provisions and wine from his own drink, so that they might be educated for three years, and at the end of that time, they might enter the king's service. Among these from the tribe of Judah were Daniel, Ananias, Mishael, and Azarias. The master of the eunuchs gave them new names: he called Daniel, Belteshazzar; Ananias, Shadrach; Mishael, Meshach; and Azarias, Abednego. But Daniel resolved in his heart that he would not defile himself with the royal food or the wine, and he requested of the master of the eunuchs that he might be allowed this. God moved the master of the eunuchs to show Daniel kindness and mercy, and he said to him: "I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink; if he should notice that your faces look gloomier than the other youths of your condition, you would cause me to lose my head to the king." Then Daniel spoke to Melzar, whom the master of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Ananias, Mishael, and Azarias: "Please, test us for ten days, and let us be given pulse <note>original: "legumina," referring to vegetables and grains</note> to eat and water to drink. Then let our appearance be compared with 

<column-break/>

the appearance of the youths who eat the royal food, and deal with us according to what you see." So he agreed to this request and tested them for ten days. When the ten days were over, they appeared healthier and better nourished in body than any of the youths who ate the royal food. Therefore, Melzar took away their portion of food and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables. God gave these four youths knowledge and understanding of all literature and wisdom, and he made Daniel skilled in the interpretation of all visions and dreams. When the time had passed which the king had set for them to be brought to him, the master of the eunuchs presented them before Nebuchadnezzar. After the king spoke with them, no one was found among them all to be the equal of Daniel, Ananias, Mishael, and Azarias. Thus, they entered the king’s service. In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and diviners in his entire kingdom. Daniel
<margin>See below, chapter 6.</margin>
remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.

#### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Concerning the statue which Nebuchadnezzar saw in his dreams.</margin>
In the second year of his reign, King Nebuchadnezzar had dreams which troubled his spirit so much that sleep fled from him. Therefore, he ordered the summoning of the diviners, magicians, sorcerers, and Chaldeans to declare the king's dreams to him. When they had come and stood in the king's presence, the king said to them: "I have had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to know what it was." The Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic <note>original: "Syriacè," referring to the language change in the biblical text at this point</note>: "O King, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will explain what it means." But the king answered the Chaldeans: "The matter has escaped me. Unless you show me both the dream and its meaning, you shall be cut to pieces, and your houses shall be turned into dunghills. But if you reveal the dream and its meaning, you shall receive from me great gifts, rewards, and honors. Therefore, explain the dream and its significance." They answered a second time: "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will provide the interpretation." Then the king said: "Truly, I see that you are trying to buy time because you see the matter has escaped me. If you do not show me the dream, there is but one sentence for you—you have agreed to speak lying and corrupt words before me
<margin>a. So that you may drag out the time while I let the matter drop.</margin>
until the time is changed. Therefore, tell me the dream, so that I may know you are able to bring me its interpretation." The Chaldeans answered the king: "There is no man on earth, O King, who can reveal this matter; for no king, prince, or ruler has ever asked such a thing of any magician, diviner, or Chaldean. The thing you ask, O King, is so difficult that there is no one else who can explain it to you except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals." At this, the king was provoked to violent rage and ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed. Once this sentence was pronounced, the wise men were to be put to death, and they sought Daniel and his companions to kill them. Then Daniel inquired about the plan and the decree from Arioch, the king's captain of the guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.

## CHAPTER II.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'A' with floral motifs.</image-desc><margin>Concerning the statue which Nebuchadnezzar saw in his dreams.</margin>In the second year of his reign, King Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams which troubled his spirit, and sleep left him. They answered again: "Let the king tell the dream to us, and we will provide the interpretation." Then the king: "Truly, I perceive that you are trying to buy time, because you see that the thing has escaped me. The thing you ask, O king, is so difficult that there is no other who can explain it to you except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals." Enraged by this, the king commanded all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed. When this sentence was pronounced, it remained for the wise men to be killed, and Daniel and his companions were sought out for death. ### CHAPTER XIII.
->G. L.<-

<margin>The story of Susanna.</margin>
There was a certain man living in Babylon named Joacim. He married a wife named Susanna, daughter of Helcias, a very beautiful woman and one who feared the Lord; she was born of good parents and had been instructed by them in the law of Moses. Joacim was very rich and had gardens very close to his house. The Jews used to frequent his house because he was the most illustrious of them all. In that year, two elders of the people were appointed as judges, of whom the Lord spoke when he said that "iniquity came forth from Babylon from the ancient judges who seemed to govern the people." These men frequented Joacim’s house, and all who had legal disputes came to them. When the people had left at midday, Susanna used to enter her husband’s gardens and walk there. When the two elders saw her entering and walking every day, they were seized with lust for her; they turned away their minds and averted their eyes from heaven so that they would not look toward God or remember justice and equity. Although they both suffered for her, they did not reveal their pain to each other, for they were ashamed to confess their desire to possess her. Yet they watched diligently every day to see her. When they had said to each other, "Let us go home, for it is time for lunch," they departed. But having returned and met in the same place again, they questioned each other for the reason, and both confessed their lust. Then they together appointed a time when they might find her alone. And while they were watching for a suitable day, she entered the gardens as was her custom with only two maids, and she wished to wash herself there, for it was hot. And there was no one there except the two elders hiding and watching her. She told the maids to bring her oil and ointments and to shut the garden doors so she could wash. They did as she said; they closed the garden gate and went out through a side back door to fetch what they were commanded, not noticing the elders because they were hidden. When the maids had gone out, the elders rose up

We, being in a corner of the garden and seeing this wickedness, ran toward them and saw them together, but him we could not catch. For since he was stronger than we, he opened the door and leaped out. We only caught this woman and asked who the young man was, but she refused to tell us. To these things we bear witness." Thus the assembly believed them, as they were elders and judges of the people, and Susanna was condemned to death. Then she cried out with a loud voice, saying: "O immortal God, who knows hidden things, who perceives all things before they come to be, you know that these men have borne false witness against me; and behold, I must die, though I have done none of these things which they have maliciously invented against me." The Lord heard her voice.

At this, the whole assembly broke into a great shout, giving thanks to God, who saves those who trust in him. And they rose up against the two elders, whose testimony Daniel had refuted by their own words. They were punished with the same penalty they had prepared for their neighbor by slander, according to the Law of Moses; <margin>Deut. 19</margin> that is, they were put to death. And on that day, the life of an innocent person was saved. Helcias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, together with her husband Joacim and all her relatives, because no shameful thing had been found in her. Therefore, from that day forward, Daniel was held in great name and glory among the people.

### CHAPTER II.

*Call your brothers "My People," and your sisters "Pitiable." <note>original: "miserandas," also translated as "Pitied"</note> Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, since she is not my wife, nor am I her husband, so that she may remove her fornications from her face and her adulteries from between her breasts. Otherwise, I will strip her and lay her bare, and make her as she was on the day of her birth; I will reduce her to the state of a wasted desert and kill her with thirst. Nor will I have mercy on her children, for they are the children of harlotry. For their mother plays the harlot; she who conceived them acts shamelessly, saying: "I will follow my lovers, who provide me with bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink." Therefore, I will hedge up your ways with thorns and wall her in with a fence, so that she cannot find her paths. Though she pursues her lovers, she shall not overtake them; and seeking them, she shall not find them. Then she will say: "I will return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than it is now." She does not know that it was I who supplied her with grain, new wine, oil, and much silver and gold, which they used for Baal. For this reason, I will take back my grain and my wine in its season, and I will take away my wool and my flax, with which her nakedness <note>original: "uerenda," literally "the parts to be respected"</note> is covered. Now I will uncover her madness before the eyes of her lovers, and no one shall rescue her from my hand. I will take away all her pleasures, her feasts, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her solemn assemblies. I will lay waste to her vines and fig trees (which she says are her wages given to her by her lovers), and I will turn them into a forest to be devoured by the beasts of the field. I will punish her for the days of the Baals, to whom she offered incense, when she adorned herself with earrings and necklaces and followed her lovers, forgetting me, says Jehovah. <note>original: "Ioua"</note> Therefore, I will allure her and lead her into the wilderness and speak kindly to her. From there I will give her her vineyards and the Valley of Achor as a door of hope; there she shall sing as she did in the days of her youth, when she came up out of Egypt. At that time, says Jehovah, you will call me "My Husband" and no longer call me "My Master." I will remove the names of the Baals from your mouth, so that their names shall no longer be mentioned. Then I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, the birds, and the things that move upon the earth; and having broken the bows, swords, and wars from the land, I will make them lie down in safety. I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in mercy, and in compassion. I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you shall know Jehovah. In that time I will respond, says Jehovah; I will respond to the heavens, and they shall respond to the earth, and the earth shall respond to the grain, the wine, and the oil, and these shall respond to Jezreel. <summary>This section of Hosea delivers a scathing indictment of the political and religious leadership of Israel and Judah, condemning their reliance on foreign alliances (Assyria and Egypt) and their hollow religious rituals. The text uses vivid metaphors, such as a "cake not turned" and a "faulty bow," to illustrate the people's spiritual instability and inevitable judgment.</summary>

<summary>This passage concludes the Book of Hosea, juxtaposing God's righteous anger against Israel's idolatry with a tender promise of healing and restoration if they return to Him. It uses historical parallels of Jacob and poetic imagery of nature to emphasize the contrast between human infidelity and divine mercy.</summary>

# JOEL

## CHAPTER I.

->The word of Jehovah spoken to Joel, son of Pethuel.<-

<margin>a. The locusts.</margin>
**H**ear this, you elders, and listen, all you who inhabit the land: has anything like this happened either in your times or in the times of your ancestors? Tell this to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children to the generation that follows. What the caterpillar <note>original: "erucæ"</note> left, the locust has consumed; what the locust left, the young locust <note>original: "bruchus"</note> has consumed; and what the young locust left, the blight <note>original: "rubigo"; typically "mildew" or "rust," here referring to the final stage of agricultural destruction</note> has consumed. Wake up, you drunkards; weep and wail, all you drinkers of wine, because the sweet juice has been snatched from your mouths. For a powerful and innumerable <margin>a</margin> nation has invaded my land, with the teeth of a lion and the molars of an old lion; it has laid waste my vines and stripped my fig trees bare by peeling away their bark, leaving their <margin>b. While she mourns.</margin> branches white. Wail like a virgin girded in sackcloth <margin>b</margin> for the husband of her youth. The grain offering and the drink offerings have been taken away from the house of Jehovah; the priests, the ministers of Jehovah, are in mourning. The field is wasted, the ground mourns: for the corn is ruined, the wine is spoiled, and the oil has perished. The farmers are ashamed; the vinedressers wail for the wheat and the barley, because the harvest of the field is lost. The vines are withered, the fig trees have perished; the pomegranate, the palm, and the apple—briefly, all the trees of the field have dried up, for joy has withered away from the human race. <margin>e. Namely the singers.</margin> Gird yourselves and lament, O priests; wail, you ministers of the altar. Go, spend the night in sackcloth <note>original: "centonibus," literally rags or patched cloths</note>, O ministers of my God, for the grain <margin>e</margin> and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God. <margin>Below in Chapter 2</margin> Declare a fast; proclaim a holy assembly; gather the elders and all the inhabitants into the house of Jehovah your God, and cry out to Jehovah. Alas for the day! For the day of Jehovah is near, a destruction coming from the Almighty. Surely the food is taken away from before our eyes—joy and gladness from the house of our God. The seeds have rotted under their clods, the storehouses are desolate, the granaries are broken down, for the corn has withered. How the beasts groan! The herds of cattle low because they have no pasture; even the flocks of sheep are punished. To you, Jehovah, I will cry out, for fire has consumed the open pastures, and the flame has burned all the trees of the countryside. Even the beasts of the field cry out to you, because the water channels have dried up, and fire has consumed the green places of the wilderness.

## CHAPTER II.

**B**low the trumpet in Zion; sound the alarm on my holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants tremble, for the day of Jehovah is coming, for the day of darkness and gloom is near, a day of clouds and

<margin>a. Just as the mountains, so they occupy all things. b. The devastation of the locusts is like a fire.</margin>
thick darkness. <margin>a</margin> Just as the dawn spreads over the mountains, so a great and powerful people arrives, such as has never been seen before, nor shall be again for many generations to come. <margin>b</margin> Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame burns. Before them the land is like the Garden of Eden; behind them, a desolate wilderness, and nothing escapes them. Their appearance is like the appearance of horses, and they run like horsemen. Like the sound of chariots, they leap over the mountain tops; like the crackling of a flame of fire devouring stubble; like a powerful people prepared for battle. Before them the peoples tremble, and every face turns pale. They run like soldiers, they climb walls like warriors; each moves on his own path, and they do not swerve from their ranks. ### CHAPTER VII.

The Lord Jehovah showed me something of this sort. He was forming locusts at the beginning of the late growth of
grass. Now, this was the late growth after the king’s mowing. # OBADIAH ▶

## The Oracle of Obadiah.

Thus says the Lord Jehovah to Edom <note>original: "Idumææ," the Greek and Latin name for the land of Edom, the descendants of Esau</note>. We have heard a report from Jehovah, and a messenger has been sent among the nations, saying: "Arise, and let us rise up against her for war." Though I have made you the smallest among the nations, so that you are utterly despised, you are puffed up with the pride of your heart, dwelling in the clefts of the rocks—your lofty seat—thinking in your heart: "Who will bring me down to the ground?" Even if you soar aloft like an eagle, and though you set your nest among the stars, from there I will pull you down, says Jehovah. <margin>a</margin> If thieves, if midnight robbers had invaded you (oh, how you are destroyed!), surely they would have stolen only as much as was enough for them. If grape-gatherers had come upon you, surely they would have left some clusters behind. But how the descendants of Esau have been searched out! How their hidden treasures have been hunted for! All your allies have driven you to the very borders; the men who were at peace with you have deceived you and prevailed against you; your own companions <margin>b</margin> have placed a trap beneath you while you were unaware. <note>The Latin 'vunus' (wound/trap) suggests a betrayal by those Jonah trusted.</note> Surely in that time, says Jehovah, I will destroy the wise men of Edom and understanding from the mountain of Esau, and your warriors, O Teman, shall be terrified, so that every man from the mountain of Esau may be cut off by slaughter. Because of the cruelty shown toward your brother Jacob, you shall be covered with shame and cut off forever. On the day you stood aloof, while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates, casting lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them. <margin>c</margin> But do not gaze upon the day of your brother in the time of <margin>d</margin> his misfortune; do not rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their ruin; and do not <margin>e</margin> boast proudly in their time of distress. Do not enter the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; do not you, of all people, gloat over their suffering in the day of their ruin; do not seize their wealth in the day of their ruin; do not stand at the crossroads to cut off those who escape; and do not deliver up their survivors in the time of distress. For the day of Jehovah is near upon all nations: as you have done, so it shall be done to you; your deeds shall return upon your own head. For as you have drunk upon my holy mountain, so all the nations shall drink continually; they shall drink and be swallowed up, so that they will be as if they had never been. But on Mount Zion there shall be those who escape, and it shall be holy, and the descendants of Jacob shall possess their own possessions. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau shall be like stubble; they shall burn them and consume them, so that no survivor shall remain from the house of Esau, for Jehovah has spoken. Those in the South shall possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the lowlands shall possess the land of the Philistines; they shall occupy the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria, and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The exiles of this host of Israelites, who are among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad, shall occupy the cities of the South. Deliverers shall go up to Mount Zion to rule the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom shall be Jehovah’s.

# JONAH ▶

## CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'I' featuring a woodcut illustration of a fortified city with classical towers and gates, representing Nineveh.</image-desc> Jehovah gave a command to Jonah, the son of Amittai, that he should set out for Nineveh, that great city, and preach against it, because its wickedness had ascended into Jehovah’s sight. But Jonah, for the sake of fleeing from Jehovah, hastened to go to Cilicia <note>The Latin identifies "Tarshish" as Cilicia, a region in modern-day Turkey</note> and went down to Joppa. Finding a ship that was going to Cilicia, he paid the fare and went aboard to go with them to Cilicia, avoiding Jehovah. But Jehovah stirred up a great wind upon the sea, and such a great storm arose in the sea that the ship was nearly broken apart. Therefore the sailors were terrified, and each one called out to his own god; and for the sake of lightening the ship, they threw the cargo overboard, while Jonah meanwhile had gone down into the sides of the ship and was lying down, fast asleep. The shipmaster approached him and spoke to him thus: "Why do you sleep? Arise, call upon your God, if perhaps God will take thought of us, so that we do not perish." Then they said to one another: "Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know who is the cause of this evil for us." And so they cast lots; and when the lot pointed to Jonah, they questioned him thus: "Explain to us for what reason this evil has happened to us; what is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country, and from what people are you?" He answered them that he was a Hebrew, and that he revered Jehovah, the God of heaven, who had made the sea and the dry land. Then the men, after they learned from his own testimony that he was fleeing from the presence of Jehovah, were struck with great fear and spoke to him: "What shall we do to you, so that the sea may be calm for us?" For the sea was growing more and more tempestuous. He said to them: "Take me up and throw me into the sea; thus the sea will be calmed for you. For I know that it is because of me that this great storm is harassing you." But the men tried to row back to land; and when they could not, because the storm of the sea was growing steadily against them, they implored Jehovah with these words: "We beseech you, Jehovah, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life, <margin>a</margin> and do not demand from us punishment for innocent blood. For you, Jehovah, do according to your will." <margin>2. Do not punish us as if we were killers of an innocent man.</margin> Then they lifted Jonah up and threw him into the sea, and its raging ceased. Therefore the men revered Jehovah with great fear; they offered a sacrifice to Jehovah and made vows. Now Jehovah had prepared a huge fish to swallow Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights, and in that fish’s belly he prayed to Jehovah his God in these words:
