## CHAPTER XII.

<margin>Philippians 4.</margin>
<margin>a. Whereby you offer yourselves, a rational animal, not unthinking beasts.</margin>
Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercy of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, and acceptable to God, which is your <term>rational worship</term><sup>a</sup>. Do not make yourselves like this age, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may approve what God wills—what is good, acceptable, and perfect. For I declare, <margin>Ephesians 5. 1 Thessalonians 4.</margin> through the benefit that has been granted to me, to every one of you, not to claim more for himself than he ought to claim: but to claim only so much as to be sober in his claim, according to the measure of faith which God has distributed to each. For just as <margin>1 Corinthians 12. Ephesians 4.</margin> we have many members in one body, and all these members do not have the same function: so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another, but having various gifts according to the benefit granted to us: such as prophecy, according to the proportion of faith: or ministry, for ministering: or if one teaches, for teaching: or if one exhorts, for exhorting: or if one is a distributor, let him do it with sincerity: or if one leads, with diligence: or if one gives, let him do it with cheerfulness. Let love <margin>Amos 5. Ephesians 4. 1 Peter 2, 3.</margin> be free of pretense: hating what is evil, clinging to what is virtuous, inclined toward brotherly and mutual love, outdoing one another in honor, not lazy in zeal, burning in spirit, serving the time, rejoicing in hope, patient in adversity, constant in prayer, helping the needs of the saints, practicing hospitality. <margin>Hebrews 13. Matthew 5. Luke 6.</margin> Speak well of those who persecute you; speak well, and do not <margin>b. One must rejoice in the good of others, and grieve at their misfortunes.</margin> curse them. <sup>b</sup> Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep, being of the same mind toward one another: not being haughty in mind, but associating with the humble. Do not be conceited in yourselves, repay no one evil for evil, take care to conduct yourselves honorably among all men: if it is possible (as much as lies in you) live at peace with everyone, not avenging yourselves, O my most dear ones, but <margin>Proverbs 3. Isaiah 5. 1 Peter 3. Proverbs 20. 2 Corinthians 8. Exodus 20.</margin> giving <sup>c</sup> place to wrath. For it stands written: Vengeance is mine, <margin>c. To God, when he inflicts punishment.</margin> I will repay, says the Lord. Therefore if your enemy is hungry, give him something to eat: if he is thirsty, give him something to drink. For in doing this, you will heap burning coals upon his <margin>Deuteronomy 32. Hebrews 10, 12. Proverbs 25.</margin> head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

## CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>1 Peter 2. Wisdom 6.</margin>
Let all mortals obey the superior powers. For there is no power except from God: and the powers that exist have been established by God. Therefore, whoever resists the power resists the ordinance of God: and those who resist will bring punishment upon themselves. For magistrates are not to be feared for good deeds, but for evil ones. Do you wish not to fear the power? Do good, and you will receive praise from it. For he is God's servant for your good. But if you do evil, be afraid. For he does not carry the sword without cause, since he is God's servant to inflict punishment on those who do evil. Therefore it is necessary to obey, not only for fear of punishment, but also because it is a duty. Indeed, for this reason you pay taxes: for they are God's public servants, attending to this very thing. <margin>a Pay all things that you owe. Deuteronomy 5. Leviticus 19:11. Matthew 22. Galatians 5. James 2.</margin>
...to whom fear is due, fear; to whom honor is due, honor. Owe nothing to anyone, except to love one another. For he who loves others has fulfilled the law. For these commands: "Do not commit adultery," "Do not kill," "Do not steal," "Do not bear false witness," "Do not covet," and if there is any other commandment, it is summarized in this saying: "Love the other as yourself." Love does no harm to another. Therefore, the fulfillment of the law is love, especially since we know that the time and hour has come in which we must now 
<margin>Luke 21.</margin>
awaken from sleep. For now salvation is nearer to us than when we first believed. The night has passed; the day is at hand. Therefore, let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light. Let us conduct ourselves honestly, as if in the daylight—not in feasting and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and lusts, not in quarreling and envy. Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the body to indulge its desires.

### CHAPTER XIV.

If anyone is weak in faith, help them without any hesitation of mind. One person believes it is lawful to eat all things; another, who is weak, eats only vegetables. 
<margin>James 4.</margin>
The one who eats must not despise the one who does not. Likewise, the one who does not eat must not condemn the one who does, since God has supported him. Who are you to judge another’s servant? He stands or falls to his own Master. But he will stand, for God is able to establish him. 
<margin>a He makes a distinction between days.</margin>
One person distinguishes one day from another; another considers all days to be the same. Let each person be fully convinced in his own mind. He who regards the day, regards it for the Lord; likewise, he who does not regard the day, does not regard it for the Lord. He who eats, eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God. Likewise, he who does not eat, does not eat for the Lord, and he gives thanks to God. For none of us lives to himself, and none of us dies to himself. For if we live, we live for the Lord; if we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we are the Lord’s. For this reason Christ both died and rose and lived again, so that he might rule over both the dead and the living. 
<margin>James 4.</margin>
But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise your brother? Since we must all appear before the tribunal of Christ. 
<margin>Isaiah 45. Philippians 2. 2 Corinthians 2.</margin>
For it is written: "As I live," says the Lord, "every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall praise God." Therefore, each of us will give an account for himself before God. Consequently, let us no longer judge one another, but rather decide this: not to be a cause of offense or an inconvenience to a brother. I know, and am persuaded through Jesus Christ, that nothing is profane <note>original: "profanum," often translated as "unclean" in a ritual sense.</note> in itself, except that to the one who considers something profane, to him it is profane. But if your brother is offended because of food, you are no longer acting out of love. Do not destroy the one with your food for whom Christ died. Therefore, do not allow 
<margin>b Of the Gospel</margin>
your good to be spoken of as evil. For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but justice, and peace, and joy through the Holy Spirit. For he who serves Christ in these things is both acceptable to God and approved by men. Therefore, let us pursue those things which lead to peace and mutual benefit. Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of

<column-break/>
<page-num>188</page-num>

<margin>Titus 1.</margin>
food. All things indeed are pure, but it is an evil thing if someone eats while causing another to stumble. 
<margin>1 Corinthians 8.</margin>
It is right neither to eat meat, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything by which your brother either trips, is harmed, or 
<margin>c Even if it is lawful for you to know, do not let it hinder anyone.</margin>
is made weak. You have faith; keep it to yourself in the sight of God. Happy is the man who does not condemn himself in what he approves. 
<margin>d To act with certain persuasion.</margin>
But he who doubts is condemned if he eats, because he does not do it with confidence <note>original: "fiducia," traditionally translated as "faith" in this context.</note>; and whatever is not done with confidence is sin.

### CHAPTER XV.

<margin>Galatians 6.</margin>
We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the feeble, and not merely indulge ourselves. Let each of us please the other for their good, to their benefit. For even Christ did not indulge himself, but as it was recorded: 
<margin>Psalm 68 <note>Psalm 69 in modern numbering.</note>.</margin>
"The insults of those who insulted you fell upon me." For whatever was written before was written for our instruction, so that through patience and the comfort of the scriptures, we might have hope. May the God who is the author of patience and comfort grant you to think the same way among yourselves, as is worthy of Christ Jesus, so that with one mind and one voice you may celebrate the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, help one another, just as Christ helped us to the glory of God. 
<margin>a To serve the Jews, so that God’s faithfulness might be cherished, because he had promised it to them.</margin>
I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of circumcision for the sake of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the ancestors, and so that the other nations might celebrate God for his mercy, just as it is written: 
<margin>2 Kings 22 <note>2 Samuel 22:50.</note>.</margin>
"Therefore I will celebrate you among the nations, and sing to your 
<margin>Psalm 117.</margin>
name." And again: "Rejoice, O nations," he says, "with his people." And again: "Praise the Lord, all you nations, and let all peoples praise him." 
<margin>Isaiah 11.</margin>
And Isaiah says: "There shall be that root which shall arise to rule the nations; in him the nations shall have hope." Now may the God who is the author of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit. Indeed, I am persuaded of this regarding you, my brothers: that you are full of all goodness and filled with all knowledge, so that you are able to warn one another. But I have written to you somewhat more boldly, brothers, to remind you of the grace bestowed upon me by God—that I should be a public minister of Jesus Christ to the <term>foreigners</term> <note>original: "extraneos," meaning the Gentiles.</note>, administering the sacred gospel of God, so that 
<margin>e Those things which are offered to God.</margin>
the offering of the <term>foreigners</term> might be acceptable, consecrated by the Holy Spirit. Therefore, I have reason to glory in Christ Jesus regarding things pertaining to God. For I would not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me (to make the nations obedient) both in word and deed, through such great power of signs and miracles, and such power of the Divine Spirit, that from Jerusalem and all around as far as Illyricum, I have filled all with the gospel of Christ. I have done this in such a way that I strived to teach the gospel where Christ was not named, so that I might not build on another’s foundation. 
<margin>Isaiah 52.</margin>
But as it is written: "Those who were not told about him shall see, and those who had not heard shall understand." For this reason I was often hindered from coming to you. But now, since I no longer have a place in these regions, and having a desire for many years to visit you...

...I have been held by a desire for many years now, whenever I set out for Spain, I will visit you. For I hope to see you on my journey and to be sent on my way there by you, if first I have somewhat satisfied my longing for you. Now, however, I am setting out for Jerusalem to serve the saints. For it pleased those in Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem. It pleased them, I say, <margin>2 Corinthians 9</margin> and indeed they owe it to them. For if the outsiders <note>original: "extranei" – Castellio's term for Gentiles/non-Jews</note> have shared in their spiritual things, they ought in turn to help them in earthly matters. Therefore, when I have finished this and have delivered this fruit to them, I will head to Spain by way of your city. I know that when I come to you, I will come with a full abundance of the Christian gospel. Now I exhort you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to help me by making supplications to God for me, so that I may escape those in Judea who are disobedient; and that the service I am performing in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints, so that I may visit you with joy by the will of God and be refreshed with you. May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

### CHAPTER XVI.

I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a minister <note>The Latin "ministram" suggests an official role, often translated as "deaconess"</note> of the church at Cenchreae, so that you may receive her in the Lord as is worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matter she may need from you. For she has helped many others, including myself. Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in the business of Christ Jesus (who risked their own necks for my life; to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the outsiders) and the church in their house. Greet Epaenetus, most dear to me, who is the first-fruit of Achaia in Christianity. Greet Mary, who has worked hard for our sake. Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and at one time my fellow prisoners, who are distinguished among the Apostles, and who turned to Christ even before I did. Greet Amplias, most dear to me in the Lord. Greet Urbanus, our helper in Christ, and Stachys, my most dear friend. Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus. Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who labor in the business of Christ. Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the business of Christ. Greet the most dear Persis, who has labored much in Christ. Greet Rufus, a chosen man in Christ, and his mother and mine <margin>a. He calls her "mother" out of honor.</margin>. Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers with them. Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints with them. Greet one another with a holy kiss. The churches of Christ greet you. Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who cause seditions and offenses against the teaching you have received, and avoid them. For such men serve not the Lord Jesus Christ but their own bellies, and by smooth and flattering speech they deceive 

<column-break/>

<page-num>190</page-num>

the minds of the innocent. For your obedience has become known to all, for which reason I rejoice for you. But I want you to be wise toward what is good and simple toward what is evil. The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. May the favor of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Timothy, my helper, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen. I, Tertius, who wrote this letter in the Lord, greet you. Gaius, my host and the host of the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, and Quartus the brother. Now to Him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept secret for eternal ages but now made clear, and through the prophetic writings by the decree of the immortal God, explained to all nations for the obedience of faith—to the only wise God through Jesus <margin>Romans 16</margin> Christ be glory forever. Amen.

### PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE *Corinthians.*

### CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>An ornate woodcut initial letter P showing a figure in a state of prayerful study inside an architectural frame.</image-desc>

Paul, called to be an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, to the divine church which is at Corinth, to those sanctified through Christ Jesus, called to be saints, as well as to all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, whether theirs or ours: grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. # PAUL’S EPISTLE

...to have baptized <note>original: "lauisse" – Castellio uses the classical Latin word for "washing" or "cleansing" rather than the traditional ecclesiastical "baptizare."</note> in my own name. I also baptized the family of Stephanas. For the rest, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else. For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to teach the gospel, not with the eloquence of speech, <margin>b. Not that he attributes nothing to the gospel (which the cross teaches), but rather to eloquence.</margin> $^b$ lest the cross of Christ be made empty. For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved, it is the power of God. <margin>Isaiah 29. Obadiah 1. Isaiah 33.</margin> For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the prudence of the clever I will abolish. Where is the wise man? Where is the scholar? Where is the debater of this age? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish? <margin>c. In the most wisely established works of the world. d. Which may appear to be foolish. Matthew 12, 24; Luke 11.</margin> For since, by $^c$ divine wisdom, the world did not so use its wisdom as to know God, it pleased God through the $^d$ foolishness of preaching to save those who believe. For while the Jews demand a portent <note>original: "portentum" – typically translated as a "sign" (signum) in other versions.</note>, and the Greeks seek wisdom, we preach Christ crucified: a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the Greeks. But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, we preach Christ as the power of God and the wisdom of God. For what is the "foolishness" of God is wiser than men, and what is the "weakness" of God is stronger than men. <margin>e. It has the appearance of foolishness.</margin> For you see how you were called, brothers: not many wise according to human standards, not many powerful, not many noble. But God chose the most foolish things of the world to put the wise to shame; and God chose the weakest things of the world to put the strong to shame. And the most ignoble and despised things of the world God chose—even things that are nothing—to abolish the things that are something, so that no mortal should boast before God. <margin>f. Namely, in God. You are God’s men. Jeremiah 9. 2 Corinthians 10.</margin> $^f$ But from Him you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God, and righteousness, and holiness, and liberation, so that, as it is written: Let him who boasts, boast in the Lord.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>a. To conduct myself in such a way that I seemed to know nothing else.</margin>
And so when I came to you, brothers, I came not to explain the divine oracle to you with any excellence of speech or wisdom. For I had determined $^a$ to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified. Thus I was among you with much weakness and fear and trembling; and my speech and preaching were not based on the persuasive words of human wisdom, but consisted of a demonstration of divine power, so that your faith might not rest in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God. Yet we do speak wisdom among the mature—a wisdom, I say, not of this age, nor of the leaders of this age, who are passing away. Instead, we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, a hidden wisdom which God destined before the ages for our glory, which none of the leaders of this age knew. For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory. But (as it is written): what no human eye <margin>Isaiah 64.</margin> has seen, nor ear has heard, nor mind has conceived—the things God has prepared for those who love Him. But God has revealed them to us through His Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, even the deep secrets of God. For who among men knows a man's business except the man's own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the business of God except the Spirit of God. Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that comes from God, so that we might understand what

<column-break/>

God has freely given us. These things we also speak, not in the learned words of human wisdom, but in words learned from the Holy Spirit, <margin>b. Divine matters in unpolished speech. c. Human and divine matters suitably, humbly, and as one removed from the divine. Wisdom 9. Isaiah 40. Romans 11.</margin> $^b$ matching spiritual things with spiritual words. $^c$ But the natural man does not grasp the things of the divine Spirit, for they are foolishness to him; therefore he cannot know them, because they must be spiritually examined. But the spiritual man explores all things, yet he himself is explored by no one. For who has known the mind of the Lord so as to instruct Him? But we have the mind of Christ.

### CHAPTER III.

But I, brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as humans—as infants in the Christian life. I gave you milk to drink, not solid food. For you were not yet able to take it; indeed, even now you are still not able, because you are still human. For while there is jealousy, and strife, and division among you, are you not human, and do you not behave in a human way? For when <margin>See Chapter 1.</margin> one says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I am of Apollos," are you not human? Who then is Paul? And who is Apollos? Only ministers through whom you believed, as the Lord gave to each. I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. Therefore, neither the planter nor the waterer is anything, but only God who gives the growth. The sower and the waterer are one, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor. For we are God's co-workers; you are God’s field, God’s building. According to the grace of God granted to me, like a wise master builder I laid the foundation, and another builds upon it. But let each one see how he builds upon it. For no one can lay any other foundation than the one which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw, each one's work will become clear. For the Day will declare it, because it will be revealed by fire; and the fire will test what sort of work each has done. If the work that someone has built survives, he will receive a reward. If anyone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss, <margin>1 Corinthians 6.</margin> though he himself will escape, but only as through fire. Do you not know that you are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you? If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, and you are that temple. Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you seems wise in this life, let him become a fool so that he may become truly wise. For the wisdom of this world is <margin>Romans 1. Job 5. Psalm 93.</margin> foolishness with God. For it stands written: He catches the wise in their own craftiness. And again: The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are vain. Therefore, let no one boast in men. For all things are yours—whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come—all are yours; and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

Let men regard us in this way: as ministers of Christ and stewards of the divine mysteries. Moreover, it is required in stewards that one be found faithful; but to me it is of very little concern...

regarding myself, it matters very little if I am judged by you, or by any human court <note>original: "humana die" — literally "human day," a classical legalism for a set day of trial or judgment</note>; indeed, I do not even pass judgment on myself. For although I am aware of nothing against myself, I am not thereby acquitted. But he who will pass judgment on me is the Lord. Therefore, do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the intentions of hearts; and then at last, each one will receive praise from God. I do not write this to shame you, but to warn you as my dearest children. Now, some have become puffed up, as if I were not coming to you; but I will come to you shortly, if the Lord wills, and I will learn not the talk of these puffed-up people, but their power; for the divine kingdom consists not in talk, but in power. Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a gentle spirit?

### CHAPTER VI.

<margin>a. Not Christians.

Therefore, if you have controversies regarding the business of this life, do you refer them to the judgment of those who are held in contempt in the church? I say this to your shame. It is already a total failing in you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather suffer injury? Why not rather be defrauded? Instead, you yourselves do injury and defraud—and your own brothers at that!

Do you not know that the unjust will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor sodomites <note>original: "cinædi" — those practicing unnatural vice</note>, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor robbers will inherit the kingdom of God. And such were some of you. But you were washed, you were made holy, you were made just, through the name of the Lord Jesus and through the spirit of our God. Anything is permitted for me, though not everything is beneficial; anything is permitted for me, though I will not be enslaved by anything. Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food, but God will abolish both the one and the other. The body is not for immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. Truly God both raised the Lord and will raise us up through his power. Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? Never! Do you not know that he who joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For "the two," he says, "shall become one body." But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit...

A woman is bound by law as long as her husband lives; but if her husband dies, she is free to marry whomever she wishes, provided it is in a manner worthy of the Lord; though she is happier if she remains as she is, in my opinion. And I think that I also have the divine spirit.

### CHAPTER IX.

<margin>a. A Christian.</margin>
Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord? That when I teach, the gospel of Christ is provided without expense <margin>d. ### ->CHAPTER XI.<-

<margin>20</margin> I praise you indeed, brothers, because you remember all my things, and you hold to the institutions just as I delivered them to you. But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ: the head of the woman is the man: <margin>Ephesians 5</margin> the head of Christ is God. Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered dishonors his head. Conversely, every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered dishonors her head: for it is exactly the same as if she were shaven. For a man indeed ought not to veil his head, since he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of man. For man is not from woman, but woman from man, since man was not created for the <margin>Genesis 2</margin> <margin>30</margin> woman, but woman for the man. Does not nature itself teach you that if a man grows his hair long, it is a disgrace to him? But if a woman grows her hair long, it is an honor to her? Since hair is given to her as a covering. Now in giving this instruction, I do not praise you, because you meet together not for the better, but for the worse. Therefore, when you come together into the same place, it is not to eat the Lord’s supper, since each one takes his own supper beforehand while eating; and one is hungry, another is drunk. ### ->CHAPTER XII.<-

<margin>20</margin> Regarding spiritual matters, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant. You know that when you were outsiders, you were led and carried away to mute minor gods. Therefore I declare to you that there is no one who, speaking by divine inspiration, curses Jesus with words: likewise, there is no one who can call Jesus "Lord," except <margin>1 Cor. 10; 4 Mark 9</margin> through the Holy Spirit. Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit: and there are varieties of ministries, but the same Lord: and there are varieties <margin>30</margin> of workings, but the same God, who works all things in all people. But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to each for what is profitable. For to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit: to another the word of knowledge, by the same Spirit: to another faith, through the same Spirit: to another the workings of miracles: to another prophecy: to another the discernment of spirits: to another various kinds of tongues: to another the interpretation of tongues. And one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each one individually as <margin>40</margin> he wills. For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the one body, though they are many, are one body, so also is <margin>Romans 12 Ephesians 4</margin> Christ. For in one Spirit we were all washed into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and we have all drunk of one Spirit. For <margin>50</margin> the body is not one member, but many. If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body," is it therefore not of the body? Likewise if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," is it therefore not of the body? If the whole body were an eye, where would be the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where would be the sense of smell? Now God has placed each one of the members in the body just as he willed. But if they were all one member, where would the body be?

Now there are many members, but it is one body. Nor indeed can the eye say to the hand: "I do not need you," or again the head to the feet: "I do not need you." On the contrary, the more a member of the body seems to be weak, the more necessary it is; and those parts which we judge to be less honorable in the body, we surround with greater honor; and our most unpresentable parts obtain the greatest dignity, while our most honorable parts have no such need. Indeed, God has so tempered the body, giving the greatest honor to the part that lacked it, so that there would be no division in the body, but that the members <margin>Romans 8</margin> might have the same care for one another. And if one member <margin>Hebrews 4</margin> should suffer, all the members should suffer with it; <margin>Ephesians 4</margin> or if one member should be honored, all the members should rejoice with it. Now, you are in some measure the body of Christ and his members; and God has appointed some in the church: first apostles, then prophets, <note>original: "uates" — Castellio uses this classical term for "divinely inspired poets/seers" instead of the traditional ecclesiastical "prophetae."</note> thirdly teachers, then miracles, <note>original: "portenta" — literally "omens" or "prodigies," used here for miraculous powers.</note> then gifts of healing, assistants, administrations, and various kinds of languages. Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle-workers? Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all <margin>Below, 14</margin> interpret? Truly, you should desire the most excellent gifts, but I will now show you a yet more excellent way.

### CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>LOVE.</margin>
If I speak in the tongues of men and of spirits, <note>original: "geniorum" — Castellio used the classical term "genii" to refer to angels, a choice that was highly controversial among his contemporaries.</note> yet am not endowed with love, I am like a clanging brass or a tinkling cymbal. And if I should have such power of divination that I grasp all secrets and all knowledge, and if I am endowed with such faith that I might even move mountains, yet am not endowed with love, I am nothing. And if I should distribute all my resources in many acts of generosity, and if I should deliver even my body to be burned, yet am not endowed with love, I gain nothing. <margin>Above, 10</margin> Love is patient, it is kind; love <margin>Philippians 2</margin> is not envious; love is not reckless, it is not puffed up, it does not behave disgracefully, it does not seek its own, it is not irritable, it thinks no evil, it does not rejoice in injustice but delights in the truth; it endures all things, believes all things, hopes all things, sustains all things. Love never fails. But as for prophecies, they will be abolished; and as for tongues, <margin>a. That is: this [knowledge] which is imperfect can be increased; it will be succeeded by the perfect.</margin> they will cease; and <sup>a</sup> <gloss>knowledge will be destroyed.</gloss> For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when perfection comes, then that which is partial will be destroyed. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. But when I became a man, I destroyed childish things. For now we see through a mirror in riddles; <note>original: "per ambages" — referring to obscure or indirect speech, often translated as "darkly."</note> but then we shall be present face to face. Now I know in part; but then I shall recognize, just as I have been recognized. Now indeed remain faith, hope, and love, but the greatest of these three is love.

### CHAPTER XIIII.

<margin>Above, 12</margin>
Pursue love, and truly desire spiritual things, but especially that you may prophesy. For he who speaks in a foreign tongue does not speak to men <margin>a. Understands.</margin> but to God, since no one <sup>a</sup> <gloss>hears</gloss> him, but in his spirit he speaks secrets. But he who prophesies speaks to men for their benefit, both by encouraging and by consoling. He who speaks in a foreign tongue profits himself;

<column-break/>

<page-num>202</page-num>
but he who prophesies profits the assembly. <note>original: "concioni" — Castellio uses this term for a public gathering or congregation.</note> I would indeed wish that you all spoke in foreign tongues, but even more that you would prophesy. For he who prophesies is greater than he who speaks in foreign tongues—unless he interprets, so that the assembly may receive benefit. Otherwise, brothers, if I come to you speaking in foreign tongues, how will I profit you, unless there be in my speech a revelation, or knowledge, or prophecy, or teaching? Even inanimate things that give a sound, such as a flute or <margin>10</margin> a harp, unless they make a distinction in the sounds, how will it be understood what is being played on the flute or the harp? For if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will prepare himself for battle? Similarly, unless you produce significant words with your tongue, how will it be understood what is said? For you will be those who speak into the air. There are (for example) so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without meaning. If, therefore, I do not understand the power of the voice, I shall be a barbarian to the speaker, and the speaker will be a barbarian <margin>20</margin> to me. So you, since you are seekers of the gifts of the spirit, take care that you excel in them so that it may be of use to the assembly. Therefore, let him who speaks in a foreign tongue pray that he may interpret. For if I pray in a foreign tongue, my spirit indeed prays, but as far as the meaning <margin>b. I contribute nothing to others.</margin> is concerned, <sup>b</sup> <gloss>I am unfruitful.</gloss> What is it then? I will pray with my spirit so that I pray meaningfully; I will sing with my spirit so that I sing meaningfully. For if you speak praises with your spirit, how <margin>30</margin> will he who holds the place of the unlearned say "Amen" to your thanksgiving? Since he does not know what you are saying. For you indeed give thanks well; <margin>Above, 2</margin> but the other is not helped. I give thanks to my God that I possess foreign tongues more than any of you. But in the assembly, I would rather speak five words in this way—so that my speech is understood and I may instruct others—than ten thousand words in an unknown language. Brothers, <margin>Ephesians 4</margin> do not be infants in your minds, but be children in regards to vice, and in your minds be adults. In the teaching it is recorded in memory: "With foreign tongues and lips I will speak to this people, <margin>Isaiah 28</margin> and yet even so they will not obey me," <margin>40</margin> says the Lord. Therefore, tongues are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers; but prophecy is not for unbelievers, but for believers. Therefore, if the whole assembly comes together in the same place, and everyone speaks in foreign tongues, and the unlearned or unbelieving enter, will they not say you are insane? But if everyone prophesies, and some unbeliever or unlearned person enters, he is rebuked by all, he is examined by all, and thus the secrets of his heart become clear: so it happens that he falls prostrate and worships God, confessing that God is truly <margin>50</margin> among you. What is it then, brothers? When you meet, each of you has a song, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation; let all things be done for benefit. If anyone speaks in a foreign tongue, let it be by two, or at most three, and that in turns, and let one interpret. But if an interpreter is absent, let him be silent in the assembly, and speak to himself and to God. Likewise, let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge. But if something is revealed to another sitting by, let the first be silent. For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged. And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace, as is the case in all the assemblies of the saints. Your wives should be silent in the assemblies. ### CHAPTER XV.

<margin>Galatians 1</margin>
Now I declare to you, brothers, the gospel which I taught you, which you also received, in which you stand, and through which you will be saved—if you hold to the reason I taught it to you—unless you have believed in vain. For first of all, I delivered to you what I had received: that Christ died for our sins, as it is in the scriptures; <margin>Isaiah 53 a. Hosea 6</margin> and that he was buried, and rose again on the third day, as it is held in the scriptures; and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve, then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, <margin>Matthew last [chapter], Mark 16</margin> most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep. Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles. Last of all, as if to an untimely birth, <note>original: "abortui" — literally "to an abortion," a self-deprecating term Paul uses for his late arrival to the faith.</note> he appeared also to me. <margin>Ephesians 3</margin> For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the divine church. But by the favor <note>original: "beneficio" — Castellio often uses this instead of the ecclesiastical "gratia" (grace).</note> of God I am what I am, and his favor toward me was not so empty that I did not labor more than any of them—or rather, not I, but the favor of God which was with me. Therefore, whether it was I or they, so we preach, and so you believed. But if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how is it that some among you deny there will be a resurrection of the dead? For if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not risen either. And if Christ has not risen, then our preaching is vain, and your faith is vain, and we are found to be false witnesses of God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise, if indeed the dead do not rise. For if the dead do not rise, then Christ has not risen: and if Christ has not risen, your faith is vain; <margin>b. Not yet justified, since your righteousness is situated in his resurrection.</margin> you are still in your sins. Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished. If we have hope in Christ only for the sake of this life, we are the most miserable of all men. <margin>Colossians 1, 1 Thessalonians 4</margin> But now Christ has risen from the dead: he was the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead also comes through a man. For as through Adam all die, so through Christ all will be made alive, but each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then Christians at his coming, then the end will be, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he has indeed abolished all principality, and all power and authority. <margin>Psalm 110, Hebrews 2</margin> For he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet; the last enemy to be destroyed is death. For he has put all things under his feet. But when he says that all things are to be subjected, it is to be understood in this way:

<column-break/>

that he who subjected all things to him is excluded. But when all things have been subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all. Otherwise, what will they do who are washed <note>original: "lauantur" — Castellio translates "baptized" with the more classical/literal "washed."</note> for the dead, if the dead do not rise at all? Why are they washed for the dead? And why do we face danger at every hour? I die daily—I swear by our glorying which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord. <margin>c. Looking at nothing else than this victory, as men are accustomed to do.</margin> If, in a human manner, I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what benefit is that to me if the dead do not rise? Let us eat and drink: for tomorrow we shall die. Do not be deceived. <margin>Wisdom 2, Isaiah 22</margin> Bad conversations corrupt good character. <note>original: "Mores bonos colloquia corrumpunt mala" — a quote from the Greek poet Menander.</note> Be sober, as is right, and do not sin. For some are ignorant of God, which I say to your shame. But someone will say: "How do the dead rise? Or with what kind of body do they come?" O foolish man: what you sow does not come to life unless it dies: and what you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be, but a bare grain—of wheat, for example, or of something else. But God gives it a body as he pleased, and to each of the seeds its own body. Not all flesh is the same flesh: but there is one flesh of men, another of beasts, another of fish, and another of birds. Likewise, there are celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies: but the splendor of the celestial is one thing, and that of the terrestrial is another; there is one splendor of the sun, another of the moon, and another of the stars: for one star excels another in splendor. Such also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown with mortality, it will rise with immortality; it is sown with disgrace, it will rise with glory; it is sown with weakness, it will rise with power; it is sown a natural body, it will rise a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body. <margin>Genesis 2</margin> And as it is written, the first man Adam was made a living soul, the last Adam is a life-giving spirit. But the spiritual was not first, but the natural, then the spiritual. The first man was from the earth, earthly; the second man is from heaven, heavenly. As the earthly man was, such also are the earthly; and as the heavenly man is, such also are the heavenly. And just as we have borne the image of the earthly, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly. Now I say this, brothers, because flesh and blood cannot obtain the divine kingdom, nor will mortality obtain immortality. Indeed, I tell you a mystery: we shall not all fall asleep, but we shall all be changed, in a single point of time, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet-blast. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise incorruptible, <margin>d. That is, those who will be living then, as we are living now.</margin> and we shall be changed. For it is necessary for this corruptible nature to be clothed with incorruption, and this mortal to be clothed with immortality. But when this corruptible has been clothed with an incorrupt nature, and this mortal has been clothed with immortality, then <margin>Hosea 13, Hebrews 2, 1 John 5</margin> what is said in that scripture will happen: "Death is swallowed up victoriously." Where is your sting, O death? Where is your victory, O Orcus? <note>original: "Orcus" — a classical Latin name for the underworld or the god of the dead, used here by Castellio instead of "Hades."</note> Now the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, my dearest brothers, show yourselves constant, immovable, always excelling in the Lord's business, knowing that your labor in the Lord's cause is not in vain.

### CHAPTER XVI.

Regarding the collection to be gathered for the saints, you should do just as I directed the assemblies in Galatia. On the first day after the Sabbath, each of you should set something aside at home, collecting what he can comfortably afford, so that collections are not only being made when I finally arrive. When I do arrive, I will send those whom you have approved by letter to carry your gift <note>original: "beneficium" — literally a 'benefit' or 'kindness,' here referring to the charitable collection.</note> to Jerusalem. If it seems worthwhile for me to go as well, they shall travel with me. I will come to you after I have passed through Macedonia; for I intend to travel through Macedonia. I may perhaps stay with you, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I go next. For I do not wish to see you merely in passing; rather, I hope to remain with you for some time, if the Lord permits. I will stay in Ephesus, however, until Pentecost <note>original: "quinquagesimam" — the fiftieth day, or Pentecost.</note>. For a great and effective door is open to me, and there are many adversaries. If Timothy comes, see to it that he is among you without fear. For he does the work of the Lord, just as I do. Therefore, let no one despise him, but send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me. For I am expecting him with the brothers. Concerning our brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his will to go now; however, he will come when it is convenient for him. Be vigilant, stand firm in the faith, be courageous and constant, and let all your deeds be done with love. I exhort you, brothers: you know that the household of Stephanas and Fortunatus are the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints; you should likewise submit to such people, and to everyone who assists and labors. I am glad of the arrival of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because they have supplied what was lacking from you, for they have refreshed both my spirit and yours. Therefore, recognize such men. The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, along with the assembly in their house. All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. This greeting is by my own hand, Paul’s. If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. *The Lord is coming* <note>original: "Maranatha" — an Aramaic phrase meaning "The Lord has come" or "Come, O Lord."</note>.
<margin>a The Lord our Lord comes. But if anyone does not love Him, they wait for another in vain.</margin>
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you. My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.

# PAUL THE APOSTLE'S
## SECOND LETTER
## TO THE CORINTHIANS.

### CHAPTER I.

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by
the will of God, and Timothy
our brother, to the assembly of God which
is at Corinth, and to all the saints
dwelling in all Achaia: grace

<column-break/>

and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus
Christ. Praiseworthy is the God and Father of our
Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all
comfort, who comforts us in all our calamity,
so that we may be able to comfort those who are in
any calamity with that same comfort by which
we ourselves are encouraged by God. For just as the
sufferings we endure for Christ increase, so through Christ
our comfort is even greater. For whether we are afflicted,
it is for your comfort and salvation, which is
at work in the enduring of the same sufferings that we also
suffer; or if we are encouraged, it is for your
comfort and salvation. We have a firm hope for you,
knowing that just as you are sharers in the hardships,
so you will also share in the comfort. For we do
not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of how great an affliction
pressed upon us in Asia, being beyond our strength
to such an extent that we even despaired of life.
<margin>a. We were in extreme danger of death.</margin>
Indeed, we ^a felt the sentence of death within ourselves,
so that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God who
raises the dead; He who defended us from such a death
and continues to defend us, and whom we hope will
defend us hereafter, provided you also assist us with prayer,
so that thanks may be given to God by many people
on our behalf for the benefit granted to us for your sake.
For this is our boast: the testimony of our conscience,
that with divine simplicity and sincerity—not with human wisdom, but with
divine grace—we have conducted ourselves in the rest of the world, and
especially among you. For we write nothing else to you
than what you read or even recognize, and,
as I hope, you will recognize to the end, just as
you have partially recognized us: that we ^b are
<margin>b. We are those in whom you may boast.</margin>
your boast, as you are ours, on the day
of the Lord Jesus. And with this confidence I wanted to
come to you, and to be sent on my way by you into Judea.
Therefore, in deliberating this, did I act with levity? Or what I
decide, do I decide in a human way, so that with me there is
"yes, yes" and "no, no"? God is faithful, for our
word to you was not "yes" and "no." For the Son of
God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—
by me, Silvanus, and Timothy—was not
"yes" and "no," but in Him it was "yes." For all
the promises of God are such that in Him they are "yes,"
and in Him they are "amen," which brings glory to God through us. And He
who confirms us with you in Christ, and who
anointed us, is God, who also sealed us and
placed the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts. I indeed
call God as witness to my soul, that it was for the sake of sparing you
that I have not yet come to Corinth; not that we
rule over your faith, but we work with you for your joy,
for by faith you stand.

cheer me except the one who is grieved by me? And I wrote this
very thing to you so that, when I came, I would not be afflicted with grief by those
who ought to make me rejoice; having confidence in all of
<margin>a. All of you, rejoice when I rejoice.</margin>
you ^a that my joy is the joy of you all. For with much
distress and anguish of heart I wrote to you, with many

...with tears, not so that you might be pained, but so that you might know the love with which I especially follow you. But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused me sorrow, except to some extent, so as not to burden you all. Such a punishment by the majority is enough for him, so that instead you should rather forgive and comfort him, lest perhaps he be consumed by excessive grief. Therefore, I urge you to exercise your charity toward him. For I wrote for this purpose: to put you to the proof, to see if you are obedient in all things. But to whomever you forgive anything, I also forgive. For indeed, if I have forgiven anything, I did it for your sake in the person of Christ, so that we might not be outwitted by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his efforts <note>original: "conatus" — Paul refers to the "designs" or "schemes" of the devil to cause division through unforgiveness.</note>. Furthermore, when I had come to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door was opened to me in the Lord’s business, I had no rest in my spirit because I did not find my brother Titus; so, having said farewell to them, I set out for Macedonia. But thanks be to God, who always makes us triumph in the business of Christ <note>original: "Christi negocio" — Castellio uses this term to emphasize the active work or "affair" of Christ's ministry.</note>, and through us spreads the scent of His knowledge in every place. For we are the sweet odor of Christ to God, among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing: to the latter, a deadly smoke leading to death; to the former, a vital odor leading to life. And who is fit for such things? For we are not like many who peddle the divine doctrine <note>original: "cauponantur" — literally "to act like a huckster or tavern-keeper," implying the watering down or selling of God's word for profit.</note>; but we speak as from sincerity, as from God, in the sight of God, in the business of Christ.

### CHAPTER III.

Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we, like some, need letters of recommendation either to you or from you? You are our letter, written in our hearts, to be known and read by all men. It is clear that you are a letter of Christ, administered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets, but on the fleshy tablets of the heart. Such is the confidence we have through Christ toward God, not because we are fit of ourselves to think of anything as coming from ourselves, but our fitness is from God, who has made us fit ministers of a new covenant—not of the letter, but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

<margin>Exod. 34</margin>
But if the ministry of death, imprinted in letters on stones, was yet of such splendor that the Israelites could not look upon the face of Moses because of the splendor of his face—which was to perish—shall not the ministry of the Spirit be even more joined with splendor? For if the ministry of condemnation is splendid, the ministry of justice excels much more in splendor.
<margin>a. The splendor of the Law is nothing if compared with the gospel.</margin>
For indeed ^a that which was splendid was not even splendid if compared with the surpassing splendor. For if that which perishes was joined with splendor, much more does that which remains exist in splendor. Having therefore such a hope, we use great freedom of speech,
<margin>Ibid.</margin>
not as Moses, who put a veil over his face so that the Israelites would not look at the end of what was perishing, but rather their minds were dulled. For to this very day, the same veil remains in the reading of the Old Covenant, and it is not uncovered because it is abolished in Christ. Indeed, to this very day, whenever Moses is read, a veil

<column-break/>

<page-num>108</page-num>
<header>TO THE CORINTHIANS.</header>

<margin>John 4</margin>
covers their hearts. But whenever one returns to the Lord, the veil is taken away. Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. And we all, with unveiled faces, beholding as in a mirror the splendor of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image, with splendor being made perpetual, as if by the Spirit of the Lord.

### CHAPTER IV.

Therefore, having this administration (which is by divine mercy toward us), we do not grow weary;
<margin>a. Things which are usually hidden.</margin>
rather, having ^a rejected hidden shames, we do not conduct ourselves craftily, nor do we handle the divine doctrine deceitfully; but by the declaration of truth, we commend ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God. But if our gospel is covered, it is covered to those who are perishing, whose minds—
<margin>b. The Devil. Isa. 6, John 12</margin>
namely the unbelievers—the ^b god of this age has blinded, so that the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of the invisible God, might not shine upon them. For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded light to shine out of darkness, is the one who has shone in our hearts, for the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the person of Jesus Christ. But we have this treasure in earthenware vessels <note>original: "testaceis uasis" — fragile clay pots, contrasting the weakness of the human messenger with the value of the message.</note>, so that such excellent power may be God’s, and not from us. We are indeed pressed in all things, but not crushed; we are in distress, but not in despair; we are persecuted, but not abandoned; we are cast down, but we do not perish; always carrying about the killing of the Lord Jesus in our body, so that the life of Jesus may also be represented in our body. For we who live are always being given over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be represented in your mortal body. So then, death works in us, but life in you. And endowed with the same spirit of trust, as it is written:
<margin>Psalm 115</margin>
*I believed, and therefore I spoke*, we also believe, and therefore we speak, knowing that He who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us through Jesus and present us with you. For all things are for your sake, so that such a generous benefit might abound through the thanksgiving of many to the glory of God. For this reason we do not grow weary, for even if our outward man is corrupted, yet the inner man is renewed day by day. For our brief and light calamity produces for us a glory that is incredible to describe, so eternal and so heavy, while we look not at things which are seen, but at things which are not seen. For things which are seen are temporary, but things which are not seen are eternal.

### CHAPTER V.

For we know that if the tent of our earthly house is dissolved, we shall have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. For in this we groan, desiring to put on our heavenly dwelling, if indeed, being clothed, we shall not be found naked. For we who are in this tent groan, being burdened, since we would not wish to be unclothed, but rather clothed over, so that mortality may be swallowed up by life. Now He who has made us for this very thing is God, He who has given us the Spirit...

<summary>Paul describes the superiority of the New Covenant's spiritual glory over the temporary glory of the Law of Moses, and explains that despite human frailty and suffering, the believer is sustained by the hope of eternal life.</summary>

<page-num>209</page-num>

<header>T H E  S E C O N D  L E T T E R</header>

the Spirit gave the pledge <note>original: "arrabonem" — a legal or commercial term for a down payment or deposit that guarantees the full amount later.</note>. Therefore we are always confident: and since we know that while we are traveling in the body, we are traveling away from the Lord (for we live in the trust of the thing, not in the thing itself), we are confident: and <margin>Romans 14</margin> we would prefer to be away from the body and present with the Lord. Accordingly, we strive so that whether we are present or absent, we may be acceptable to him. For we must all appear before Christ’s judgment seat <note>original: "tribunal" — the raised platform where a Roman magistrate would sit to pass judgment.</note>, so that each one may carry away the reward for what he did in the body, whether of good or of evil. Knowing therefore that the Lord is to be feared, although we persuade men, we are indeed transparent to God: and I hope we are also transparent in your minds. For we do not again commend ourselves to you, but we give you an occasion to boast of us, so that you may be fortified against those who boast in appearance and not in spirit. For if we are out of our minds, we are so for God; if we are sane, we are so for <margin>2 Corinthians 5:14</margin> you. For the love of Christ holds us, judging this: that if one died for all, then all have died, and therefore he died for all, so that the living should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and lived again for them. Therefore, from now on, we know no one according to human standards. <margin>who at that time, while on earth, were this, then etc. to Apostle 22 Charity, for it was, to be sent to us for reconciliation, etc. and man to God, whom we served. today.</margin> Even if we knew Christ as a man, yet now we no longer know him so. Therefore, if anyone is a Christian, he is a new thing: the old things have passed away, behold, all things have been made new: and all things are from God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave us the administration of reconciliation, namely that God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself, and not imputing their sins to them: and he has entrusted to us the word <note>original: "orationem" — specifically the message or spoken word of the gospel.</note> of reconciliation. Therefore, since we act as ambassadors for Christ, as though God were exhorting through us, we pray on Christ’s behalf: be reconciled to God, who made the one who knew no sin to be a source of sin for us, so that in him we might become the innocent ones of God.

### CHAPTER VI.

<margin>Isaiah 49</margin> But we, as helpers in this matter, exhort you to take care that you do not receive God’s benefit in vain. For he says: *In an acceptable time <margin>1 Corinthians 4</margin> I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you.* Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation. We offer no offense anywhere, lest the ministry be criticized: but in all things we commend ourselves as ministers of God, in much patience, in blows, in imprisonments, in turmoils, in labors, in watchings, in fastings, in chastity, in knowledge, in clemency, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in genuine charity, in the word of truth, in the power of God, with the weapons of righteousness on the right hand and the left, through glory and disgrace, through bad reports and good reports: as deceivers, and yet true; as unknown, and yet known; as dying, and yet behold we live; as those who are punished, yet not put to death; as grieving, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things. Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians; our heart is wide. If you are restricted,

<column-break/>

you are not restricted toward us, but toward the person with whom you are intimate. I, however, as if from children, ask for a return in kind: be wide in heart yourselves; do not be yoked partners with the unfaithful. <margin>Sirach 13</margin> For what partnership has righteousness with wickedness? What communion has light with darkness? What concord has Christ with Belial <note>original: "Beliale" — a Hebrew term for "worthless" or "wicked," personified as a demon or the devil.</note>? Or what common dealing has a believer with an unbeliever? What agreement has the temple of God with <margin>1 Corinthians 3, 6</margin> idols <note>original: "deastris" — Castellio's term for "lesser gods" or false idols.</note>? For you are the temple of the living God, just as God said: *I will dwell <margin>Leviticus 26</margin> and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they <margin>Isaiah 52</margin> shall be my people.* Therefore, *come out from the midst of them, and be separate,* says the Lord: *and do not touch anything impure; and I will receive you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me,* says the Lord Almighty.

### CHAPTER VII.

Having these promises, therefore, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every stain of both body and mind, performing holiness with the fear of God. Receive us: we have done wrong to no one, we have corrupted no one, we have cheated no one. I do not say this to condemn you, for I have already said that you are in our hearts to die or to live together. I have great freedom of speech with you; I have great boasting about you. I am full of consolation; I overflow with joy in all our calamity. For when we had come into Macedonia, our person had no rest, but we were pressed on every side—battles without, fears within. Nevertheless, God, the consoler of the humble, comforted us by the arrival of Titus. And not only by his arrival, but also by the consolation with which he was moved regarding you, explaining to us your longing for us, your lamentation, and your zeal, so that I rejoiced even more, even though I may have caused you sorrow through my letter. I do not regret it, even if I had regretted it. For I see that if that letter caused you sorrow, though only for a short time, you did not just grieve, but (for which I rejoice) you grieved toward a correction of life. For you grieved according to God, so that you were affected by no disadvantage through us. <margin>1 Peter 3</margin> For divine sorrow effects a correction of life toward a salvation that is never regretted. But worldly sorrow produces death. For behold, this very thing, that you grieved according to God—how much diligence it produced in you? Indeed, what defense? What indignation? What fear? What longing? What zeal? What justice? In all these things you have proved your innocence in that deed. Therefore, if I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did the wrong, nor for the sake of the one who suffered it, but so that your zeal for us might be made manifest among you in the sight of God. For this reason, we were confirmed by the consolation arising from you: but we received a much greater pleasure from the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by all of you. For if I had boasted anything to him about you, I was not put to shame; rather, as we spoke everything truly to you, so our boasting about you to Titus was true. And he follows you with singular charity, recalling the obedience of you all, how you received him with fear and trembling. I rejoice that I can trust you in all things.

### CHAPTER VIII.

Now we make known to you, brothers, the gift <note>original: "beneficio" — Castellio often uses this word for the Greek 'charis' (grace), emphasizing the practical benefit or favor bestowed by God.</note> of God conferred upon the churches of Macedonia: that in the great trial of their calamity, their singular eagerness and deepest poverty worked together to reveal the wealth of their sincerity. For according to their means (I bear witness) and even beyond their means, they voluntarily pleaded with us with many prayers that we would receive the gift and the common service toward the saints. And this was not as we had hoped; rather, they gave themselves first to the Lord, and then to us by the will of God, so that we exhorted Titus that, just as he had already begun, he should also complete this gift among you. Therefore, as you excel in all things—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all diligence, and in this love of yours toward us—see that you also excel in this gift. I say this not by way of a command, but to test the genuineness of your love through the diligence of others.

<margin>Romans 10</margin>
For you know the gift <note>original: "beneficium" — referring to the grace or favor of Christ.</note> of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might be made rich. And in this I give my advice: for this is to your advantage, since you began not only to act but also to be willing since last year. Now therefore, complete the doing of it, so that as there was a readiness of will, so there may be a completion according to your means. For if the eagerness is present, a person is accepted according to what they have, not according to what they do not have. For it is not intended that there be relief for others and distress for you, but that by way of equality, at the present time, your abundance may supply their need, so that their abundance may in turn supply your need, that there may be equality, just as

<margin>Exodus 16</margin>
it is written: *Neither did he who gathered more have too much, nor did he who gathered less have too little.* <note>A reference to the gathering of Manna in the wilderness, where everyone had exactly what they needed.</note> But thanks be to God, who put the same care for you into the heart of Titus, who accepted the exhortation and, being more diligent, went to you of his own accord. And we have sent with him the brother who is praised in the service of the Gospel throughout all the churches, and who was also appointed by the vote of the churches to be our travel companion in this gift being administered by us, to the glory of the Lord and to show your eagerness. We are taking care that no one should

<margin>Romans 12</margin>
blame us regarding this abundance being administered by us, providing that things are honorable not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men. And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have often found diligent in many things, but now far more diligent because of his great confidence in you. Whether as for Titus, he is my partner and a colleague toward you; or as for our brothers, they are the messengers <note>original: "apostoli" — used here in the sense of 'sent ones' or delegates of the churches.</note> of the churches, the glory of Christ. Therefore, give to them and in the sight of the churches a proof of your love and of our boasting about you.

### CHAPTER IX.

For concerning the service toward the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you. For I know your eagerness, of which I boast on your behalf to the Macedonians, that Achaia <note>A Roman province in Greece where Corinth was located.</note> has been prepared since last year; and your zeal has stirred up many.

<column-break/>

<page-num>212</page-num>
<header>TO THE CORINTHIANS.</header>

However, I have sent the brothers so that our boasting about you should not be empty in this regard; so that (as I was saying) you may be prepared. Otherwise, if the Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we (not to say you) would be ashamed in this matter of boasting. Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brothers to go ahead to you and prepare your previously announced gift, so that it might be ready—not as a matter of greed, but as a true gift. But this I say: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Let each one give as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.

<margin>Sirach 35</margin>
And God is able to make every gift abound toward you, so that having all sufficiency in all things, you may abound in every good work, just as it is written: *He scatters and gives to the poor; his righteousness remains forever.* Now may he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, supply and multiply your seed and increase the harvest of your righteousness, so that you may be enriched in everything with all sincerity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us. For the administration of this service not only supplies the needs of the saints, but also overflows through many thanksgivings to God. Through the proof of this service, they glorify God for the obedience of your confession to the Gospel of Christ and for the sincerity of your distribution to them and to all, and by their prayer for you, as they long for you because of the singular favor of God upon you. Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift.

### CHAPTER X.

Now I, Paul, myself exhort you by the gentleness and mildness of Christ—I who am humble when present among you, but bold toward you when absent.

<margin>a. Let him see it thus. b. Or: then naturally, so that it is not necessary for me to treat anyone too harshly.</margin>
But I beg you that<sup>a</sup> you act so that when I am present I might not have to be<sup>b</sup> bold with that confidence with which I intend to be bold against some who consider us as if we walked according to human ways. For though we walk in humanity, we do not wage war according to human ways. For the weapons of our warfare are not human, but powerful through God for the pulling down of strongholds. With these weapons we cast down arguments and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and we lead every mind captive to the obedience of Christ, and we are prepared to punish all disobedience once your obedience is complete. Do you look at the appearance of things? If anyone has persuaded himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this again: that just as he is Christ’s, so also are we. For even if I should boast somewhat more about our authority—which the Lord gave us for building you up and not for destroying you—I will not be ashamed. I do not want to seem as though I am trying to terrify you through letters; for his letters (they say) are weighty and strong, but his physical presence is weak and his speech is contemptible. Let such a person consider this: that what we are in word through letters when absent, such we will also be in deed when present. For we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some<sup>c</sup> who commend themselves; but they, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves to them-

<margin>c. It is unworthy of those with whom we do not compare ourselves.</margin>
