...they do not understand how to compare themselves. But we will not boast excessively, but according to the measure of the rule which God has assigned to us, so that we might reach even as far as you. For we do not overextend ourselves, as if we did not reach you; for we have indeed come to you with the Gospel of Christ, not boasting beyond measure in the labors of others, but having hope that, as your faith grows in you, we may be greatly enlarged within our own boundaries, so that we may teach the Gospel beyond your borders, not boasting in another’s territory regarding things already prepared. But he who boasts, let him boast in the Lord. For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

### CHAPTER XI.

<margin>Genesis 3</margin>
I wish you would bear with a little of my folly; and indeed, do bear with me! For I am jealous for you with a divine jealousy, since I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. But I fear lest perhaps, as the serpent deceived Eve by its craftiness, so your minds might be corrupted and turned away from the simplicity that ought to reside in Christians. For if someone comes preaching another Jesus than the one we preached, or if you receive a different spirit than the one you received, or another gospel than the one you accepted, you might well endure him. But I consider myself to be in no way inferior even to the "super-apostles." Even if I am unskilled in speech, I am not so in knowledge; indeed, we have been made clearly known to you in every way and in all things. Did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I taught you the divine Gospel for free? I "robbed" other churches by taking a salary from them to serve you; and when I was present with you and in need, I did not drain anyone. For the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my need; and so in all things I have kept myself, and will keep myself, from being a burden to you. I confirm this truly through Christ, that I will not allow this boasting to be silenced in the regions of Achaia. Why? Because I do not love you? God knows. But what I do, and will continue to do, I do to cut off the opportunity from those who seek an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things they boast about. For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ. And no wonder, since Satan himself transforms into an angel <note>original: "genium" — Castellio uses "genius" where others use "angelus" (angel), reflecting his humanist Latin style of using classical terminology for spiritual beings.</note> of light. <margin>a. Him [referring to the false apostle]</margin> Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also disguise themselves to appear as ministers of justice; their end will be according to their deeds. I say again: let no one think me a fool. But if someone does, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little. What I say, I say not as is worthy of the Lord, but as if in folly, in this matter of boasting. Since many boast in a human way, I too will boast, since you—being so wise yourselves—gladly tolerate fools. For you tolerate it if someone treats you like slaves, if someone devours you, if someone takes your goods, if someone puts on airs, if someone strikes you in the face. I speak to my shame:

<column-break/>

as if we were too weak for that! But in whatever anyone else dares to boast (I speak foolishly), I also dare. 
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the offspring of Abraham? So am I. <margin>1 Corinthians 4; Above, 6; 2 Thessalonians 3</margin> Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as if insane) I am more so: <margin>b. In physical hardships.</margin> in far more labors, in more beatings, in more imprisonments, and often near death. <margin>Acts 16:23</margin> Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one; three times I was beaten with rods; once I was stoned; three times I suffered shipwreck; a night and a day I spent in the open sea. I have been frequently on journeys, in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own citizens, dangers from foreigners, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers; in labor and toil, often in sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, frequently in fastings, in cold and nakedness. Besides these things, there are the daily pressures upon me: namely, the care for all the churches. <margin>Acts 20</margin> Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn? <margin>c. You would be much more offended</margin> If I must boast, I will boast of my weakness. The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to be praised forever, knows that I am not lying. <margin>Acts 9</margin> In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes, wanting to seize me. But I was let down in a basket through a window in the wall, and so I escaped his hands.

### CHAPTER XII.

Boasting is certainly not profitable for me, for I will come to visions and revelations from the Lord. I know a Christian man who fourteen years ago (whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know, God knows) was snatched up to the third heaven. And I know this man (whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know, God knows) was snatched into Paradise, and heard secret words which it is not lawful for a man to speak. On behalf of such a man I will boast; but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in my weaknesses. For if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, <margin>a. Containing [inc.]</margin> since I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone should think more of me than what he sees me to be or hears from me. And so that I would not exalt myself too much because of the greatness of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a spirit <note>original: "genius" — again used for a spiritual messenger or angel, here a messenger of Satan.</note> of Satan, to beat me, lest I be too exalted. <margin>Deuteronomy 3</margin> Three times I prayed to the Lord about this, that it might leave me; but he said to me: "My favor is enough for you; for my strength is perfected in weakness." Therefore, I will most gladly boast in my weaknesses, so that the strength of Christ may dwell in me. Accordingly, I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties for Christ. For when I am weak, then I am strong. I have been a fool to boast; you forced me to it, when I ought to have been commended by you. For I was in no way inferior to the "super-apostles," even though I am nothing. The signs of an apostle were indeed produced among you with all patience, in wonders and miracles and portents. For in what were you less favored than the other churches, except that I did not drain you? Forgive me this injustice! Now for the third...

In the final chapters of 2 Corinthians, Paul prepares the congregation for his third visit, shifting from a defense of his ministry to a stern warning for those who persist in sin. The transition to Galatians marks a change in tone; Paul immediately defends his apostolic authority as being derived directly from God, rather than human institutions, in response to teachers who were leading the Galatian converts away from his teachings.</meta>

I am ready to visit you, and yet I will not be a burden to you. For I do not seek what is yours, but you yourselves; for children ought not to gather wealth for their parents, but parents for their children. I, for my part, will most gladly both spend and be spent for the sake of your souls, even though the more I love you, the less I am loved in return. But be that as it may, I did not personally burden you; yet, being crafty, I suppose I caught you by trickery. Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I sent to you? I urged Titus to go, and sent a brother with him; did 
<margin>10</margin> Titus take advantage of you? Did we not act in the same spirit? Did we not walk in the same footsteps? Do you think again that we are making excuses to you? <margin>Galatians 5</margin> I may be found by you as you would not wish: lest perhaps there be strife, jealousies, anger, quarrels, slanders, gossiping, arrogance, and disorders: lest when I come to you again, my God may humble me, and I may have to mourn for many who 
<margin>20</margin> sinned before and have not turned away from the uncleanness, fornication, and lust in which they have been occupied.

## CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>Deuteronomy 17, Matthew 18 <note>Original: Mat. 13</note>, John 8, Hebrews 10</margin>
This is the third time I am coming to you: by the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established. I have said before, and I say it now—as I did when I was present the second time, so now while absent I write to those who have sinned before, and to all the others—that if I come again, I will not be lenient, since you seek proof of 
<margin>30</margin> Christ speaking in me, who is not weak toward you, but is powerful among you. For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him; but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you. Test yourselves, to see if you are in the faith; examine yourselves. Or do you not recognize yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless perhaps you are disqualified <note>Latin: "reiectanei", meaning those who fail the test or are rejected.</note>. But I hope you will understand that we are not disqualified. Now I pray to God that you do no evil, not so that we may appear to be approved, but that 
<margin>40</margin> you may do what is right, even if we appear to be disqualified. For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth; for we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. This also we pray for: your restoration. Therefore I write these things while absent, so that when present I may not have to use severity according to the authority which the Lord has given me for building up, and not for tearing down. Finally, brothers, rejoice, be restored, be comforted, be of the same mind, live in peace, 
<margin>50</margin> and the God of love and peace will be with you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.

# THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE
## TO THE GALATIANS.

### CHAPTER I.
Paul, an apostle—not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia: grace and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins, to rescue us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father, to whom be glory for all eternity. Amen.

I wonder that you are so quickly <gloss>a</gloss> turning away from him who called you <gloss>b</gloss> in the grace of 
<margin>a. My paraphrase. b. In the Christian religion.</margin>
Christ, to another gospel; which is not another, except that there are some who trouble you and want to pervert the Gospel of Christ. But even if we, or a heavenly spirit <note>Latin: "coelestis genius", usually translated as "angel from heaven".</note>, should teach you something different from what we taught you, 
<margin>20</margin> let him be accursed <note>Latin: "detestabilis".</note>. As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone teaches you something different from what you received, let him be accursed. For <gloss>c</gloss> am I now seeking the favor of men, 
<margin>c. I do not preach men, but Christ.</margin>
or of God? Or do I strive to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ. But I declare to you, brothers, that the 
<margin>30</margin> Gospel preached by me is not of human origin. For I did not receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came through a revelation of Jesus Christ. For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism: how I excessively persecuted and ravaged the church of God, 
<margin>Acts 9</margin>
and I surpassed many of my own age among my people in my progress in Judaism, being far more zealous for the traditions of my forefathers. But as soon as 
<margin>Philippians 3</margin>
it pleased God (who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by his 
<margin>40</margin> grace) to reveal his Son in me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately <gloss>d</gloss> confer with flesh and blood <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning "with human beings".</note>, nor 
<margin>d. With men</margin>
did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus. Then after three years, I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter, and stayed with him for fifteen days. But I saw no other of the apostles, except James the Lord’s brother. And in what I am writing to you, I witness before God that I am not lying. Afterward I went into the regions of Syria and 
<margin>50</margin> Cilicia. But I was unknown by face to the Christian churches of Judea. They had only heard: "He who once persecuted us now preaches the faith which he once ravaged," and they gave thanks to God because of me.

### CHAPTER II.
Then after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also. I went up by divine revelation, and I presented to them the Gospel which I preach among the Gentiles—privately, however, to those of reputation—lest perhaps...
<meta>catchword: lest perhaps...</meta>

<header>TO THE GALATIANS.</header>

<margin>217</margin>
...lest perhaps I should run, or had run, in vain. But not even Titus, my companion, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised, and that was because of false brothers who were brought in secretly. They had slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might bring us into slavery. To them we did not yield in subjection, even for an hour, so that the truth of the Gospel might remain with you.
<margin>Romans 2. Ephesians 6. Colossians 3. 1 Peter 1. Acts 10. 1 Peter 2. John 4.</margin>
As for those who seemed to be important—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality to any man—those influential men contributed nothing to me. On the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the Gospel for the uncircumcised <note>original: præputij, literally "of the foreskin"</note>, just as Peter had been for the circumcised (for He who worked in Peter as an apostle to the circumcised also worked in me for the <term>Gentiles</term> <note>original: alienigenarum, literally "those born elsewhere" or foreigners</note>)—and when they recognized, I say, the grace bestowed upon me, James, Cephas <note>Peter</note>, and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship. They agreed that we should go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised, provided only that we should be mindful of the poor, which very thing I was eager to do.
<margin>2</margin>
But when Peter came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned. For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they arrived, he drew back and separated himself, fearing those of the circumcision party. And the rest of the Jews joined him in this hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was led astray by their simulation. But when I saw that they were not acting rightly according to the truth of the Gospel, I said to Peter in front of everyone: "If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, why do you compel the Gentiles to <term>Judaize</term>? <note>To adopt Jewish customs and laws.</note>"
<margin>3</margin>
<margin>Romans 3.</margin>
We, who are Jews by nature and not "Gentile sinners," knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but only through <term>trust</term> <note>original: fiducia, implying a confident reliance or faith</note> placed in Jesus Christ, we also have believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by trust in Christ and not by works of the law; for by the works of the law, no mortal will be justified. But if, while seeking to be justified through Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, is Christ then a minister of sin? Certainly not! For if I rebuild the very things I tore down, I prove myself a transgressor. For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live for God; I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the body, I live by trust in the Son of God, who loved me so much that He gave Himself up for me. I do not reject the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.

<margin>below 5. a. so declared that he seems to have been crucified among you.</margin>

Have you suffered so much in vain?—if indeed it was in vain. Does He who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you do so by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
<margin>Genesis 15.</margin>

So then, those who are of faith are blessed along with the faithful Abraham.
<margin>Romans 4. James 2. b. God, as it is held in the scriptures, Genesis 22.</margin>

Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, because "the righteous shall live by faith."

Brothers, let me speak in human terms. Even though it is only a man's covenant, once it has been ratified, no one rejects it or adds to it. Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, "And to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "And to your seed," who is Christ. What I am saying is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God in Christ, so as to cancel the promise. For if the inheritance depends on the law, it no longer depends on a promise; yet God gave it to Abraham through a promise.
<margin>Romans 4. Romans 5.</margin>
Why then the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made; it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not for one party alone, but God is one. Is the law then contrary to the promises of God? By no means! For if a law had been given that could confer life, then righteousness would certainly have been based on the law.
<margin>c. all things are under sin, as the scriptures teach</margin>
But the Scripture has locked up all things under sin, so that the promise through trust in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe. Before trust <note>faith</note> came, we were kept under guard by the law, locked up until the trust that was to be revealed.
<margin>d. so that it might preside over us until the coming of Christ.</margin>
Thus the law was our <term>tutor</term> <note>original: pædagogus, a household guardian or schoolmaster for children</note> to lead us to Christ, so that we might be justified by trust. But now that trust has come, we are no longer under a tutor. For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
<margin>4</margin>
For as many of you as were baptized have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
<margin>Romans 6.</margin>
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.

The Letter to the Ephesians begins with a grand theological vision of God’s plan to unite all things in Christ, moving from the individual’s salvation by grace to the corporate unity of the Church, composed of both Jews and Gentiles.</meta>

#### CHAPTER I.

PAUL, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, to the saints who are at Ephesus, and to those who are faithful through Christ Jesus: grace and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed be God <note>original: "Concelebrandus Deus," literally "God is to be praised together"</note> and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every divine abundance in heavenly Christian matters, just as he chose us in him before the world was founded, that we should be holy and blameless in his sight, endowed with love. For he had destined us for adoption through Jesus Christ, <sup>a</sup> into the same, according to the choice of his will, to the praise of his glorious beneficence <note>original: "beneficentiae," often translated as "grace"</note>, by which he made us accepted through his most beloved [Son], in whom we have liberation through his blood—namely, the forgiveness of sins—according to his so rich beneficence, which he used so generously toward us, with the highest wisdom and prudence, by declaring to us the secret <note>original: "arcanum," the mystery</note> of his will. And he did this because it seemed good to him, so that he himself might determine that when the times were fulfilled, all things should be restored through Christ, both heavenly and earthly. Through Christ, I say, through whom we have been called into our lot, destined by the decree of the one who works all things by the choice of his will, so that we—who placed our hope in Christ—might be for his praise and glory; in whom you also placed your hope, having heard the word of truth, which is the Gospel of your salvation. By believing in it, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit <sup>b</sup> of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the claim of the acquired possession, which matter produces glorious praise for him. Therefore, I, hearing of your faith placed in the Lord Jesus and your love toward all the saints, do not cease to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers, so that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the Spirit as the author of wisdom and revelation, by which you may know him, with the eyes of your mind enlightened, so that you may know what is to be hoped for by those called by him, and how rich and glorious is his inheritance destined for the saints, and how excellent is the magnitude of his power toward us who believe, which he exerted in Christ according to the strength of his extraordinary might, by raising him from the dead.

And he subjected all things under his feet, and gave him as the head over all things to the Church (which is his body), the <sup>c</sup> fullness of him who fills all in all.

# THE APOSTLE PAUL'S
## EPISTLE TO THE Ephesians.

### CHAPTER I.

<margin>Galatians 6. 1 Corinthians 1.</margin>
PAUL, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints who are at Ephesus, and to those who are faithful through Christ Jesus: grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Praiseworthy is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every divine abundance in heavenly matters through Christ, just as he chose us in him before the world was founded, so that we might be holy and blameless in his sight, endowed with love. For he destined us for adoption through Jesus Christ, <margin>ª that is, to be adopted into him: this means he would make them sons of God through him.</margin> ª into himself, according to the choice of his own will, to the praise of his glorious kindness, by which he made us accepted through his beloved Son. In him we have liberation through his blood—namely, the forgiveness of sins—according to the richness of his kindness, which he has used so generously toward us with the highest wisdom and prudence, by declaring to us the secret of his will. And he did this because it seemed good to him, so that he might determine within himself that when the times were fulfilled, all things—both heavenly and earthly—should be restored through Christ. <margin>Galatians 4.</margin> Through Christ, I say, through whom we have been called into our lot, <margin>Romans 8.</margin> having been destined by the decree of the one who accomplishes all things by the choice of his own will. This was done so that we, who first placed our hope in Christ, might exist for his praise and glory. In him you also placed your hope after you heard the word of truth—that is, the Gospel of your salvation. By believing in this, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit <margin>ᵇ who rightly gives us faith, so that the promised inheritances might be granted to us.</margin> ᵇ of the promise, which is the pledge of our inheritance, until the full possession of what was won is claimed, a matter which brings him glorious praise. Therefore, hearing of your faith placed in the Lord Jesus and your love toward all the saints, I do not cease to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers. I pray that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation so that you may truly know him. I pray that the eyes of your mind may be enlightened, so that you may know what hope there is for those called by him, how rich and glorious is his inheritance destined for the saints, and <margin>Romans 1.</margin> how excellent is the greatness of his power toward us who believe, which he exerted in Christ according to the strength of his extraordinary might when he raised him from the 

<column-break/>

dead. And this Christ sat at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above every principality, power, might, and dominion, and above every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come. And he put all things under his feet and gave him as the head over all things to the Church (which is his body) <margin>Psalm 8. ᶜ Christ is the one through whom God fills and perfects all things.</margin> ᶜ the fullness of him who fills all things in every way.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Colossians 2.</margin>
Indeed, you were once dead in your offenses and sins, in which you once lived according to the way of this world and the will of the prince of the power of the air—that is, the spirit who now works in rebellious men. We also once lived among those same sins in the desires of our flesh, doing whatever the flesh and our thoughts wanted, and we were by nature worthy of punishment, just like the others. But God, who is rich in mercy, embraced us with such great love that even when we were dead in our sins, he called us back to life together with Christ (you are saved by his favor) and raised us up together, and <margin>ª in that we are Christians.</margin> ª placed us in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus. He did this to show in the ages to come the rich kindness which he used toward us in Christ Jesus out of his own goodness. For you have been saved by favor through faith, and that not of yourselves. It is the gift of God, not from works, lest anyone should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared so that we might live in them. Therefore, remember that you were once Gentiles in the flesh (called "uncircumcision" by those who call themselves "the circumcision" made in the body by hands); remember, I say, that at that time you were without Christ, excluded from the commonwealth <note>original: "republica," suggesting a structured community or state</note> of Israel, lacking the covenants of the promise, having no hope, and being without God in the world. But now in Christ Jesus, you who were once far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who made <margin>ᵇ from both foreigners and Jews.</margin> ᵇ one out of both, and broke down the dividing wall <note>original: "septum interstitium," the barrier between the court of the Gentiles and the inner temple</note>, abolishing in his own body the enmity—the law of commandments contained in decrees. He did this to create in himself one new man out of the two, making peace, and to reconcile both to God in one body through the cross, having destroyed the enmity by it. And he came to announce peace <margin>Luke 2.</margin> both to you who were far off and to those who were near. For through him we both have access by one Spirit to the Father. Therefore, you are no longer strangers and guests, but citizens with the saints and members of God's household, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ himself as the cornerstone. Through him, the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord, in which you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the divine breath <note>original: "divino afflatu," the inspiration or breath of the Spirit</note>.

TO THE EPHESIANS

### CHAPTER III.

For this reason, I, Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ, on behalf of you foreigners <note>original: "alienigenas," referring to the Gentiles or non-Jewish nations</note>, serve as an ambassador: if indeed you have heard of the stewardship <note>original: "dispensationem"</note> of God’s favor, which was bestowed upon me for you: since He revealed the mystery to me by divine means, just as I wrote briefly before, from which you are able to perceive, by reading, my understanding of the mystery of Christ, which was not made known to the human race in other ages, as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets <margin>10</margin> by divine inspiration: namely, that the foreigners <note>Gentiles</note> are fellow heirs, and part of the same body, and sharers in the divine promise in Christ, through the Gospel, of which I was made <margin>1 Corinthians 15.</margin> a minister, by the gift of divine favor, which favor was bestowed upon me by the power of divine might. To me, the least of all the saints, this favor was given, so that I might proclaim the infinite wealth of Christ among the external nations, and make clear to everyone what the fellowship of the mystery is, which from all eternity was hidden in God (who created all things through Jesus Christ), so that the manifold and various wisdom of God might now be made known to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places through the Church, just as He had decreed <margin>20</margin> from every age, and fulfilled in Christ Jesus our Lord, in whom we have boldness and access with confidence <margin>a. namely, to the Father.</margin> through the faith that is to be held in Him. Therefore, I ask that you do not lose heart because of those calamities which I bear for you, which are your glory. For this reason, I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every family <margin>30</margin> in heaven and on earth is named, that according to His glorious wealth He may grant you to be strongly reinforced through His spirit in the inner man, so that Christ may dwell in your souls through faith, and that you may be rooted in love, so that you may be able to comprehend and know, together with all the saints, <margin>b. namely, toward us.</margin> how far and wide, how high and sublime it extends, and how the love of Christ exceeds all knowledge, so that you may be perfected with all divine perfection. Now to Him, who by that power which is active in us is able to do all things <margin>40</margin> far and much more abundantly than we can ask or think, to Him, I say, be glory in the Church through Christ Jesus, throughout all ages forever,
->Amen.<-

### CHAPTER IIII.

I therefore, a prisoner for the Lord’s sake, exhort you to conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of that <margin>50</margin> calling to which you were called, with all modesty and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, striving to preserve the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body, and one spirit, just as <margin>1 Cor. 7. 2 Cor. 12. Psalm 12. S. Cor. 12.</margin> you were called in the one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one washing <note>original: "lotio," referring to baptism</note>, one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and

<column-break/>

in you all. However, favor was given to each one of us according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Therefore (He says), ascending on high, He led away captives, and gave gifts to men. But what does "He ascended" mean, except <margin>John 3.</margin> that He had first descended into the lower parts of the earth? He who descended is the same one who ascended above all the heavens, <margin>1 Cor. 11.</margin> so that He might fill all things. And He gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as Evangelists, some as pastors and teachers, for the building up of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the construction of the body of Christ, until <margin>a. The Christian commonwealth. 1 Cor. 14.</margin> we all arrive at the unity of faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, into a mature man, to the measure of the full Christian age, so that we may no longer be children, tossed about and carried around by every wind of doctrine, by the craftiness of men who attack us with malice to deceive us: but holding the truth with love, let us altogether <margin>b. in Christ, while Christ is the body.</margin> grow up into Him who is the head, namely Christ, from whom the whole body is joined and connected by every joint (through which the administration is effected), and by the action (which is according to the measure of each part) causes the growth of the body, for its own building up in love. This, therefore, I say and warn through the Lord: that you no longer <margin>Romans 1.</margin> conduct yourselves as the other foreigners <note>Gentiles</note> conduct themselves, in the vanity of their minds, darkened in spirit, alienated from the divine life because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the numbness of their hearts; who, having become calloused, have given themselves over to lust, greedily committing every obscenity. But you did not learn Christ in this way, if indeed you heard Him and were taught by Him (as the truth is in Jesus) to put off the old man (which was your former way of life), who <margin>Romans 6. Col. 3. Heb. 11.</margin> perishes through deceitful desires, and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and to put on the new man, created by God in righteousness and true piety. Therefore, having put away <margin>c. specifically the religious spirit.</margin> falsehood, speak the truth with one another, since <margin>1 Peter 1.</margin> we are members of one another. Be angry in such a way that you do not sin: do not let the sun set on your anger, and do not <margin>Zechariah 8. Psalm 4.</margin> give a place to the devil. Let him who stole steal no more, but rather let him labor with the work of his hands for good things, so that he may <margin>Jonah 4. d. lest through anger a place be given to the devil for calling back and forth.</margin> have something to share with those in need. Let no corrupt speech come out of your mouth: but if any is good for the instruction that is needed, so that it may confer a benefit on the listeners; and do not grieve the holy spirit of God, by which you were sealed for the day of liberation. Let all bitterness, and hatred, and anger, and clamor, and evil speaking, and finally all vice, be removed from you: and be <margin>Col. 3.</margin> kind to one another, merciful, forgiving one another, just as God forgave you in Christ.

TO THE PHILIPPIANS.

# THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE
## TO THE PHILIPPIANS.

### CHAPTER I.

PAUL and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, together with the bishops and ministers: grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
<margin>2 Corinthians 2; Galatians 1; Ephesians 1; 1 Peter 1.</margin>
I give thanks to my God whenever the memory of you comes to mind, always making my prayer for you all with joy in every one of my supplications, because you have shared in the gospel from the first day until now. I am confident of this: that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ. Just as it is right for me to feel this way about you all, because I have you in my heart both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel; you are all, I say, joint-partakers of the grace bestowed upon me. For God is my witness how <margin>a. Christian</margin> ᵃ I long for you all with a deep affection worthy of Jesus Christ. And this I pray: that your love may overflow more and more in knowledge and all perception, so that you may approve what is excellent, that you may be sincere and blameless for the day of Christ, filled with the fruits of righteousness which come through Jesus Christ to the glory and praise of God. Now I want you to know, brothers, that my circumstances have actually turned out for the progress of the gospel, so that my chains in Christ have become well-known throughout the whole <margin>b. of the court.</margin> ᵇ praetorium <note>original: "praetorium" — referring to the headquarters of the Roman imperial guard or the governor’s palace</note> and to everyone else. As a result, many of the brothers in the Lord, gaining confidence from my chains, dare all the more fearlessly to speak the word. Some, indeed, preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill. Those who do so out of ambition do not proclaim Christ purely, <margin>c. Because the more Christians there are, the greater will be the hatred of my enemies toward me. d. While I live.</margin> ᶜ thinking to add affliction to my chains. But the others do so out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the Gospel. But what does it matter? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed; and in this I rejoice, and will continue to rejoice. For I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ. According to my earnest expectation and hope, I shall be put to shame in nothing, but with all boldness of speech, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death. <margin>d. While I live.</margin> ᵈ For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain. But if living in the body allows for fruitful work, I do not know which I should choose. I am torn between the two: I desire to depart and be with Christ, for that would be far better; yet to remain in the body is more necessary for your sake. Confident in this, I know that I will remain and continue with you all for your progress

<column-break/>

and the joy of faith, so that through me your boasting in Christ Jesus may abound when I come to you again. Only conduct your lives in a manner worthy of the Gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear of you: that you stand firm in one spirit, with one mind struggling together for the faith of the gospel, and not being terrified in any way by your adversaries. This is a sign of destruction for them, but of salvation for you—and that from God. For it has been granted to you, not only to believe in Christ, but also to suffer for his sake, having the same struggle which you saw in me and now hear to be in me.

### CHAPTER II.

Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the spirit, if any compassion and mercy, fulfill my joy by being of the same mind, having the same love, being in full accord and of one mind. Do nothing through rivalry or conceit, but in humility let each count the other better than himself, looking out not only for his own interests, but also for the interests of others. For you ought to be so minded as was Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. And being found in human form, he humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore God has highly exalted him and given him a name which is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. Therefore, my beloved, as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling. For it is God who, according to his good will, works in you both to will and to accomplish. TO THE PHILIPPIANS.

<margin>
He came to the Philippians.
</margin>
...But I thought it necessary to send to you your messenger <note>original: "apostolum" — here used in the sense of a messenger or envoy</note> and the substitute for my service, since he was longing for you all and was distressed because you had heard he was sick. Indeed, he was so ill that he was close to death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow. Therefore, I sent him all the more eagerly, so that by seeing him again you may rejoice, and I may be less sorrowful. Therefore, receive him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such men in honor; for because of the work of Christ he came so near to death, having no regard for his own life, so that he might make up for the lack of your service toward me.

## CHAPTER III.

Furthermore, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It does not weary me to write the same things to you, and for you it is safe. Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of the "mutilators" <note>original: "concisos" — a pun playing on "circumcision," suggesting that those who insist on it are merely cutting the flesh</note>. For we are the circumcision, who worship God by divine inspiration and glory in Christ Jesus, not relying on the flesh: although I myself might have reason to 
<margin>Acts 23, Galatians 1, Acts 9.</margin>
rely on the flesh. If anyone else thinks he can have confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee; according to zeal, a persecutor of the church; according to the righteousness found in the law, blameless. But those things that were gains to me, I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ. Indeed, I count all things as loss because of the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and I count them as dung <note>original: "stercoribus" — refuse or waste</note>, so that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having my own righteousness, which depends on the law, but that which is placed in faith in Christ, a righteousness from God based on faith—to know him and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, while being conformed to his death, if somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead. Not that I have already attained it or am already perfect, but I press on to take hold of it, just as I have been taken hold of by Christ Jesus. Brothers, I do not consider myself to have yet attained it; but one thing I do: forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead, I press on toward the goal, for the prize to which I have been called from above by God through Christ Jesus. Therefore, let those of us who are perfect think this way; and if in anything
<margin>1 Corinthians 4, ch. 11.</margin>
you think otherwise, God will reveal that to you as well. In the meantime, let us hold true to what we have attained: let us live by the same rule. Be imitators of me, brothers, and observe those who conduct themselves as we do—for many (of whom I have often told you, and now tell you even weeping) conduct themselves as 
<margin>Romans 16.</margin>
enemies of the cross of Christ. Their end is destruction; their god is their belly, and they glory in their shame; they set their minds on earthly things. For our citizenship <note>original: "respublica" — commonwealth or state</note> is in heaven, from which we also await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform our humble body so that it may have the same form as his glorious body, by the power by which he is able to subject all things to himself.

## CHAPTER IV.

Therefore, my brothers, dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and my crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, O beloved. I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to be of the same mind in the Lord. And I ask you also, true companion, help these women who have struggled with me in the gospel, together with Clement and the rest of my colleagues, whose names are in the book of life. Rejoice in the Lord always; and again I say, rejoice. Let your moderation <note>original: "aequitas" — fairness or gentleness</note> be known to all men. The Lord is near. Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God; and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus. Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is gracious, 
<margin>a. If there is anything associated with virtue and praiseworthy,</margin>
if there is any virtue and if there is any praise, think on these things—which you have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me. Do these things, and the God of peace will be with you. But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly that now at last your care for me has flourished again; though you were indeed concerned, you lacked the opportunity. I do not say this because of want; for I have learned to be content with what I have. I know how to be humbled, and I know how to excel; in every place and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my distress. You Philippians also know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I set out from Macedonia, no

church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving <note>original: "rationem expensorum & acceptorum" — an accounting of expenses and receipts</note> except you alone, who sent what I needed to Thessalonica more than once. Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the profit that may abound to your account. I have all things and abound; I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent—a sweet fragrance, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God. ### CHAPTER II.

->TO THE THESSALONIANS.<-

...there is no need for us to say anything. For they themselves report concerning us what kind of reception we had among you, and how you turned from false gods <note>original: "deastris", a diminutive or derogatory term for idols or minor deities</note> to God, to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus, who defends us from the coming punishment.

## CHAPTER II.

<margin>Galatians 1.</margin> For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain: but even though we had previously suffered evils and insults at Philippi (as you know), nevertheless, through our God, we dared to speak the divine gospel to you freely, with much struggle. For our exhortation did not spring from error, or impurity, or fraud; but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing men, but God, who searches our hearts. For we never used flattering speech, as you know; nor did we do anything out of greed; God is witness; nor did we seek glory from men, neither from you nor from others. And although we could have been a burden as apostles of Christ, yet we were so gentle among you, just as a nurse cherishes her own children, that out of our longing for you we were willing to impart to you not only the divine gospel, but even our own souls; so dear were you to us. For you remember, brothers, our labor and weariness, for <margin>2 Thessalonians 3, Acts 20.</margin> working night and day (so as not to be a burden to any of you), we proclaimed the divine gospel among you. You are witnesses, and God also, how piously, justly, and blamelessly we behaved toward you who believe <note>original: "fidentes", literally "those trusting"</note>, just as you know how we exhorted, comforted, and warned each one of you, as a father does his children, so that you would walk in a way worthy of God, who calls you into his kingdom and glory. Therefore, we also give thanks to God continually, because when you received the word of God which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but (as it truly is) the word of God, which is at work in you who believe. For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God which are in Judea in Christ Jesus: since you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as we did from the Jews, who killed both the Lord Jesus and their own <margin>Matthew 5, 23; 10, 15.</margin> prophets <note>original: "vates", a classical term for divinely inspired poets or seers</note>, and drove us out; they do not please God and are contrary to all men, forbidding us to speak to the foreigners <note>original: "alienigenas", referring here to the Gentiles</note> so that they might be saved, thus always filling up the measure of their sins; for the ultimate wrath of God has come upon them. But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a short time—in presence, not in heart—endeavored all the more eagerly with great desire to see you face to face. Therefore we wanted to come to you, I, Paul, again and again, but Satan hindered us. For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting? Is it not you in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? For you are our glory and joy.

<column-break/>

## CHAPTER III.

Therefore, when we could endure it no longer, we thought it best to be left behind at Athens alone, and sent Timothy, our brother and God's minister, and our colleague in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and to encourage you concerning your faith, so that no one might be shaken by these calamities. For you yourselves know that we are destined for this. For even when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we would suffer affliction, just as it happened, as you know. For this reason, I could no longer restrain myself and sent to learn of your faith, lest perhaps the tempter had tempted you, and so our labor might have been in vain. But now that Timothy has come to us from you and brought us the good news of your faith and love, and that you always have a good memory of us, desiring to see us just as we also desire to see you. Because of this, we have been comforted concerning you, brothers, in all our distress and adversity through your faith, so that we now truly live, if you stand firm in the Lord. For what thanks can we return to God for you, for all the joy which we feel because of you before our God, praying most earnestly night and day that we might see you face to face and supply what is lacking in your faith? May God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, <margin>1 Thessalonians</margin> prosper our journey to you; and may the Lord make you to increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all, just as we do toward you: so that your hearts may be established in blameless holiness in the sight of God our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.

## CHAPTER IV.

Furthermore then, brothers, we beg and exhort you through the Lord Jesus, that just as you learned from us how you ought to walk and please God, you should excel in this even more. For you know what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus. For this is the will of God and your holiness: that you abstain from sexual immorality, and that <margin>Romans, Ephesians</margin> each one of you should know how to possess his own vessel <note>The "vessel" here refers to one's own body or perhaps a spouse.</note> in holiness and honor, not (as the foreigners <note>original: "alienigenæ", i.e., the Gentiles</note> who do not know God) in the passion of lust; and that no one <margin>Leviticus</margin> should overreach or cheat his brother in business. Since <margin>Genesis</margin> the Lord is the avenger of all these things, as we also told you before and testified. For God has not called us to impurity, but to holiness. Therefore, whoever *rejects* this, rejects not man but God, who gives his Holy Spirit to you. # SECOND EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS.

### CHAPTER I.

PAUL, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians, which is in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. We ought to give immortal thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith grows so much, and the mutual love of all of you so abounds, that we ourselves glory in you in the divine churches, for the patience and faith with which you are endowed in all the persecutions and calamities that you endure. This is an indication that you will attain the kingdom of God by his just judgment, for which you are suffering. Indeed, it is right for God to repay those who afflict you with affliction, and to give rest to you who are afflicted, along with us, when the Lord Jesus shall appear from heaven with his powerful angels <note>original: "genijs", spirits/angels</note> in flaming fire, to inflict punishment <gloss>a</gloss> on those who do not know God, and on those
<margin>a. those who despise God.</margin>
who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. reason, we always pray for you, that God may make you worthy of the state to which you were called, and that he may perfect in you both goodness and the work of faith most willingly and strongly, so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be celebrated in you, and you in him, according to the benevolence of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

<margin>a. he exists now, and then will be his time.</margin>
time; for the mystery of lawlessness <note>original: "sceleris mysterium"</note> is already at work. He who now holds it back will continue to do so until he is taken out of the way; and then finally that wicked one will appear, whom the Lord will consume with the breath
<margin>Isaiah 11</margin>
of his mouth and destroy with the brightness of his coming. The coming of this wicked one, by the work of Satan, will be accompanied by every kind of false omen, portent, and miracle, and with every deception of wickedness among those who are perishing, because they did not accept the love of the truth by which they might be saved. Therefore we give thanks to God continually, because when you received the word of God which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but (as it truly is) the word of God, which is at work in you who believe. For you, brothers, became imitators of the divine churches which are in Judea, as far as Christ Jesus is concerned; for you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as we did from the Jews, who killed both the Lord Jesus and their own prophets <note>original: "vates," a classical term for seers or divinely inspired poets</note>, and drove us out, and they do not

For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting? Is it not you in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, at his coming? For you are our glory and joy.

### CHAPTER III.

And so when we could no longer endure it, it seemed good to us to be left alone in Athens, and to send Timothy, our brother and a minister of God, and our colleague in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and to remind you of your faith, so that no one should be shaken by these calamities. ## CHAPTER I.

We ought to give immortal thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith grows so much, and the mutual love of you all overflows, so that we ourselves glory in you in the divine churches, because of the patience and faith with which you are endowed in all your persecutions and calamities which you endure. This is an indication that you will attain the divine kingdom by the righteous judgment of God, for which you suffer. Indeed, it is just that God should repay affliction to those who afflict you, and to you who are afflicted, rest along with us, when the Lord Jesus appears from heaven with the spirits <note>original: "genijs," meaning angels</note> of his power, in flaming fire,

These will suffer the penalty of eternal destruction from the Lord and from his glorious power, when he comes on that day to be glorified in his saints and to be marveled at among all believers, because our testimony to you was believed. For 
<margin>Colossians 1, 1 Thessalonians 3</margin>
this reason we always pray for you, that God may make you worthy of the state to which you were called, and that he may fulfill every desire for goodness and the work of faith both most willingly and powerfully, so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be celebrated in you, and you in him, according to the benevolence of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

<margin>Matthew 24, Mark 13, Luke 21, Ephesians 5, Daniel 9</margin>

...God [sends] a power of error so great that they believe a lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but delighted in wickedness might be condemned. But we ought to give immortal thanks to God for you, brothers, beloved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation, through the sanctification of the spirit and faith in the truth, to which he called you through our gospel, for the purpose of seeking the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. May our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who out of his favor loved us and gave us eternal consolation and good hope, stabilize your souls and confirm you in every good word and work.

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>Not all are faithful and true Christians.</margin>
Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the Lord’s teaching may run and be glorified, just as it is among you, and that we may be defended from troublesome and evil men: for faith is not for everyone. But the Lord, as he is faithful, will confirm you and protect you from the Evil One. And indeed, we have confidence concerning you through the Lord, that you are doing and will do the things we command you. May the Lord direct your souls to divine love and Christian patience. We command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to avoid every brother who carries himself in a disorderly way <note>original: "intemperanter," meaning without restraint or discipline</note>, not according to the teaching <note>original: "institutione"</note> he received from us. For you yourselves know how we ought to be imitated, since we did not behave ourselves in a disorderly way among you, nor did we receive food for free from anyone, but performed laborious work night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you. Not because we did not have the right, but so that we might offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate. For even while we were there, we declared this to you: if anyone will not work, he should not eat. For we hear that some among you live immodestly, doing nothing but being busybodies <note>original: "superuacaneā agere," literally 'doing superfluous things'</note>. To these we command and exhort them through our Lord Jesus Christ, that by working quietly they seek their own food. But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing right. If anyone does not obey our words, mark him by letter and abstain from his company, so that he may be ashamed; yet do not treat him as an enemy, but correct him as a brother. May the Lord of peace himself give you peace always and in every way. The Lord be with you all. The greeting is in my own hand, Paul’s, which is the sign in all my letters. Thus I write:

## THE APOSTLE PAUL’S
### FIRST EPISTLE TO
### Timothy.

### CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>Large decorative woodcut initial 'P' featuring intricate foliate and floral designs within a square frame.</image-desc>
<margin>On the Christian religion.</margin>
<margin>2 Corinthians 1.</margin>
<margin>Galatians 1.</margin>
<margin>Ephesians 1.</margin>
<margin>1 Peter 1.</margin>
PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the command of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope, to Timothy, my true son in the faith: favor, mercy, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, our Lord. Just as I urged you when I was setting out for Macedonia, remain in Ephesus, so that you may command certain people not to follow other doctrines, nor to pay attention to fables and endless genealogies <note>original: "antiquitates," literally 'antiquities'</note>, which produce questions rather than divine instruction in faith. Now the goal of the commandments is love, proceeding from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a faith not faked; wandering from these, some have turned aside into the vanity of speech, wanting to be teachers of the law, though they do not know what they are saying or what they affirm. We know indeed that the law is good,
<margin>Romans 7</margin>
<margin>Galatians 4</margin>
<margin>Exodus 20.</margin>
<margin>Leviticus 18</margin>
<margin>1 Corinthians 5</margin>
<margin>1 Timothy 5</margin>
<margin>He does rightly, where he uses it rightly.</margin>
if one uses it lawfully, understanding this: that the law was not made for the righteous, but for the wicked and rebellious, the impious and the unrighteous, the irreligious and profane, for those who kill fathers and mothers, for murderers, the unchaste, sodomites <note>original: "cinaedis," a term for those of 'soft' or 'shameful' morals</note>, kidnappers <note>original: "plagiarijs," those who steal people into slavery</note>, liars, perjurers, and if there is anything else contrary to sound doctrine, which is found in the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was entrusted to me. And I give thanks to him who gave me strength, Christ Jesus our Lord, who considered me so faithful as to appoint me to this ministry, though I was previously a blasphemer against God,
<margin>Acts 9</margin>
<margin>Galatians 1</margin>
and an enemy, and insolent. But I was shown mercy because I acted ignorantly, being without faith; but the benefit of our Lord was most excellent, with faith and love placed in Christ Jesus. It is a certain thing and worthy of all approval, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save the guilty <note>original: "fontes," a legal term for those at fault or sinners</note>, of whom I am the first. But for this reason mercy was granted to me, so that in me first, Jesus Christ might display his supreme clemency as an example to those who would believe in him for eternal life. Now to the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honor and glory forever and ever, Amen. I commend this command to you, son Timothy, according to the prophecies previously made about you, so that as they require, you may wage a noble warfare, having faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and so made shipwreck of their faith—among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan, so that they may unlearn their impious speech.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Instruction.</margin>
I exhort therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men, for kings and all those who hold power, so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life with all piety and gravity. ...he gave himself as the price of liberation for all, a matter <margin>1 Timothy 1</margin> to be testified to in its own time, for which I have been appointed a herald and an Apostle. Likewise, that women adorn themselves in modest clothing with shamefacedness and sobriety, not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or expensive clothing, but as <margin>1 Corinthians 14, Ephesians 5</margin> becomes women professing godliness through good works. Let a woman learn in silence with all obedience. I do not permit a woman to teach, nor to claim authority for herself over a man, but to be silent. For Adam <margin>Genesis 3</margin> was formed first, then Eve; and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, being deceived, fell into transgression. Nevertheless, she will be saved through the procreation of children, if she remains in faith, and charity, and holiness with sobriety.

### CHAPTER III.

This is a certain thing: if anyone seeks the office of a bishop, he desires a good work. Therefore, a bishop must be blameless, <margin>Titus 1</margin> the husband of one wife, sober, temperate, modest, hospitable, fit for teaching, not given to wine, not a striker, not greedy for filthy lucre, but fair-minded, far from brawling and avarice, managing his own house well, having children who are obedient with all gravity. For if anyone does not know how to manage his own house, how will he take care of the church of God? He should not be a new convert, lest being puffed up, he fall into the accusation of the Devil. He must also be commended by the honorable testimony of <margin>a Of those who are not Christians, regarding the Christian religion, which is a secret matter.</margin> ^a outsiders, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the Devil. Likewise, ministers <note>original: "ministri," referring to deacons</note> must be serious, not <margin>b That is, in that [mystery].</margin> double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for filthy lucre, keeping ^b the secret of the faith in a good conscience. And let these first be proven, then let them serve as ministers being blameless. ^c Likewise, the wives must be serious, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the ministers be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. For those who have served well as ministers obtain for themselves a distinguished standing, and great freedom in the faith which is placed in Christ Jesus. I write these things to you, hoping to come to you shortly, so that, if I am delayed, you may know how it is necessary to behave in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. <margin>a The Christian religion.</margin> And truly, great is the ^a secret of godliness: God was manifested in the body, was approved by the spirit, was seen by heavenly spirits <note>original: "genijs," a classical term for spirits or angels</note>, was preached to the nations, was believed in the world, and was received up into glory.

<margin>2 Timothy 3, 2 Peter 3, Jude</margin>
However, the Spirit expressly says that in the final times some will fall away from the faith, being devoted to deceptive spirits and the doctrines of demons, through the hypocrisy of men who speak lies, having their conscience seared as with a hot iron, forbidding to contract marriages, and commanding to abstain <margin>Ecclesiastes 39</margin> from foods, which God created so that those who believe and understand the truth might eat them with thanksgiving; namely, that everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected which is taken with thanksgiving, for it is purified by the words of God and prayer. ### CHAPTER V.

Do not rebuke an elder <note>original: "seniorem," meaning an older man</note>, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brothers; the older women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity. Honor widows who are truly widows. But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let her first learn to practice godliness toward her own family and to give back a recompense to her parents. For this is honorable and acceptable to the Lord. <margin>Above, chapter 2.</margin> A true widow, being desolate, has hope in God, and stays occupied in supplications and prayers night and <margin>a Namely, to God.</margin> day. But the widow who indulges in pleasures is ^a dead while she lives. And proclaim these things, so that they may be without fault. But if anyone does not have a care for his own, and especially for those of his household, <margin>b The Christian religion.</margin> he has denied ^b the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. Let a widow ^c be chosen <margin>c Namely, for serving the saints. Acts 6.</margin> who is not less than sixty years old, who has been the wife of one man, well-spoken of for good deeds, if she has brought up children, if she has practiced hospitality, if she has washed the feet of the saints, if she has helped those in trouble, and if she has followed every good work. But <margin>d Do not admit them for service.</margin> ^d reject the younger widows. For after they have begun to grow wanton, rejecting Christ, they want to marry, being condemned because they have broken their first faith. Added to this, being idle, they learn to wander about through houses; and not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they should not. Therefore, I want the younger widows to marry, to give effort to bearing children, to rule the household, and to give no occasion to the adversary for slander. For some have already turned aside after Satan. If any faithful man or woman has widows, let them help them, and let not the Church be burdened, so that it may suffice for those who are truly widows. Let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor <note>original: "gemino præmio," literally 'double reward' or 'double payment'</note>, especially those who labor in the word and doctrine. <margin>Deuteronomy 25, 1 Corinthians 9, Deuteronomy 19</margin> For the scripture says: "Do not muzzle the ox that treads out the grain," and "The laborer is worthy of his reward." Do not admit an accusation against an elder unless there are two or three witnesses. Rebuke those who sin in the presence of everyone, so that the others may be struck with fear. I charge you in the sight of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen heavenly spirits <note>original: "lectorum geniorum," meaning the elect angels</note>, that you carry out these things without any prejudice, doing nothing through favoritism. Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, <margin>e If you admit a corrupt person, his sins will be imputed to you.</margin> ^e nor participate in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.

## OF PAUL THE APOSTLE 
## TO TIMOTHY.

### CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>Woodcut ornamental initial 'P' depicting a figure, likely St. Paul, standing in a landscape holding a sword (the symbol of his martyrdom) and a book (the Word of God).</image-desc>
PAUL, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life placed in Christ Jesus, to Timothy, my dear son: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our <margin>10</margin> <margin>2 Corinthians 1; Galatians 1; 1 Peter 1; Romans 1</margin> Lord. I give thanks to God, whom I worship with a pure conscience after the manner of my ancestors, because I hold a constant memory of you in my prayers night and day, desiring to see you, mindful of your tears, so that I may be filled with joy, calling to mind your unfeigned faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and (as I am persuaded) is in you also. For this reason, I remind you to stir up the divine gift which you were <margin>20</margin> <margin>Romans 8</margin> endowed with through the laying on of my hands. For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of strength, and of love, and of sobriety. Therefore, do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me, his prisoner; but together endure the hardships of the Gospel by the power of God, who saved us and <margin>Titus 3</margin> called us to a holy state, not because of our works, but because of his own decree and benefit, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before all the eternity of time, but is now revealed by the coming of our <margin>30</margin> Savior Jesus Christ, who has both abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the Gospel, for which I was appointed a herald to the foreign nations <note>original: "externarum gentium," usually translated as 'Gentiles'</note>, and an Apostle, and a teacher; for <margin>1 Timothy 1</margin> which reason I suffer these things; but I am not ashamed. For I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to keep <gloss>a</gloss> my deposit <margin>a. Mine, even as far as it pertains to me.</margin> until 그 day. Hold fast the pattern of sound words which you heard from me, with faith <margin>40</margin> and love placed in Christ Jesus. Keep that excellent deposit through the Holy Spirit dwelling in us. All those in Asia have turned away from me (this you know), among whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes. May the Lord grant mercy to the family of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains; rather, after he arrived in Rome, he sought me out diligently and found me. May the Lord grant that he find mercy from the Lord on 그 day. And how much he helped at Ephesus, you know well enough.

### CHAPTER II.

Therefore you, my son, be strong in the benefit placed in Christ Jesus; and the things which you heard from me before many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who shall be fit to teach others also. You, therefore, endure hardships as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No one serving as a soldier entangles himself in the affairs of life, so that he may please the leader of the army. Likewise, if anyone competes, he is not crowned unless he has competed according to the rules. <margin>1 Corinthians 9</margin> The hardworking farmer ought to be the first to receive the fruits. Understand what I say: may the Lord give you industry in all things. Remember that Jesus Christ [rose] from the dead...
