## RUDOLF GUALTHER
## of Zurich <note>Rudolf Gualther (1519–1586) was a major figure in the Protestant Reformation in Zurich and the son-in-law of Huldrych Zwingli</note>.

Recently, when Orpheus <note>The legendary Greek musician whose music was so beautiful it could charm animals and move stones</note> had seen these harmonies of Sixtus <note>Sixtus Birck, also known as Xystus Betulius, the author of the concordance</note>,
He uttered such sounds from his mouth with a groan:
"Woe is me! Who hereafter will marvel at this sweet-sounding
Cithara <note>A professional version of the lyre</note>, and the talkative strings of my lyre?
What does it profit to have drawn wild bears from the mountains,
And for the forests to have stood amazed at my charming sounds?
I see a greater work, in which a second Orpheus
Silently harmonizes words sought from the sacred books.
We, therefore, soothed foolish ears with singing;
He draws the minds of men and their hard hearts.
We gave trifles and the false dreams of the Sages <note>original: "Sophorum," referring to worldly philosophers or the "wise" of antiquity</note>;
He sounds the voices of God and His sacred words.
As much, then, as heaven towers above all the earth,
So much greater also will his glory be."
He spoke, and in his anger he broke both cithara and lyre,
And cast the sounding plectrum <note>A small tool used to pluck or strum the strings of an instrument</note> from his sorrowful hand.
Therefore, will anyone blame your labors, Sixtus?
And will there be anyone who disapproves of your daring?
Believe me, such a person would dare to pluck at the divine books themselves,
And tear them apart with a cruel hand.

<summary>A commendatory Latin poem by Rudolf Gualther using the myth of Orpheus to argue that Sixtus Birck's biblical concordance is a higher form of 'harmony' than any secular art. Gualther claims that while music charms the ears and animals, Birck’s work on the Word of God transforms the human heart and mind.</summary>

### THE PRINTER TO THE READER.

Since, during the printing of this book, it was discovered that a few entries had accidentally crept in out of alphabetical order here and there, and yet, due to the pressing necessity of the printing process, they could no longer be placed in their proper alphabetical sections, we considered it worthwhile to list them right here at the very threshold of the work. We do this rather than giving anyone an opportunity for criticism, or failing to abundantly satisfy the needs of the reader (at least regarding these specific entries). Therefore, Reader, take this effort of ours in good part, and may you happily enjoy the treasury offered here.

¶ <term>Aeneas</term> <note>original Greek: Αἰνείας (Aineias)</note>, a proper name.

<margin>Acts 28</margin> for concerning this **sect**

# CONCORDANCE

-># CONCORDANCE <-
<note>original: Σ Υ Μ Φ Ω Ν Ι Α (Symphōnia)</note>

### ¶ Two hundred <gloss>original: διακόσιοι, Latin: ducenti</gloss>
<margin>Mark 6</margin> Shall we go and buy **two hundred** denarii worth of bread?
<margin>John 6</margin> **Two hundred** denarii worth of bread is not enough for them.
<margin>Acts 23</margin> Prepare **two hundred** soldiers.

### ¶ Two hundred seventy-six <gloss>original: διακόσια ἑβδομήκοντα ἕξ, Latin: CCLXXVI</gloss>
<margin>Acts 27</margin> All the souls together were **two hundred seventy-six**.

### ¶ To hear a case <gloss>original: Διακούω, Latin: audio causam</gloss>
<margin>Acts 23</margin> I will **hear your case** when your accusers also arrive.

### ¶ To discern or judge <gloss>original: Διακρίνω, Latin: dijudico, æstimo</gloss>

<margin>1 Cor. 11</margin> Not **discerning** the body of the Lord.
<margin>1 Cor. 14</margin> And let the others **judge**.

### ¶ To judge or waver <gloss>original: Διακρίνομαι, Latin: dijudico</gloss>
<margin>Rom. 14</margin> But he who **doubts** <note>or "wavers," literally "judges between options"</note> if he eats.

### ¶ To be judged or condemned <gloss>original: Διακρίνομαι, Latin: dijudicor, damnor</gloss>
<margin>Jas. 2</margin> And have you not **made distinctions** among yourselves?
<margin>Jude</margin> On some have mercy, **who are in doubt**.

### ¶ To doubt or hesitate <gloss>original: Διακρίνομαι, Latin: dubito, hesito</gloss>
<margin>Matt. 21</margin> If you have faith, and do not **doubt**.
<margin>Mark 11</margin> And does not **doubt** in his heart.
<margin>Acts 10</margin> Go with them, **doubting** nothing.
<margin>Rom. 4</margin> He did not **waver** at the promise of God through unbelief.
<margin>Jas. 1</margin> For he who **doubts** is like a wave of the sea.

### ¶ To dispute or contend <gloss>original: Διακρίνομαι, Latin: discepto, certo</gloss>
<margin>Acts 11</margin> Those of the circumcision **disputed** with him.
<margin>Jude</margin> When he **disputed** with the devil and argued.

### ¶ Discernment or distinction <gloss>original: Διάκρισις, Latin: dijudicatio, discretio</gloss>
<margin>Rom. 14</margin> Not for **disputes** <note>or "deciding"</note> over opinions.
<margin>Heb. 5</margin> Because of practice have their senses trained for the **discernment** of good and evil.

### ¶ To prevent or hinder <gloss>original: Διακωλύω, Latin: prohibeo</gloss>
<margin>Matt. 3</margin> But John **tried to prevent** him, saying...

### ¶ To reason, argue, or speak <gloss>original: Διαλέγομαι, Latin: dissero, disputo, loquor</gloss>
<margin>Acts 17</margin> For three Sabbaths he **reasoned** with them from the Scriptures.
<margin>Acts 18</margin> He **reasoned** in the synagogue.

# OF THE NEW TESTAMENT
<note>original: ΚΑΙΝΗΣ ΔΙΑΘΗΚΗΣ (Kainēs Diathēkēs). This is the Greek title for the New Testament.</note>
<meta>Catchword: ap- (indicating the start of the next page's word, likely "apokalypsis" or "apostolos")</meta>

-> **To serve / To be a slave** <-
<note>original: δουλεύω (douleuō). This verb describes the act of serving as a slave or being in a state of bondage.</note>

"I have **served** you for so many years, and I never disobeyed your command." Luke 15
"No **servant** can **serve** two masters." Luke 16
"You cannot **serve** God and Mammon." <note>Mammon is a Syriac term for wealth or profit.</note> Ibid.
"And we have never been **enslaved** to anyone." John 8
"The nation to whom they will be in **bondage**, I will judge," said God. Acts 7
"How I was with you the whole time, **serving** the Lord." Acts 20
"So that we might no longer be **enslaved** to sin." Romans 6
"I myself **serve** the law of God with my mind." Romans 7
"So that we **serve** in the newness of the spirit." Romans 7
"The older shall **serve** the younger." Romans 9
"**Serving** the time." <note>original: τῷ καιρῷ δουλεύοντες. Some ancient manuscripts read "serving the Lord" (kyriō) while others read "serving the time" (kairō), as seen here.</note> Romans 12

# NEW TESTAMENT

<center>NEW TESTAMENT</center>

¶ **Praise** <note>original: Έπαινος, Latin: laus</note>
**whose praise is not of men, but of God.** Rom. 2
**and you shall have praise from the same** Rom. 13
**whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches** 2. Cor. 8
**unto the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory** Eph. 1
**according to the good pleasure of his will, to the praise of the glory of his grace.** Eph. 1
**that we should be to the praise of his glory.** Eph. 1
**which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.** Philip. 1
**if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise** Philip. 4
**unto praise and honor and glory.** 1. Pet. 1
**for the praise of them that do well** 1. Pet. 2

¶ **Lift up** <note>original: Επαίρω, Latin: extollo, eleuo</note>
**and when he had lifted up his eyes** Matth. 17
**Lift up your eyes** Ioan. 4
**When Jesus then lifted up his eyes** Ioan. 6
**he that eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me** Ioan. 13
**and lifted up his eyes to heaven.** Ioan. 17
**lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting** 1. Tim. 2

¶ **Be exalted / Lifted up** <note>original: Επαίρομαι, Latin: extollor</note>
**and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God** 2. Cor. 10
**if a man exalt himself** 2. Cor. 11

¶ **Be ashamed** <note>original: Επαισχύνομαι, Latin: pudet me</note>
**Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this generation** Mar. 8
**For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed.** Luc. 9
**For I am not ashamed of the gospel.** Rom. 1
**What fruit had you then in those things whereof you are now ashamed?** Rom. 6
**Be not you therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord** 2. Tim. 1
**and was not ashamed of my chain.** 2. Tim. 1
**he is not ashamed to call them brothers.** Heb. 2
**wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God** Heb. 11

¶ **Beg** <note>original: Επαιτέω, Latin: mendico</note>
**to beg I am ashamed** Luc. 16

¶ **Follow after / Accompany** <note>original: Επακολουθέω, Latin: subsequor</note>
**and confirming the word with signs following** Mar. 16
**and some they follow after** 1. Tim. 5
**if she has diligently followed every good work.** 1. Tim. 5
**that you should follow his steps.** 1. Pet. 2

¶ **Hear / Answer** <note>original: Επακούω, Latin: exaudio</note>
**I have heard you in a time accepted** 2. Cor. 6

<column-break/>

¶ **Necessary** <note>original: Επανάγκης, an adverb used in place of an adjective; Latin: necessarium</note>
**than these necessary things** Act. 15

¶ **Put out / Thrust out** <note>original: Επανάγω, Latin: abduco</note>
**to thrust out a little from the land** Luc. 5

¶ **Return** <note>original: Επανάγω, Latin: reuertor</note>
**Now in the morning as he returned into the city,** Matth. 21

¶ **Remind / Put in mind** <note>original: Επαναμιμνήσκω, Latin: commonefacio</note>
**as putting you in mind because of the grace** Rom. 15

¶ **Rest upon** <note>original: Επαναπαύομαι, Latin: requiesco</note>
**your peace shall rest upon it** Luc. 10
**and rest in the law** Rom. 2

¶ **Rise up against** <note>original: Επανίσταμαι, Latin: insurgo</note>
**children shall rise up against their parents.** Mar. 13

¶ **Correction** <note>original: Επανόρθωσις, Latin: correctio</note>
**for correction, for instruction.** 2. Tim. 3

¶ **Above / Over / More than** <note>original: Επάνω, Latin: supra, pluris</note>
**stood over where the young child was** Matth. 2
**they set him thereon [above them]** Matth. 21
**and put on them [above them] their clothes** Matth. 21
**whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it** Matth. 23
**and set up over his head his accusation written** Matth. 27
**and sat upon it** Matth. 28
**it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence** Mar. 14
**he that comes from above is above all.** Ioan. 3
**he that comes from above is above all.** Ioan. 3 <note>This verse is repeated in the original text.</note>
**After that, he was seen of above five hundred brothers at once** 1. Cor. 15

¶ **Relieve / Assist** <note>original: Επαρκέω, Latin: supporto</note>
**that it may relieve them that are widows indeed** 1. Tim. 5
**If any man or woman that believes have widows, let them relieve them** 1. Tim. 5
**if she has relieved the afflicted** 1. Tim. 5

¶ **Province** <note>original: Επαρχία, Latin: prouincia, praefectura</note>
**he asked of what province he was** Act. 23
**Now when Festus was come into the province** Act. 25

¶ **Habitation / Dwelling** <note>original: Επαυλις, Latin: commoratio</note>
**Let his habitation be desolate.** Act. 1

¶ **The next day / Following day** <note>original: Επαύριον, Latin: postridie, postero die</note>
**The next day John sees Jesus coming unto him** Ioan. 1
**Again the next day after John stood.** Ioan. 1
**The next day Jesus would go forth into Galilee** Ioan. 1
**The day following, when the people which stood on the other side of the sea** Ioan. 6
**On the next day much people that were come to the feast** Ioan. 12

# CONCORDANCE

¶ **Epaphras**, <note>A proper name; a shortened form of Epaphroditus. He was a collaborator of Paul and likely the founder of the church at Colossae.</note>
as you also learned from Epaphras the beloved — Col. 1
Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, greets you — Col. 4
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner, greets you — Philem.

¶ **To foam out**, <note>original: Ἐπαφρίζω, Latin: despumo (to skim foam or froth)</note>
foaming out their own shame — Jude

¶ **Epaphroditus**, <note>A proper name; a Christian messenger mentioned in the Letter to the Philippians.</note>
Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier — Philip. 2
I am full, having received from Epaphroditus — Philip. 4

¶ **To stir up**, <note>original: Ἐπεγείρω, Latin: concito (to incite or rouse)</note>
they stirred up and poisoned the souls [of the Gentiles] — Acts 14

¶ **Otherwise**, <note>original: Ἐπεὶ ἄρα, Latin: alioqui (in another way)</note>
otherwise your children would be unclean — 1 Cor. 7

¶ **Since**, <note>original: Ἐπειδὴ, Latin: postquam (after or because)</note>
since the world did not know — 1 Cor. 1
for since by man [came death] — 1 Cor. 15
since he was longing for you all and was distressed — Philip. 2

¶ **To look upon**, <note>original: Ἐπείδω, Latin: respicio (to regard), clementiam exhibeo (to show mercy)</note>
in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among men — Luke 1

¶ **Introduction**, <note>original: Ἐπεισαγωγή, Latin: introductio (a bringing in)</note>
the introduction of a better hope — Heb. 7

¶ **Then**, <note>original: Ἔπειτα, Latin: postea (afterwards)</note>
then powers, then gifts of healings — 1 Cor. 12
afterward the spiritual — 1 Cor. 15
then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia — Gal. 1
then we who are alive — 1 Thess. 4
then for the [sins] of the people — Heb. 7

¶ **To stretch out**, <note>original: Ἐπεκτείνομαι, Latin: enitor (to strive or reach forward)</note>
stretching forward to the things that are before — Philip. 3

¶ **Tunic**, <note>original: Ἐπενδύτης, Latin: tunica (an outer garment or cloak)</note>
he wrapped his outer garment around him — John 21

¶ **To be clothed upon**, <note>original: Ἐπενδύομαι, Latin: superinduo (to put on over another garment)</note>
longing to be clothed upon with our dwelling from heaven — 2 Cor. 5

¶ **To ask**, <note>original: Ἐπερωτάω, Latin: interrogo (to question)</note>
they asked him, saying — Matt. 12
they asked him to see a sign from heaven — Matt. 16
the disciples asked him — Matt. 17
one of them, a lawyer, asked him, testing him — [Matt. 22]
while the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus asked them — Ibid. <note>original: Ibid., meaning "in the same place."</note>
nor did anyone dare from that day to ask him any more — Matt. 22
the governor asked him, saying — Matt. 27
he asked him, "What is your name?" — Mark 5

<column-break/>

his disciples asked him about the parable — Mark 7
then the Pharisees and the scribes ask him — Mark 7
and they asked him, saying — Mark 9
and he asked his father something — Ibid.
and Pharisees came and asked him — Mark 10
I also will ask you one question — Mark 11
and they asked him — Mark 12
Peter asked him privately — Mark 13
the high priest, standing up in the midst, asked Jesus — Mark 14
Pilate asked him — Mark 15
they asked him if he had been dead long — Ibid.
let me ask you something — Luke 6
then he asked again — John 18
I became manifest to those who did not ask for me — Rom. 10
let them ask their own husbands at home — 1 Cor. 14

¶ **Appeal**, <note>original: Ἐπερώτημα, Latin: interrogatio (question), responsio (answer), convenientia (agreement). This word in 1 Peter 3:21 is debated; it can mean a pledge, a craving, or an appeal.</note>
but the appeal of a good conscience toward God — 1 Pet. 3

¶ **To come upon**, <note>original: Ἐπέρχομαι, Latin: ingruo (to break in), supervenio (to befall)</note>
so that he might show in the ages to come — Eph. 2
weep and howl for the miseries that are coming upon you — James 5

¶ **To attend to**, <note>original: Ἐπέχω, Latin: attendo (to give heed)</note>
but he gave heed to them — Acts 3
pay attention to yourself and to the teaching — 1 Tim. 4

¶ **To mistreat**, <note>original: Ἐπηρεάζω, Latin: calumnior (to slander or treat spitefully)</note>
pray for those who mistreat you — Matt. 5, Luke 6
those who slandered [you] may be put to shame — 1 Pet. 3

¶ **To mount**, <note>original: Ἐπιβαίνω, Latin: conscendo (to go up onto)</note>
mounted on a donkey and on a colt — Matt. 21

¶ **To belong to**, <note>original: Ἐπιβάλλω, Latin: conveniens (fitting), competens (belonging to)</note>
give me the portion of the estate that falls to me — Luke 15

¶ **To throw on**, <note>original: Ἐπιβάλλω, Latin: injicio (to cast or lay upon)</note>
and they threw their garments on it — Mark 11
not that I may throw a snare upon you — 1 Cor. 7

¶ **To lay hands on**, <note>original: Ἐπιβάλλω τὰς χεῖρας, Latin: injicio manus</note>
they laid hands on Jesus — Matt. 26
and they laid their hands on him — Mark 14
no one laid hands on him — John 7

¶ **To put on**, <note>original: Ἐπιβάλλω, Latin: immitto (to put in or send in)</note>
no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment — Matt. 9

¶ **To add**, <note>original: Ἐπιβάλλω, Latin: adjicio (to add), absolute (used on its own)</note>
and when he thought on it, he wept — Mark 14 <note>The phrase 'epibalon eklaie' is famously difficult to translate; it may mean he began to weep, he covered his head, or he thought back upon his actions.</note>

<margin>Mark 10</margin> it is **easier** for a camel to go through the eye of a needle
<margin>Luke 5</margin> which is **easier**
<margin>Luke 16</margin> but it is **easier** for heaven and earth to pass away
¶ **Reverence**, *piety, fear* <note>original: Εὐλάβεια (Eulabeia); Latin: reuerentia, pietas, metus.</note>
<margin>Hebrews 5</margin> having been heard because of his **reverence**, although he was a son
<margin>Hebrews 12</margin> let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably with godly fear and **reverence**
¶ **Pious**, *devout or religious* <note>original: Εὐλαβής (Eulabēs); Latin: pius, religiosus.</note>
<margin>Luke 2</margin> righteous and **devout**
<margin>Acts 8</margin> **devout** men carried Stephen [to his burial]
<margin>Acts 2</margin> **devout** men from every nation
¶ **To fear**, *to be cautious or stand in awe* <note>original: Εὐλαβέομαι (Eulabeomai); Latin: uereor.</note>
<margin>Acts 23</margin> the commander, **fearing** lest Paul be torn in pieces by them
<margin>Hebrews 11</margin> **being cautious**, he prepared an ark
¶ **To praise**, *to bless (of men toward God)* <note>original: Εὐλογέω (Eulogeō); Latin: laudo.</note>
<margin>Luke 24</margin> praising and **blessing** God
<margin>1 Corinthians 14</margin> since if you **bless** with the spirit
<margin>James 3</margin> with it we **bless** our God and Father.

¶ **To bless**, *to speak well of* <note>original: Εὐλογέω (Eulogeō); Latin: benedico</note>, [used of] God toward mortals
<margin>Mark 10</margin> ...putting his hands on them, he **blessed** them.

<margin>Mat. 14</margin> ...looking up to heaven, he **blessed** [the bread].
<margin>Mark 8</margin> ...and having **blessed** [them], he told them to set them before [the people].
<margin>Mark 6</margin> ...he **blessed**, and broke the loaves.
<margin>Luke 9</margin> ...taking the five loaves, he **blessed** them.
<margin>Luke 24</margin> ...taking the bread, he **blessed** it.

<margin>Heb. 7</margin> ...and he **blessed** him who held the promises.

<margin>Ibid.</margin> <note>Latin: "In the same place."</note> ...by faith Isaac **blessed** Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.

<margin>Gal. 3</margin> ...those of faith **are blessed** with the faithful Abraham.
<margin>Heb. 7</margin> ...the lesser **is blessed** by the greater.

¶ **Blessed**, *the blessed one* <note>original: Εὐλογητὸς (Eulogētos); Latin: benedictus</note>, [used as] a name

<margin>Rom. 9</margin> ...who is over all, God **blessed** forever.

<margin>2 Cor. 1, Ephes. 1</margin> <note>Cross-references for the same phrasing.</note>
<margin>2 Cor. 11</margin> ...who is **blessed** forever.

¶ **Blessed**, *blessed one* <note>original: Εὐλογημένος (Eulogēmenos)</note>, participial form, [referring] to Christ by a title of honor.

¶ **Blessed ones**, [applied] to men
<margin>Mat. 25</margin> ...Come, you **blessed** of my Father.

<column-break/>

¶ **Blessing** <note>original: Εὐλογία (Eulogia); Latin: benedictio</note>
<margin>Rom. 15</margin> ...I shall come in the fullness of the **blessing** of the gospel of Christ.
<margin>Rom. 16</margin> ...and through smooth speech and **flattery** <note>original: εὐλογίας (eulogias), here used in the sense of fair speech.</note> they deceive hearts.
<margin>1 Cor. 10</margin> ...the cup of **blessing** which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ?

<margin>Ephes. 1</margin> ...who has blessed us with every spiritual **blessing**.

<margin>James 3</margin> ...out of the same mouth proceed **blessing** and cursing.
<margin>1 Pet. 3</margin> ...so that you might inherit a **blessing**.
<margin>Rev. 7</margin> ...the **blessing** and the glory.

¶ **Blessing**, *a contribution, a good alms*
<margin>2 Cor. 9</margin> ...and prepare beforehand your previously promised **gift** <note>original: εὐλογίαν (eulogian).</note>

¶ **Generous**, *kind, liberal* <note>original: Εὐμετάδοτος (Eumetadotos)</note>
<margin>1 Tim. 6</margin> ...to be **generous**, willing to share.

<margin>Mat. 19</margin> ...for there are **eunuchs** who were born so from their mother’s womb.

¶ **To be well-disposed**, *benevolent, reconciled* <note>original: Εὐνοέω (Eunoeō)</note>
<margin>Mat. 5</margin> ...be **well-disposed** toward your adversary.

¶ **To have a prosperous journey** <note>original: Εὐοδώομαι (Euodoōmai)</note>
<margin>Rom. 1</margin> ...if by any means now at last I might **have a prosperous journey** by the will [of God].

¶ **To prosper**, *when a matter succeeds happily*
<margin>1 Cor. 16</margin> ...storing up, according as he **prospers**.
<margin>3 John</margin> ...I pray that you **prosper** in all things.

¶ **Euodia**, proper name <note>meaning "good journey" or "fragrance"</note>
<margin>Phil. 4</margin> ...I implore **Euodia**.

¶ **Compliant**, *tractable, easy to persuade* <note>original: Εὐπειθὴς (Eupeithēs)</note>
<margin>James 3</margin> ...then peaceable, gentle, **easy to be entreated**.

# OF THE NEW TESTAMENT

¶ **Perfected**, <note>original: Κατηρτισμένος (Katērtismenos); Latin: *perfectus, integer*. A state of being complete or fully restored.</note> used as a participle.
<margin>Luke 6</margin> but everyone will be perfected, just as the teacher is.
<margin>1 Corinthians 1</margin> but that you might be perfected in the same mind.

¶ **Restoration**, <note>original: Καταρτισμός (Katartismos); Latin: *instauratio*. Refers to the act of equipping or setting something right.</note>
<margin>Ephesians 4</margin> for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry.

¶ **Completion**, <note>original: Κατάρτισις (Katartisis); Latin: *integritas*. The author notes this is a "metaphor from tailors" (metaphora à sartoribus), suggesting the mending of a torn garment.</note>
<margin>2 Corinthians 13</margin> and this we also pray for: your completion.

¶ **To signal with the hand**, <note>original: Κατασείω (Kataseiō); Latin: *manu signum do*. Literally to "shake down" the hand to command silence.</note>
<margin>Acts 12</margin> signaling to them with his hand to be silent.
<margin>Acts 13</margin> Paul stood up, and signaling with his hand [said...].
<margin>Acts 19</margin> but Alexander, signaling with his hand [wished to make a defense].
<margin>Acts 21</margin> he signaled with his hand to the people.

¶ **To demolish**, <note>original: Κατασκάπτω (Kataskaptō); Latin: *subruo*. To dig down or undermine a structure.</note>
<margin>Romans 11</margin> they have demolished your altars.

¶ **To be demolished**, <note>passive form of the above.</note>
<margin>Acts 15</margin> I will rebuild its demolished ruins.

¶ **To prepare**, <note>original: Κατασκευάζω (Kataskeuazō); Latin: *propero, paro*. To make ready in advance.</note>

<margin>Mark 1</margin> who will prepare your way before you.

¶ **To build**, <note>the same Greek verb Κατασκευάζω, but in the sense of construction; Latin: *fabrico, construo*.</note>

<margin>Luke 1</margin> to make ready for the Lord a people prepared.

<margin>Hebrews 3</margin> for every house is built by someone.
<margin>1 Peter 3</margin> in the days of Noah, while [the ark] was being built.

¶ **To nest**, <note>original: Κατασκηνόω (Kataskēnoō); Latin: *nidum construo* (to build a nest) or *nidulor*. Literally to "pitch a tent" or dwell.</note>

<margin>Mark 4</margin> so that the birds of heaven are able to nest under its shade.
<margin>Luke 13</margin> the birds of heaven nested in the branches.

# CONCORDANCE

¶ <term>Service</term> <note>original: "Λειτουργία" (Leitourgia). In Greek, this referred to a public work or duty performed for the state, which the New Testament writers adapted to describe religious or charitable service.</note>, priesthood, priestly office
The days of his service were completed. Luke 1

¶ <term>Service</term>, ministry, office
For the administration of this service not only supplies the needs of the saints... 2 Cor. 9
That he might fill up what was lacking in your service toward me. Philip. 2
Upon the sacrifice and service of your faith. Phil. 2
And likewise he sprinkled with blood all the vessels of the service. Heb. 9

¶ <term>Minister</term> <note>original: "Λειτουργός" (Leitourgos)</note>, priest, administrator; regarding Christ:
A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle. Heb. 8

¶ Minister; regarding angels:
And his ministers a flame of fire. Heb. 1

¶ Minister; regarding the apostleship:
That I might be a minister of Jesus Christ. Rom. 15

¶ Minister; regarding the magistracy:
For they are ministers of God. Rom. 13

¶ Assistant or provider:
A messenger and minister to my need. Phil. 2

¶ <term>Ministering</term> <note>original: "Λειτουργικός" (Leitourgikos)</note>, serving:
Are they not all ministering spirits? Heb. 1

¶ <term>Towel</term> <note>original: "Λέντιον" (Lention), a Greek transliteration of the Latin "linteum."</note>, linen cloth, <note>original: "latina vox"</note> a Latin word:
And taking a towel, he girded himself. John 13

¶ <term>Lacking</term> <note>original: "Λείπει" (Leipei)</note>, is absent, fails:
One thing you still lack: sell all that you have. Luke 18
That you might set in order the things that are lacking. Tit. 1

¶ <term>To be in need</term> <note>original: "Λείπομαι" (Leipomai)</note>, to be destitute, to be diminished:
If any of you lacks wisdom. Jas. 1
Lacking in nothing. Jas. 1
And they are lacking in daily food. Jas. 2

¶ <term>Scale</term> <note>original: "Λέπις" (Lepis)</note>, flake:
There fell from his eyes something like scales. Acts 9

¶ <term>Leprosy</term> <note>original: "Λέπρα" (Lepra)</note>:
Immediately his leprosy was cleansed. Matt. 8
Immediately the leprosy departed from him. Luke 5

¶ <term>Leper</term> <note>original: "Λεπρός" (Lepros)</note>, a person with a skin disease:

<meta>This page continues the Greek concordance of the New Testament, specifically focusing on the term "logos" (word, speech, account). # THE NEW TESTAMENT

¶ **Memory**, <note>original: Μνήμη (mnēmē)</note>, memory, mention
<margin>to keep a memory of these things <note>original: τῇ τούτων μνήμῃ ποιεῖσθαι</note> 2 Pet. 1</margin>

¶ **To remember**, <note>original: Μνημονεύω (mnēmoneuō)</note>, to recall, to keep in mind, or to make mention of
Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves? Matt. 16
And do you not remember? Mark 8
Remember the word that I said to you. John 15
When the hour comes, you may remember them, that I told you. John 16
She no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy. John 16 <note>original citing "Ioan. 17" but this is John 16:21</note>
Only that we should remember the poor. Gal. 2
Therefore remember that you, once Gentiles in the flesh... Eph. 2
Remember my chains. Col. 4
Remembering without ceasing your work of faith. 1 Thess. 1
For you remember, brothers, our labor. 1 Thess. 2
Do you not remember that when I was still with you, I told you these things? 2 Thess. 2
Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead. 2 Tim. 2
By faith, Joseph, when he was dying, made mention of the departure of the sons of Israel. Heb. 11
And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from which they came out, they might have had opportunity to return. Heb. 11
Remember those who lead you. Heb. 13
For God has remembered her iniquities. Rev. 18

¶ **Memorial**, <note>original: Μνημόσυνον (mnēmosynon)</note>, a memorial, a pledge of remembrance
What this woman has done will also be told as a memorial to her. Mark 14
Your alms have ascended as a memorial. Acts 10

¶ **To be betrothed**, <note>original: Μνηστεύομαι (mnēsteuomai)</note>, to be promised, specifically to a groom
For when his mother Mary was betrothed... Matt. 1
To a virgin betrothed to a man... Luke 1
With Mary, his betrothed wife... Luke 2

-> M O <-

¶ **Having a speech impediment**, <note>original: Μογιλάλος (mogilalos)</note>, stammering, hindered in tongue
And they brought to him a deaf man who had an impediment in his speech. Mark 7

¶ **A bushel**, <note>original: Μόδιος (modios)</note>, a dry measure <note>The Roman "modius" was a grain measure of about 9 liters.</note>
Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel. Matt. 5
Is a lamp brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? Mark 4
Nor under a bushel. Luke 11

¶ **Adulteress**, <note>original: Μοιχαλίς (moichalis)</note>, an adulterous woman
An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign. Matt. 12
In this adulterous generation. Mark 8

<column-break/>

While her husband lives, she [is called] an adulteress... <note>original: Rom. 7:3</note>
Adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? <note>original: James 4:4</note>
Having eyes full of adultery... <note>original: 2 Pet. 2:14</note>

¶ **To commit adultery**, <note>original: Μοιχάομαι (moichaomai)</note>, to commit adultery [passive/middle form]
Causes her to commit adultery.
And marries another, commits adultery.
And is married to another, commits adultery.

¶ **Adultery**, <note>original: Μοιχεία (moicheia)</note>
Murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts. Mark 7
A woman caught in adultery. John 8
Which are adultery, fornication, etc. <note>original: Gal. 5:19</note>

¶ **To commit adultery**, <note>original: Μοιχεύω (moicheuō)</note>, to violate a marriage, to commit adultery [active form]
You have heard it was said to the ancients, "You shall not commit adultery."
Where you shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery.
You know the commandments, "Do not commit adultery."
And marrying another, he commits adultery.
Do not commit adultery.
You who say one should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery?
Either you commit adultery, or you steal.
For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder."
Those who commit adultery with her.

¶ **To be caught in adultery**, <note>original: Μοιχεύομαι (moicheuomai)</note>, passive form
This woman was caught in the very act of adultery.

¶ **Adulterer**, <note>original: Μοιχός (moichos)</note>
Extortioners, unjust, adulterers.
Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers. 1 Cor. 6
For fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
Adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God?

¶ **Scarcely**, <note>original: Μόλις (molis)</note>, hardly, with difficulty
For scarcely for a righteous man will one die.
If the righteous man is scarcely saved...

¶ **Moloch**, <note>original: Μολόχ</note>, the name of an idol
You took up the tabernacle of Moloch. Acts 7

¶ **To defile**, <note>original: Μολύνω (molynō)</note>, to stain or contaminate
Who have not defiled their garments.
Their conscience, being weak, is defiled. 1 Cor. 8
Those who were not defiled with women.

¶ **To be defiled**, <note>original: Μολύνομαι (molynomai)</note>, passive
Let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit. <note>original: 2 Cor. 7:1</note>

¶ **Defilement**, <note>original: Μολυσμός (molysmos)</note>, a stain or contamination

¶ **Complaint**, <note>original: Μομφή (momphē)</note>, a grievance, a rebuke
If anyone has a complaint against another.

¶ **Abode**, <note>original: Μονή (monē)</note>, a dwelling place, a mansion
In my Father's house are many mansions. John 14

<meta>This page continues the Greek concordance of the New Testament under the letter Nu (Ν). It begins by concluding the entries for "to conquer" and then proceeds through words related to victory, personal names like Nicodemus, and terms for washing, understanding, and the law.</meta>

¶ **Boldness**, *audacity* <note>original: "παρρησία" (parrhēsia); Latin: "audacia"</note>
*In this terminology we have also followed the translation of Erasmus.* <note>Desiderius Erasmus was a famous 16th-century scholar whose Latin translation of the New Testament updated the traditional Vulgate.</note>
In whom we have **boldness**. Ephesians 3

¶ **Boldness**, *confidence or trust* <note>original: "παρρησία" (parrhēsia); Latin: "fiducia"</note>
I have great **boldness** toward you. 2 Corinthians 7
Grant to your servants [to speak] with **boldness**. Acts 4
With all **boldness** without hindrance. Acts 28
Wherefore, having great **boldness** in Christ. Philemon
If we hold fast the **boldness** and the boasting of hope firm until the end. Hebrews 3
Let us come therefore with **boldness**. Hebrews 4
Do not cast away your **boldness**. Hebrews 10
Abide in him, so that when he is manifested, we may have **boldness**. 1 John 2
We have **boldness** toward God. 1 John 3

¶ **Boldness**, *freedom of speech* <note>original: "παῤῥησία" (parrhēsia); Latin: "libertas loquendi". This term originally referred to a citizen's right to speak their mind freely in a Greek assembly, but in the New Testament, it signifies a believer's confidence before God.</note>

<summary>This page provides a concordance of the Greek verb "poieō" (to do/make), categorizing its various biblical uses from "creating the world" to "making a profit" or "appointing disciples." --- Page 1298 ---
<meta>This page continues the Greek-Latin concordance for the New Testament, specifically focusing on the various idiomatic uses of the verb poieō (to do or to make). It organizes these uses alphabetically by the noun that follows the verb (e.g., to do "good," to do "truth," to do "sin").</meta>

-># OF THE NEW TESTAMENT<-
->1<-

¶ **To bear fruit** or **to make a branch** <note>original: ποιέω καρπὸς, κλάδος</note>: look in its own place below.

¶ It seemed good to us to observe the verb **to do** <note>original: ποιέω (poieō)</note> according to the various modes of speaking that occur everywhere in the Holy Scriptures, so that all things are not confused indiscriminately.

¶ **To do good** <note>original: ποιέω ἀγαθὰ (poieō agatha), Latin: bona facere</note>
“What good thing shall I do, so that I may have eternal life?” Matthew 19.
“Those who have done good things shall come out to the resurrection of life.” John 5.
“Do what is good, and you will have praise.” Romans 13.
“Knowing that whatever good thing each one does...” Ephesians 6.
“And let him do good.” 1 Peter 3.

¶ **To do the truth** <note>original: ποιέω ἀλήθειαν (poieō alētheian), Latin: facio ueritatem</note>
“But he who does the truth comes to the light.” John 3.
“We lie and do not practice [do] the truth.” 1 John 1.

¶ **To commit sin** <note>original: ποιέω ἁμαρτίαν (poieō hamartian), Latin: facio peccatum</note>
“For everyone who commits sin...” John 8.
“Every sin that a man does is outside the body.” 1 Corinthians 6.
“For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us.” 2 Corinthians 5.
“Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself?” 2 Corinthians 11.
“And if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.” James 5.
“Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness.” 1 John 3.

¶ **To do lawlessness** <note>original: ποιέω ἀνομίαν (poieō anomian), Latin: facio iniquitatem</note>
“And those who do lawlessness.” Matthew 13.

¶ **To do what is pleasing** <note>original: ποιέω ἀρεστὰ (poieō aresta), Latin: facio placita</note>
“For I always do the things that are pleasing to Him.” John 8.
“Doing in you what is well-pleasing in His sight.” Hebrews 13.
“And we do the things that are pleasing in His sight.” 1 John 3.

¶ **To make a beginning** <note>original: ποιέω ἀρχὴν (poieō archēn), Latin: facere initium</note>
“Jesus did this beginning of signs.” John 2.

¶ **To make a wedding feast** <note>original: ποιέω γάμους (poieō gamous), Latin: facio nuptias</note>
“Who made a wedding feast for his son.” Matthew 22.

¶ **To make a supper** or **banquet** <note>original: ποιέω δεῖπνον (poieō deipnon), Latin: facio cœnam, conuiuium</note>
“So they made a supper for Him there.” John 12.

¶ **To practice righteousness** <note>original: ποιέω δικαιοσύνην (poieō dikaiosynēn), Latin: exerceo iuſtitiam</note>
“That everyone who practices righteousness is born of Him.” 1 John 2.
“He who practices righteousness is righteous.” 1 John 3.

¶ **To make a reception** or **feast** <note>original: ποιέω δοχὴν (poieō dochēn), Latin: conuiuium facio</note>
“Levi made a great feast for Him.” Luke 5.

¶ **To perform miracles** or **mighty works** <note>original: ποιέω δυνάμεις (poieō dynameis), Latin: edo uirtutes</note>
“And He could do no mighty work there.” Mark 6.
“Did we not do many mighty works [in your name]?” Matthew 7.
“And in your name we performed many miracles.” Matthew 7.

<column-break/>

“And He did not perform many miracles there because of their unbelief.” <note>Matthew 13</note>
“For no one can perform these signs that you do.” <note>John 3</note>

¶ **To make peace** <note>original: ποιέω εἰρήνην (poieō eirēnēn), Latin: facio pacem</note>
Making peace and reconciling <unclear>enemies</unclear>. <note>interpretive gloss</note>
“Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.” <note>James 3</note>

¶ **To make a way out** <note>original: ποιέω ἔκβασιν (poieō ekbasin), Latin: facio exitum</note>
“But with the temptation He will also make a way of escape.” <note>1 Corinthians 10</note>

¶ **To do alms** <note>meaning: an act of kindness or a work of mercy; original: ποιέω ἐλεημοσύνην, Latin: benignitas, ſeu opus miſericordiæ facio</note>
“Whenever, therefore, you do alms...” <note>Matthew 6</note>

¶ **To show mercy** <note>original: ποιέω ἔλεος (poieō eleos), Latin: facio miſericordiam</note>
“For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy.” <note>James 2</note>

¶ **To do the desires** <note>meaning: to lust, that is, to follow or indulge an affection or nature; original: Επιθυμίας ποιέω, Latin: concupiſcere, id eſt, ſequi: indulgere affectui, ſiue genio</note>
“You want to do the desires of your father.” John <note>John 8</note>

¶ **To do a work** <note>original: ποιέω ἔργον (poieō ergon), Latin: facio opus</note>
“My food is to do the will of Him who sent me.” <note>John 4</note>
“So that your disciples may see the works you do.” <note>John 7</note>
“I did one work, and you all marvel.” John <note>John 7</note>

# -> NEW TESTAMENT <-

<margin>Matthew 28</margin> teaching them to **observe** <note>original: τηρεῖν (tērein) — to keep, guard, or observe</note> all that I commanded you.

<margin>Mark 7</margin> so that you might **keep** your tradition.

### ¶ Who and what? (Interrogative)
<note>original: Τίς καὶ τί (Tis kai ti). The Greek word for "who" or "what" when asking a question (Latin: "quis, quae, quid"). Note the accent mark on the 'i'.</note>

<note>original: Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί (Ti emoi kai soi). A common idiom in the New Testament roughly meaning "What does this have to do with me?" or "What is our common ground?" (Latin: "quid nostri").</note>

...through dishonor, etc.
<margin>2 Thessalonians 3</margin>
...that we received bread for free from anyone.

# CONCORDANCE

## C H A

¶ **Character** or **Exact Representation**, <note>original: "Χαρακτὴρ" (Charaktēr); Latin: "expressa imago" (an expressed image)</note>

¶ **To give freely**, **to forgive**, **to bestow**, **to give for free**, **to confer grace**, **to provide a benefit** <note>original: "Χαρίζομαι" (Charizomai); Latin: "dono, condono, largior, gratis do, gratiam confero, beneficium præsto"</note>
he **forgave** them both | Luke 7
to many who were blind he **gave** sight. Ibidem <note>Latin: "ibidem" (in the same place/book)</note>
so that a man who was a murderer was **granted** to you. Acts 3
it is not the Roman custom to **give over** any man to destruction | Acts 25
and behold, God has **granted** you all those who sail with you | Acts 27
how shall he not with him also **freely give** us all things? | Romans 8
that we might know the things **freely given** to us by God | 1 Corinthians 2
so that you ought rather to **forgive** the son <note>The translator likely meant "the brother/individual" mentioned in the context of 2 Cor 2:7.</note> | 2 Corinthians 2
And to whom you **forgive** anything, I do also | 2 Corinthians 2

¶ **Grace**. <note>original: "Χάρις" (Charis); Latin: "gratia"</note> This word has a very broad meaning, and it is not easy for everyone to notice everywhere whether "effect is put for cause" <note>The author uses the technical term "metonymy" to describe when a word for a result (a gift) is used to mean the source (God's favor).</note>, or vice versa, the "cause" (that is, favor) is put for the "effect." And certainly there is no effect unless a cause has preceded it. We separate these meanings more for simplicity than out of superstition, so that we will not start a quarrel with anyone who sees it differently.
